issues.title: Port fleet-send.sh to a loom-daemon subcommand (epic #7810)
issues.body:
## What

Port `defaults/scripts/fleet-send.sh` (the lifecycle-role safehouse posting helper, issue #4199) from bash+python to a native `loom-daemon fleet-send` subcommand, per epic #7810's script-port pattern. The script stays at its invocation-contract path as a thin stub.

## Why now

`#8237` settled fleet-send.sh as "deliberately kept shell," but the operator has directed the port: the Matrix/safehouse client code should live in Rust, not shell. This deliberately overrides that settled declaration and re-categorizes the entry (`settled` → `contract`) in the same change.

## How (the contract that must survive)

- **Hard degradation, verbatim**: absent env, no daemon, absent socket, invalid arg, connect/hello/send failure ⇒ **exit 0 SILENTLY** (no stdout, no stderr). The role's work is never blocked by the room.
- Wire protocol unchanged and now **canonical**: the subcommand reuses `safehouse::build_send_request` / `normalize_to` instead of the bash copy of the protocol (the script's doc comment already called safehouse.rs "the reference implementation" — this makes that true).
- `test-fleet-send.sh`'s assertions survive unchanged except two that pinned python's `json.dumps` byte layout (`"to": "*"` / `"op": "send"` greps); they become serialization-agnostic while asserting the same semantics.
- The stub resolves the implementation via `loom_resolve_self_daemon_bin` (the checkout build in this repo; the installed daemon in consumer repos) and must NOT go through `lib/script-helper.sh`'s loud missing-daemon path — silence IS the contract here.
- Declaration: `# requires-daemon: fleet-send optional` (an old daemon degrades to the same silent no-op it already had).
- CI: the suite moves from `shell-suite-tests` (no toolchain) to the Native Port Suites job, matching every other port in this epic; `ci-wired.txt` / `ci-excluded.txt` updated accordingly.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-fleet-send.sh` passes against the stub + built daemon (all five degradation/wire cases)
- [ ] `check-shell-allowlist.sh`, `check-daemon-subcommand-versions.sh`, `check-file-size-budget.sh`, `check-ci-suite-manifest.sh` all green
- [ ] Shell net-negative for the epic (shell-budget moves)

Part of epic #7810.

issues.title: Install-time session-mode flag: empty terminals + loom.sh start refusal
issues.body:
## Problem

Split out of #8846's "Optionally" section — a genuinely separate, larger
feature from that issue's required ask (which is just extending the
managed-CLAUDE.md-block pointer text).

In a repo run in session mode (roles invoked by an attended operator, no
daemon or interval terminals), there is currently no install-time way to
declare that intent. A repo that must never run unattended agents has no
config knob to enforce it — someone has to remember not to start the daemon,
and the stock `.loom/config.json` still ships whatever `terminals` array the
install template provides.

## Request

An install-time flag or config key (e.g. `mode: session`) that:

- writes `"terminals": []` in `.loom/config.json`,
- ensures the tmux agent-pool start path refuses to start.

**Not included here** (moved to #8862, which already covers it more broadly
than a session-mode-only fix would): stripping the stock issue templates'
external Discussions contact link. #8862 argues that problem affects every
install, not just session-mode ones, so it shouldn't be gated behind this
flag.

## Context

Verified against `origin/main` (2026-09-25, `git fetch origin main`):

- No existing "session mode" / "session-only" concept exists anywhere in
  `loom-daemon/src` or `install.sh` today (`git grep -n 'session mode\|session-mode\|attended operator'` — no hits beyond unrelated tmux-session terminology).
- `.loom/config.json`'s `terminals` array is read by `loom-daemon` at daemon
  start (see `loom-daemon/src/worktree_root.rs`, `role_validation.rs`,
  `runtime_admission.rs` test fixtures using `{"terminals": []}` as the
  degenerate case) — an empty array is already a supported, meaningful state.

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-25, verified against `origin/main`** (`grep -n "No Loom config
  with a non-empty" defaults/scripts/cli/loom-start.sh`): the "make the
  start path refuse to start" half of the original ask **already works
  today** for the tmux agent pool. `loom.sh` → `.loom/scripts/start-daemon.sh`
  → `.loom/bin/loom start` → `loom-start.sh`'s `check_config()`
  (`defaults/scripts/cli/loom-start.sh:193-218`) already hard-fails with
  `"Error: No Loom config with a non-empty \`terminals\` array found in any
  tier."` when `.loom/config.json` carries `"terminals": []`. This is
  covered by an existing regression test
  (`defaults/scripts/tests/test-config-tiers-cli-migration.sh:141-153`).
  **So there is no new refusal guard to write** — the remaining work is
  entirely on the *install-time* side: adding a `mode: session` flag/key that
  (a) makes a fresh install choose `terminals: []` instead of the default
  4-terminal array, and (b) makes that choice **persist across
  `loom update`/resync** (per `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh` and
  `install-metadata.json`, written at `scripts/install-loom.sh:1871-1879`) so
  a later reinstall doesn't silently restore the default terminals.
- **2026-09-25, scope gap identified**: an empty `terminals` array only
  disables the **tmux agent pool** (`loom.sh`/`loom-start.sh`). It does
  **not** disable the separate Rust `loom-daemon`'s autonomous role runner /
  work finder (`autonomous.roleRunner.enabled`, `autonomous.workFinder.enabled`
  in `.loom/config.json` — a distinct MCP-driven tier, started via
  `.loom/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-start.sh`, see `.loom/CLAUDE.md` §"Daemon
  Mode"). If "session mode" is meant to guarantee *no* unattended agents at
  all — which the Problem statement above implies ("must never run
  unattended agents") — the AC below needs to also force those two
  `autonomous.*` flags off, not just the `terminals` array. Flagged as an
  open design question rather than resolved here, since it changes the
  acceptance criteria's scope.

## Design questions to resolve during implementation

- Where does the `mode: session` key live — a new top-level `.loom/config.json`
  field, or an install-time-only flag that never gets written to config? Given
  the persistence requirement above (surviving `loom update`/resync), the key
  almost certainly needs to live in `.loom/config.json` (or `install-metadata.json`)
  so a later resync can read it back rather than re-deriving install-time intent.
- Does `mode: session` also need to force `autonomous.roleRunner.enabled` and
  `autonomous.workFinder.enabled` to `false` (see the scope-gap correction
  above), or is disabling the tmux pool considered sufficient for this issue
  and the daemon-tier guarantee is a separate follow-up?
- Should `--merge`/`--status`/`--stop` still work in session mode? (`--status`/
  `--stop` are read-only/idempotent against a pool that `check_config()`
  already refuses to *start* in this state, so they likely need no change.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `install.sh` (or the Rust installer path in `loom-daemon/src/init/`)
      accepts a `mode: session` install-time flag/config key
- [ ] With that flag, a fresh install writes `"terminals": []` into
      `.loom/config.json`
- [ ] The written `mode: session` marker (wherever it lands) survives
      `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh` / `loom update` — a later resync
      must not silently restore the default 4-terminal array
- [ ] Resolve the scope question above: either force `autonomous.roleRunner.enabled`/
      `autonomous.workFinder.enabled` to `false` too, or explicitly scope this
      issue to "tmux pool only" and note the daemon-tier gap in the docs
- [ ] Existing (non-session-mode) installs are unaffected — the guard is
      opt-in via the new key, never inferred from an empty `terminals` array
      alone (an empty array is already meaningful for other reasons, e.g. an
      operator manually driving session tools with no configured terminals)
- [ ] No new "refuse to start" guard needed for the tmux pool —
      `loom-start.sh`'s existing `check_config()` already covers it (see
      Verified corrections above); do not duplicate that logic

## Affected Files

- `install.sh` — new install-time flag parsing (mirroring how `--quick`/`--full`
  are already parsed)
- `scripts/install-loom.sh` — forward the flag into `INIT_FLAGS` (today only
  supports `--force`, see `install-loom.sh:1417-1421`) and persist the mode
  into `install-metadata.json`
- `loom-daemon/src/main.rs` (`Commands::Init`, around line 68) — new clap
  field for the mode flag; no such flag exists today
- `loom-daemon/src/init/scaffolding.rs` — write `terminals: []` instead of
  copying `defaults/config.json`'s 4-terminal array verbatim when the mode is set
- `defaults/scripts/resync-installed.sh` — read the persisted mode and skip
  restoring the default terminals array on resync
- `defaults/docs/` — document the new mode, its effect, and the tmux-pool vs.
  daemon-tier scope distinction from the Verified corrections above

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: install with the session-mode flag produces
      `"terminals": []` in the written `.loom/config.json`
- [ ] Automated tests: a resync/reinstall after a session-mode install does
      not restore the default terminals array
- [ ] Manual verification: a normal (non-session-mode) install is unaffected
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm `loom-start.sh`'s existing `check_config()`
      refusal still fires post-change (regression, not new behavior)

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: this is config-schema-plus-persistence work
with a clear, testable pass/fail — a mistake would surface immediately in the
new test coverage this issue's own AC requires, not silently pass review. The
one judgment call (the autonomous-role-runner scope question above) is
resolvable by a Builder reading the Design questions section, not something
requiring architecture-level review.

## Dependencies

None — self-contained.

## Related

Split out of #8846 (that issue's required scope — extending the managed
CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md pointer text — is unaffected by this split and proceeds
independently). See #8862 for the issue-template Discussions-link problem
this issue deliberately does not duplicate.

issues.title: ETA phase 6: eta.snapshot ingest record + loom-ui display (retire dashboard-side estimates)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Phase 6 of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Plan: Curator comment https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5867874254, operator decisions https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5869738711. **Depends on #9289 Phase 1** (core, heuristic registry, explanation schema, journal); do not start before it merges.

### Scope (operator decision 7)
- Loom side: a new host-scoped `eta.snapshot` record through the existing `/ingest` path every 5 min, with a slim current-estimate list per issue: `repo, issue, pr, kind, p25/p50/p75, heuristic, estimate_id, as_of, stage, no_estimate_reason`. It is **not** folded into `queue.snapshot`, since land estimates cover building/review items too.
- loom-ui side (2AMLogic/loom-ui#257/#263): FleetState DO key `eta:<hostId>` (newest per host, like `queue.snapshot`) and a display of ranges. The full explanation is fetched **on demand** from SigNoz by `estimate_id` ('why this ETA?'), and the accuracy panel queries `eta.outcome` in SigNoz. Nothing large in D1.
- Retire loom-ui's interim estimates (#250/#261/#274 area) once this ships.

---

## Consolidated from

### #9330: ETA phase 7: docs + eta-queries.sql + CI artifact test

> Phase 7 of #9289 (ETA as a Loom primitive). Plan: Curator comment https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5867874254, operator decisions https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/issues/9289#issuecomment-5869738711. **Depends on #9289 Phase 1** (core, heuristic registry, explanation schema, journal); do not start before it merges.
>
> ### Scope
> - `defaults/docs/eta.md`: the model, the explanation schema, the versioning rules, how to add v2 and compare it (backtest, then shadow).
> - `eta-queries.sql`: MAE/coverage/bias, pinball per heuristic/kind/repo/horizon, feature ranking over explanation `features` (`JSONExtractKeysAndValues` + `rankCorr`), abandonment rate.
> - A CI test that the queries parse against the schema fixtures.

Consolidated 2026-09-30 per the 2026-09-30 backlog-rightsizing pass (#9664, "Flagged: #9330 (ETA phase 7) recommended for fold into #9329 at build time"): both are the two remaining phases of epic #9289, the docs/CI-test work is small and directly describes the snapshot work this issue already delivers, and combining avoids a second full Curator→Builder→Judge cycle for ~5 points of closely related follow-on work. Consolidation gate checked 2026-09-30: #9330 carried only `loom:triage`/`points:5` (no disqualifying label), no sub-issue parent, and `loom-daemon forge check-open-pr 9330` returned exit 1 (no open PR).

---

## Curator Enhancement — 2026-09-30

Premise gate: exit 0 (`out-of-scope` — no trigger phrase, proceeds normally). Verified against `origin/main` @ `828910895` region (fetched 2026-09-30).

### Dependency status: fully clear

All five prerequisite phases are merged as of today:

| Phase | Issue | Closed via PR | Merged at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (core) | #9289 | #9355 | 2026-09-28T15:36Z |
| 2 (backfill/backtest) | #9325 | #9578 | 2026-09-30T01:54Z |
| 3 (`start-v1`) | #9326 | #9701 | 2026-09-30T14:38Z |
| 4 (CLI) | #9327 | #9721 | 2026-09-30T16:20Z |
| 5 (shadow/promotion) | #9328 | #9749 | 2026-09-30T17:52Z |

This issue (Phase 6) was body-blocked ("Depends on #9289 Phase 1... do not start before it merges") — that dependency, and every later one, is now satisfied. No `loom:blocked` is warranted.

### Verified current state of the `eta` module (origin/main, 2026-09-30)

- `loom-daemon/src/eta/` already has `mod.rs, backtest.rs, config.rs, emit.rs, explanation.rs, grid.rs, heuristics/{finish_v1,land_v1,land_v2,start_v1}.rs, history.rs, journal.rs, labels.rs, score.rs, shadow.rs, simulate.rs, tracker.rs, tracker_ready.rs` plus fixtures and a `tests/` dir — Phases 1–5 are fully built.
- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/kinds.rs` defines `EtaEstimate = "eta.estimate"` and `EtaOutcome = "eta.outcome"`, both `otlp: Logs, native: false` — **OTLP/SigNoz-only today**. There is **no `EtaSnapshot`/`eta.snapshot` kind yet** — this issue's core deliverable is genuinely unbuilt.
- The direct template to copy is `loom-daemon/src/observability/queue_snapshot.rs` + `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs` (the `queue.snapshot` kind: `gate: 11, otlp: NotExported, native: true`), which already implements the exact shape operator decision 7 asks for: a host-scoped record, sent only to the native (non-OTLP) exporter queue, emitted from the collector's snapshot cadence, "newest per host" semantics via `FleetState` DO key `queue:<hostId>` on the loom-ui side.
- `defaults/docs/eta.md` (329 lines) and `defaults/observability/signoz/eta-queries.sql` (157 lines) **already exist and are substantially complete** — Phases 1–5 built them incrementally. `eta.md` explicitly says, in its own intro: "Later phases: shadow mode and promotion (#9328), the loom-ui snapshot (#9329) and fuller docs (#9330)" — i.e. the docs already name both halves of this consolidated issue as the remaining gaps.
- **No CI artifact test exists yet** for `eta-queries.sql` (`loom-daemon/tests/` has no `eta_*_artifacts.rs`; the precedent is `loom-daemon/tests/pr_latency_artifacts.rs`, which ties `pr-latency`'s doc/query files to schema fixtures the same way #9330's AC asks for here) — this half of the consolidated scope is also genuinely unbuilt.
- 2AMLogic/loom-ui#257/#263 could not be verified from this environment (`gh issue view --repo 2AMLogic/loom-ui` fails to resolve the repository from here) — treat the loom-ui-side display work as **unverified cross-repo scope**, not confirmed ready or blocked.

### Related open work (duplicate/related-work check, #4162)

- **#9330** — absorbed via the consolidation above (same issue, not a separate disposition).
- **#9420** ("[eta] condition role-attempt dwell distributions on work actually done") — disregarded. It's a heuristic-quality fix inside the estimation model itself (conditioning dwell distributions on completed work), unrelated to this issue's ingest/display/docs scope.
- **#9664** (backlog-rightsizing report) — absorbed: this curation implements its specific recommendation to fold #9330 into #9329.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Loom-daemon side (this repo — the Builder-owned portion):**
- [ ] A new `EtaSnapshot = "eta.snapshot"` kind is added to `telemetry/kinds.rs` (`gate: NEW_KIND_SCHEMA_VERSION` per the append-marker convention, `otlp: NotExported, native: true` — mirroring `QueueSnapshot`'s row, not `EtaEstimate`'s).
- [ ] `telemetry/eta_snapshot.rs` (or a section of `telemetry/kinds/eta.rs`) defines `EtaSnapshotRecord` and a row type carrying exactly the operator-specified fields: `repo, issue, pr, kind, p25, p50, p75, heuristic, estimate_id, as_of, stage, no_estimate_reason`.
- [ ] `observability/eta_snapshot.rs` (new, mirroring `observability/queue_snapshot.rs`) reads the ETA tracker's current per-issue estimates (not a new tick loop — reuse whatever `tracker.rs`/`tracker_ready.rs` already holds in memory), maps workspace → `owner/repo` via the collector's existing slug cache, and offers `EtaSnapshot` envelopes to the **native-only** exporter queue on the collector's existing snapshot cadence (same cadence `queue_snapshot::record` uses), emitting only when the tracker's estimate set has changed since the last emission (mirrors `queue_snapshot`'s "only when the work finder has ticked" rule, applied to ETA).
- [ ] `observability/collector.rs` gains one call to the new `record(...)` (alongside the existing `queue_snapshot::record` call), and `observability/mod.rs` wires it identically to how `queue_snapshot` is wired — no new tick loop, no daemon-wide behavior change when `autonomous.eta.enabled = false`.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` documents the new kind (fields, absent-vs-zero contract) at its append point, matching the style of the `QueueSnapshot`/`EtaEstimate` entries already there.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/eta.md` is updated to state the `eta.snapshot` kind now exists (currently it only forward-references "the loom-ui snapshot (#9329)" as future work) and to drop/update the now-stale "later phases" framing for #9329/#9330 once both ship.
- [ ] A CI artifact test (new `loom-daemon/tests/eta_artifacts.rs`, mirroring `loom-daemon/tests/pr_latency_artifacts.rs`) parses `defaults/observability/signoz/eta-queries.sql`'s Q1–Q3 against the existing schema fixtures (`eta/fixtures/explanation-golden.json` and friends) and fails if the doc/query pair drifts from the live telemetry schema.
- [ ] `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh` and `scripts/check-shell-allowlist.sh` exit 0; no frozen file grows past its ratchet.

**Cross-repo (loom-ui side — file as a follow-up issue in 2AMLogic/loom-ui if that repo is reachable from the Builder's environment; do not block this issue's PR on landing it there):**
- [ ] loom-ui's Worker accepts `eta.snapshot` envelopes through the existing `/ingest` path and stores them newest-per-host under `eta:<hostId>` in the `FleetState` Durable Object (mirroring `queue:<hostId>`).
- [ ] A dashboard surface displays the per-issue ETA ranges from that snapshot, with an on-demand "why this ETA?" fetch of the full explanation from SigNoz by `estimate_id`, and an accuracy panel querying `eta.outcome` in SigNoz.
- [ ] loom-ui's interim/dashboard-side estimates (the #250/#261/#274 area, per the original body) are retired once the above ships.

### Affected Files (loom-daemon / this repo)

- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/kinds.rs` — add the `EtaSnapshot` kind row (append point already marked `// APPEND NEW KINDS ABOVE THIS LINE`).
- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/eta_snapshot.rs` (new) or `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/kinds/eta.rs` (edit) — `EtaSnapshotRecord` + row type.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/eta_snapshot.rs` (new) — collector-cadence emission, native-queue-only, mirroring `observability/queue_snapshot.rs`.
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs` (edit, one call site, alongside the existing `queue_snapshot::record` call).
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/mod.rs` (edit, wiring only).
- `loom-daemon/tests/eta_artifacts.rs` (new) — CI artifact test tying `eta.md`/`eta-queries.sql` to the schema fixtures.
- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (edit — new kind's field reference).
- `defaults/docs/eta.md` (edit — reflect the now-shipped snapshot kind; tidy the "later phases" forward references to #9329/#9330 once both land).
- `defaults/observability/signoz/eta-queries.sql` — verify still current against the CI artifact test added above; extend only if the test surfaces a real gap.
- No new `.sh` (shell-language policy); no `VERSION` edit.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a `telemetry::kind_registry` test covering the new kind's fixture/merge coverage (mirroring the existing `EtaEstimate`/`EtaOutcome` registration tests); a unit test for `observability::eta_snapshot::record` asserting native-only queue offering (no OTLP offering) using the existing `ops::capture`-style envelope capture already used by `queue_snapshot_tests.rs`; the new `loom-daemon/tests/eta_artifacts.rs`.
- [ ] Manual verification: enable `autonomous.eta.enabled = true` on one workspace with a native HTTPS exporter configured, confirm an `eta.snapshot` envelope reaches the native queue (existing envelope-capture/log tooling), and — if the loom-ui-side work has landed — confirm it appears under `eta:<hostId>` in the FleetState DO.
- [ ] Edge cases: tracker has zero current estimates (no emission, not an empty/garbage row); a `no_estimate_reason` present issue is still included in the snapshot (absence of an estimate is itself informative, not dropped); daemon restart mid-cadence (no duplicate/stale snapshot row); `autonomous.eta.enabled = false` (no `eta.snapshot` kind emitted at all, existing `queue.snapshot` emission unaffected).

issues.title: [#9244 C] liveness contract (landing state, needs-operator escalation, watchdog, blocker inheritance) + loom-ui star intents
issues.body:
Parent: #9244 (split approved by the operator into three PRs: A, B, C). This is **C: liveness contract and loom-ui star intents (Rust)**. **Blocked on A** (needs A's label, `WorkItem`/`PriorityCandidate` fields, starred listing and `queue.snapshot` fields).

## Goal

A starred issue is always either being worked on or escalated to the operator with one concrete ask. There's no silent third state. Also, a star made in loom-ui is applied to GitHub by the daemon.

## Scope

### 1. Landing state (#9244 liveness item 1)
- For each starred issue, compute `curating | ready | building | in-review | changes-requested | mergeable | merging | blocked-by(<ref>) | needs-operator(<ask>) | no-capacity(<reason>)`, plus time-in-stage and next actor.
- Publish it on A's `queue.snapshot` rows (new optional fields, documented in `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`). Show it in `loom-daemon status` and `ready-queue` (`cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs`).

### 2. Immediate `needs-operator` escalation (item 2)
- Triggers (immediate, not timed): `loom:operator-only` / `loom:operator-decision` on the issue or its PR; a forge merge refusal (405 / ruleset / merge-method, the #9268 shape); an exhausted token pool on every host managing the repo; no host managing the repo; a merge-risk or critical-file hold.
- One concrete ask per (issue, ask), deduplicated across ticks and hosts (e.g. by a marker in a comment, or a stable key in a Safehouse message).
- Channels: the `health/operator_attention.rs` section (which must stay `Verdict::Green`, per its module doc) and Safehouse (`loom-daemon/src/safehouse.rs`). **`safehouse.rs` is frozen by the file-size ratchet (`scripts/file-size-baseline.txt`, 2443)**, so new code goes in a sibling module. loom-ui gets it via the landing state on `queue.snapshot`. Putting the item at the top of the pinned hold digest (#6877) is Champion-prompt work and belongs to **B**. The daemon has **no Matrix client** today. The #9244 text lists "the team Matrix room" as a channel; either route it through an existing Safehouse bridge or record it as a follow-up. Don't add a new Matrix integration silently.

### 3. Progress watchdog (item 3)
- A starred issue with no forward progress for 30 min (configurable under `autonomous.*`, env > config > default) is escalated with what Loom last saw. Forward progress means a label transition, a push to its PR, a checkpoint write, or a CI conclusion. Look at `sweep_registry/reaper/no_progress.rs` for reusable progress signals.

### 4. Blocker inheritance (item 4)
- The blocker of a starred issue inherits its queue position (key 1/2 in A's `candidate_cmp`) and its escalation, marked `inherited` in the snapshot/UI, and loses it when the blocker clears. Blocker sources: the issue named by `loom:blocked` or a `blocked-by` edge (`dep_classify` / `stale_blocked`), the incident issue named in a merge refusal, and the red-main-fix issue for the repo.

### 5. Applying stars from loom-ui
- **Ack field.** `IngestAck` (`loom-daemon/src/observability/exporter.rs:109`, today only `host_id`) gains `#[serde(default)] operator_priority_intents: Vec<Intent>`. The wire shape is what loom-ui actually shipped (see the loom-ui comment on #9244): `{id, repo, number, action: "star"|"unstar", label, requested_at, requested_by}`. **The actor field is `requested_by`, not `actor`** as in #9244's body. A missing field means an old backend, which must keep working. `[]` means a supporting backend with nothing to do.
- **Ack size bound.** `MAX_ACK_BODY_BYTES = 4096` (`exporter.rs:~120`). A 50-intent ack (~250 bytes each) is about 12 KB and would be truncated, fail to parse, and drop both the intents **and** the #4830 host-id check. Raise the bound (e.g. 64 KiB) and add a test for a large ack.
- **Side channel.** `check_host_identity` (`exporter.rs:~202`) publishes to `HostIdStatus` (`observability/mod.rs:455`, global registration at :498-502). Add an analogous `Arc`-shared intent queue from the exporter back to the daemon main loop. Note `observability/mod.rs:~1018-1033`: some exporter paths deliberately get no `HostIdStatus`, so the new channel needs the same treatment.
- **Validate.** `label == "loom:operator-priority"` only; `repo` must be in this host's managed workspace registry; `requested_by` must be non-empty. Anything else is dropped and logged.
- **Apply** with the daemon's forge client: add or remove the label, then post one comment with `<!-- loom:operator-priority-intent=<id> requested_at=<ts> -->` "Starred for operator priority by <requested_by> via loom-ui". Check for an existing marker before posting, so a second pass or a second host posts no duplicate comment.
- **Starred-at.** The intent comment's `requested_at` takes precedence over A's `labeled`-event source for ordering (use the seam A leaves). Labels applied directly on GitHub keep A's timeline fallback.

### 6. Replay acceptance check
- A test fixture reproducing 2026-09-28: #8191 (approved PR #9276, merge refused by the #9268 method contradiction), #8256 (PR parked on `loom:operator-decision`), loom-ui#281 (label only, no workflow label, exhausted pool on the only managing host), and 2am #1180 / #1098 / #897 (`loom:operator-only`) and #869 (`loom:blocked`). Each, if starred, yields exactly one operator escalation within one tick, and #9268 inherits #8191's star.

## File-size ratchet
`work_finder.rs`, `work_finder/tests.rs`, `main.rs` and `safehouse.rs` are frozen (`scripts/file-size-baseline.txt`). Check `exporter.rs`, `observability/mod.rs` and `collector.rs` against the 1000-code-line threshold before adding code. New logic goes in sibling modules. **Never run cargo on the Mac.**

## Out of scope
- **A:** ordering, listings, overflow, red-main admission, base telemetry fields, the label definition.
- **B:** all role-prompt changes (including hold-digest ordering and Champion's retry-once rule), and the `loom:urgent` retirement.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Landing state is computed for every starred issue and published on `queue.snapshot`, `loom-daemon status` and `ready-queue`. The schema doc is updated.
- [ ] Tests drive a starred issue into each non-agent state (operator-decision, forge merge 405, all pools exhausted, unmanaged repo, merge-risk hold) and assert an **immediate** `needs-operator` escalation with a concrete ask, deduplicated across ticks and hosts.
- [ ] A starred issue with no progress for the watchdog window escalates. The window is configurable.
- [ ] A blocker of a starred issue inherits its position (marked inherited) and loses it when the blocker clears.
- [ ] `/ingest` ack intents are parsed, validated (label, managed repo, `requested_by`) and applied idempotently with one audit comment. Tests cover an old backend without the field, a repo this host doesn't manage (dropped), a duplicate intent (no second comment), unstar, and a 50-intent ack over the old 4096-byte bound.
- [ ] The replay check against 2026-09-28 passes.

issues.title: auto_update: bound the unsatisfiable-roll suppression with a cooldown retry, instead of waiting for a 900s-sampled in_flight == 0
issues.body:
## Context
<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

Follow-up from the Judge's non-blocking item 2 on #9004 (which closed #8998).

#9004 stops the 21-hour arm → refuse → retain → abandon → re-arm livelock by declaring a roll's wait condition **unsatisfiable** and suppressing further re-arms. The suppression is sticky and clears on exactly one event: an auto-update tick that *samples* `in_flight == 0`.

That clearing condition is materially harder to hit than it reads:

- It is **sampled**, not continuous — once every `autonomous.autoUpdate.intervalSecs` (default `900`, `DEFAULT_AUTO_UPDATE_INTERVAL_SECS`).
- It is sampled **with dispatch running**. The drain's own quiescence watch is continuous *and* runs with dispatch paused, so in-flight there can only fall. After abandonment dispatch resumes, and a cap-12 dispatcher refills the in-flight set as soon as the long sweep ends.

On a busy host, a 900s sample can therefore miss every lull, and the host stops auto-updating for an **unbounded** time with no time-based retry. #9004 is still a strict improvement (the counterfactual host never updated *and* also lost dispatch, and the reason is now named loudly), which is why this was not blocking — but "unbounded paused dispatch" was traded for "unbounded staleness", not for a bounded state.

## The distinction that matters

A cooldown that re-arms once every N hours is **bounded**. The livelock was **unbounded**. That is the property worth having.

## Proposed direction

Add a bounded retry to `RollStallTracker` (`loom-daemon/src/auto_update/roll_stall.rs`) so a standing declaration expires on time as well as on an idle observation:

1. A new knob (`autonomous.autoUpdate.rollStallCooldownSecs` / `LOOM_AUTO_UPDATE_ROLL_STALL_COOLDOWN_SECS`, `env > config > default`, zero/invalid dropped like every sibling) — a plausible default is several hours, long enough that one retry per long sweep is the worst case.
2. When the declaration has stood for that long, clear it and let the next tick arm a roll normally. If the host still cannot drain, the detector re-declares after `rollStallDeadlines` more deadlines, so the cost is one bounded paused-dispatch budget per cooldown period rather than a continuous one.
3. Keep the `in_flight == 0` clear as the fast path.
4. Decide whether the retry should also relax the sampling problem (e.g. remember whether in-flight was *ever* seen at zero between ticks) or whether the cooldown alone is enough — the cooldown is the simpler property to reason about and probably sufficient.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A standing unsatisfiability declaration clears after a bounded, configurable period even if `in_flight == 0` is never sampled.
- [ ] The knob follows `env > config > default` with zero/invalid dropped on both sides, like `rollStallDeadlines`.
- [ ] A host that still cannot drain re-declares rather than cycling — i.e. the retry is bounded *per cooldown*, not a return to the #8998 livelock. Pin this with a test that runs several cooldown periods and asserts the number of paused-dispatch budgets consumed.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` § "Scheduled drain-and-restart" replaces the current "no time-based retry … can stay un-updated indefinitely" caveat with the bounded behaviour.
- [ ] Unit-testable without a live daemon, clock-injected, in the existing `roll_stall.rs` style.

## Not in scope

#8998's directions 2 and 3 (age-excluding a long sweep from the drain condition; dropping the full-drain requirement for artifact rolls) — those are what would let a permanently-busy host actually roll, and each deserves its own design pass.

Refs: #9004, #8998, #6007, #8514

issues.title: ci-telemetry: poll several owners (orgs AND user accounts) so rjwalters/loom CI runs join story traces
issues.body:
## Problem

CI stitching into the D32 story trace (#9117) only happens for runs the CI poller sees. The poller captures a **single org**: `autonomous.ciTelemetry.org` (default `2amlogic`, `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_ORG`). It discovers repos with `GET /orgs/{org}/repos` (`ci_telemetry/poll.rs:~608`).

- **Loom's own CI is never captured.** `rjwalters/loom` is under a *user* account, so `/orgs/rjwalters/repos` does not apply. No story trace for a loom issue can contain a `loom.ci.run` span.
- **Measured 2026-09-27:** zero `loom.ci.run` spans in SigNoz in the last 3 days. The first derived story trace, `rjwalters/loom#9168` (trace `cf0ca10ca26dae948c2f6ac12ae45d19`, emitted by 2AMLogic/2am's storyline reconciler), has root, intake, queue_dwell, review_wait and merge spans, and no CI.

## Proposal

- Accept a list of **owners**. Add a new `autonomous.ciTelemetry.owners: ["2amlogic", "rjwalters"]`, and keep `org` as a deprecated single-owner alias. The env override `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_OWNERS` is comma-separated.
- For each owner, resolve whether it is an org or a user once, via `GET /users/{owner}` `type`, and cache the result. Discover repos with `/orgs/{o}/repos?type=all` or `/users/{o}/repos?type=owner` accordingly.
- Keep the existing per-repo ETag cache, backoff, `excludedRepos` / `logCaptureExcludedRepos` policy (entries become `owner/repo`, which they already are) and the single-captain gate.
- `ci-telemetry status` lists each owner with its kind and repo count.
- API budget: one extra `GET /users/{owner}` per owner per daemon lifetime, and one discovery walk per owner per cycle (ETag, so usually 304).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Config parsing: `owners` list, `org` alias, env override, precedence env > config > default, plus a test for each.
- [ ] Discovery: a user owner uses `/users/{u}/repos`, an org owner uses `/orgs/{o}/repos`. Both are covered by tests using the existing fake `GithubApi`.
- [ ] Existing `org`-only configs behave exactly as before (regression test).
- [ ] `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` documents `owners`.

Part of #9037. Enabling the poller on a host (captain + `enabled=true`) remains an operator step.

issues.title: [Epic #9429] story-points: points-landed-per-day throughput query and rollup
issues.body:
Parent epic: filed separately (Fibonacci story points — size-weighted throughput). Depends on: phase 3 (points on telemetry).

## Goal

The number this epic exists for: **story points landed per day**, queryable in SigNoz, retention-safe, defined once.

## Work

- [ ] Add a canonical question set under `defaults/observability/` (sibling to `cycle-time-questions.md`, same discipline: definitions fixed once, every question a committed SQL statement): points landed per day and per ISO-week (successful ships only — a failed sweep lands nothing, following the existing `ship` definition), trend over months, per-repo split
- [ ] Backend-neutral rollup + per-backend extraction, following the `loom_analytics.ship_cycle_time` pattern — raw log retention is ~7 days, so the trend question is unanswerable from raw logs; that is exactly why CT6 needed the rollup
- [ ] The join: `sweep.outcome` rows → `loom.story_points`; sweeps without points are reported as a data-gap count (CT7 discipline: missing is not zero)
- [ ] Contract tests mirroring `loom-daemon/tests/cycle_time_artifacts.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A committed query answers "points landed per day" for any window since the rollup's existence
- [ ] The answer separates successful landings from failed sweeps
- [ ] Re-running the rollup over an already-ingested window is idempotent, with a CT8-style reconciliation against raw records
- [ ] A short ops note says where to read the number for capacity tuning ("the pipeline lands N points/day — do we need another Judge?")

---

## Curator technical guidance (2026-09-29)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=3 -->

### Verified corrections

- **2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main`** (`git fetch origin --quiet`; every path below confirmed via `git ls-tree -r origin/main --name-only`): the epic's sibling phases (#9430 rubric, #9431 `points:*` labels, #9432 `loom.story_points` telemetry) all merged, and in the same window a related-but-distinct epic (**#9446/#9466, "sweep_facts"**) landed the retention-safe rollup infrastructure this issue's `## Work` section describes wanting to build from scratch. That infrastructure is **not** the `loom_analytics.ship_cycle_time` ClickHouse pattern this issue names — it's a newer, D1-based generalization of the same idea (`defaults/observability/sweep-facts/`), and it already answers a closely related question:
  - `sweep-facts-questions.md` SF2 — *"How much work lands per day?"* — is explicitly annotated `(#9466, consumed by #9433)`: the sweep-facts author already treated this issue as SF2's downstream consumer.
  - SF2 sums **LSI** (landed-size index: a continuous measurement derived from `hw_lines`/`hw_files`/tokens, see `landed-size.sql`), **not** the Curator-assigned `points:*` label. `sweep_facts` (the D1 table `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` creates) has **no `story_points` column today** — `grep -n story_points defaults/observability/sweep-facts/*.sql` returns no matches as of this commit.
  - `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`story_points` (~line 725) states outright: *"With it on the record, 'story points landed per day' (#9433) ... is a `GROUP BY` over this journal instead of a join against the forge."* — the schema doc already anticipated this issue would be built as a `sweep_facts` extension, not a parallel rollup.

**Recommendation — supersedes the literal `## Work` bullets above, which pre-date this infrastructure**: extend `sweep_facts` rather than building a second `loom_analytics`-style pipeline.

1. Add a `story_points INTEGER` column to `sweep_facts` (`sweep-facts-rollup.sql`'s `CREATE TABLE`), populated by `json_extract(r.payload, '$.story_points')` in the `INSERT OR REPLACE` — the same pattern every other optional numeric column there already follows (e.g. `doctor_cycles`, line ~150). The table's key/grain is unchanged, so idempotence (`INSERT OR REPLACE` on `(repo, issue, sweep_id)`) and SF7's existing reconciliation cover the new column with no extra work.
2. Mirror the column in both ClickHouse extraction views, reading the numeric OTLP attribute `loom.story_points` (name confirmed in `telemetry-schema.md`'s `story_points` section): `toInt64OrNull(LogAttributes['loom.story_points'])` in `sweep-facts-extract-clickstack.sql` (next to `tokens_in`, ~line 65), and the number-map-then-string-map fallback `sweep-facts-extract-signoz.sql`'s other numeric columns already use (mirror `doctor_cycles`'s handling there).
3. Add a new committed question (`SF8`) to `sweep-facts-queries.sql` / `sweep-facts-questions.md`: points landed per day and per ISO week, **landed sweeps only** (reuse `landed-size.sql`'s `landings` CTE predicate: `disposition = 'landed'`, or the documented pre-#9441 fallback). Per the operator's comment on this issue (2026-09-29, "turian"), report:
   - `landings` (issue count) — turian: "report issue count alongside," since count alone explains most of the daily variance (measured R² 0.83 by count, 0.94 with points, over a 34-day window).
   - a **data-gap count**: landed sweeps whose `story_points` is `NULL` — CT7/SF4 discipline, "missing is not zero." This is the literal `sweep.outcome → loom.story_points` join the original `## Work` bullet asks for.
   - **Do NOT `sum(story_points)` directly.** turian's comment (backed by the story-points experiment's measured data) states raw Fibonacci labels are ordinal, not a unit: the pre-registered ±30% additivity test failed on all three measured axes (tokens 1 : 1.3 : 2.2 : 3.4 : 5.1 : 8.2; lines 1 : 8.5 : 21 : 47 : 82 : 197). Report the **measured point value per bucket** instead, joining each landing's *assigned* `story_points` (cast to the `TEXT` size-class key) against `landed-size.sql`'s existing `measured_points(size_class, measured_point_tokens, measured_point_lines)` CTE — the same table SF2/`landed-size.sql` already use for the *actual* (LSI-derived) class, applied here to the *forecast* (Curator-assigned) class instead. If a raw label sum is reported at all, name it plainly as non-additive (e.g. `labels_summed_ordinal_do_not_use_as_size`), never as "points landed."
   - Cross-reference SF2's `lsi_landed` rather than recomputing LSI — SF8 adds the forecast/label side, SF2 already has the actual/measured side.
4. Extend `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs`: add `story_points` everywhere the test asserts column parity across `sweep_facts`'s `CREATE TABLE`, its `INSERT OR REPLACE` list, and both extraction views' output columns; add `"SF8"` to `QUESTION_IDS`. This is the "contract tests mirroring `cycle_time_artifacts.rs`" the original `## Work` asks for — it already exists as `sweep_facts_artifacts.rs` (same author, same shape); this issue extends it rather than writing a new one.
5. Short ops note: extend `sweep-facts-questions.md`'s existing prose/table (do not create a new file — ratchet discipline) with where to read the number for capacity tuning, e.g. beside SF2's row, since capacity tuning reads SF2 (data-driven headline) and SF8 (coverage / forecast-vs-actual) together.

### Dependency status (verified 2026-09-29 against `origin/main`)

All three sibling phases are closed and merged, no blocker remains: #9430 (rubric), #9431 (`points:*` labels — confirmed live: `gh label list --search "points:"` returns `points:1/2/3/5/8/13`), #9432 (`loom.story_points` on telemetry — confirmed: `loom-daemon/src/story_points.rs`, `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`story_points`).

### Operator context (not contested by this curation pass)

This issue carries `loom:building` from an operator-directed claim (see this issue's own 2026-09-29 comment, "Operator-directed build... Claiming #9433 as Builder"), and a fleet lease (`sweep-issue-9433-1790721183`) was active as of this curation pass. This curation is applied per explicit dispatch instructions and does not reclaim the Builder claim. **Because the finding above changes the intended implementation approach**, whoever is driving the active Builder sweep should read this section before finishing: following the literal original `## Work` bullets (a new `loom_analytics`-pattern ClickHouse pipeline) would duplicate infrastructure `sweep_facts` already provides and risks the ordinal-label-sum pitfall described above, which could pass tests/review while shipping a misleading "points landed" number.

### Acceptance criteria (refined, additive to the original)

- [ ] `sweep_facts.story_points` exists, sourced from `loom.story_points`, `NULL` when the sweep's issue carried no (or more than one, or an out-of-vocabulary) `points:*` label — never `0` (mirrors `telemetry-schema.md`'s own absent-vs-zero contract for this exact field).
- [ ] A committed query (`SF8` in `sweep-facts-queries.sql`) answers "points landed per day" and "per ISO week" for any window since `story_points` began being captured, using the bound `{since}`/`{until}` window pattern the other SF queries already use — no hand-edited date literal.
- [ ] The answer counts **landed** sweeps only (`disposition = 'landed'`, or the documented pre-#9441 fallback); a failed or non-landed sweep contributes to neither the points sum nor the landings count.
- [ ] Landed sweeps with no `story_points` are reported as an explicit data-gap count, separate from (never folded into) the points sum.
- [ ] "Points landed" is reported via the **measured point value per bucket**, not a raw sum of Fibonacci labels — see the "Do NOT `sum(story_points)` directly" guidance above and turian's comment on this issue for the measured non-additivity data this requirement is based on.
- [ ] Re-running `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` over an already-ingested window stays idempotent (structurally true via `INSERT OR REPLACE` on `(repo, issue, sweep_id)` — verify the new column doesn't change that); SF7's existing reconciliation query covers the new column with no separate CT8-style query needed, since SF7 already reconciles the whole `sweep_facts` row and this issue only adds a column to it.
- [ ] `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs` is extended to cover the new column and `SF8` the same way it covers SF1–SF7 today (static contract, no live backend required).
- [ ] A short ops note (extending `sweep-facts-questions.md`, not a new file) states where to read the number for capacity tuning.

### Affected files (verified present on `origin/main`, 2026-09-29)

- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-rollup.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-queries.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-questions.md`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-extract-clickstack.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/sweep-facts-extract-signoz.sql`
- `defaults/observability/sweep-facts/landed-size.sql` (read-only reference for the `measured_points` join — no change expected unless the join needs a new view)
- `loom-daemon/tests/sweep_facts_artifacts.rs`

### Test plan

- `cargo test -p loom-daemon --test sweep_facts_artifacts` (static contract; extend it, then run it).
- Local SQLite syntax-check of the extended `sweep-facts-rollup.sql` / `sweep-facts-queries.sql` (and `landed-size.sql` if the join needs a helper view) against an empty schema (`sqlite3 :memory: < file.sql`) — the same no-op-safe check `story-points-evidence.md` used for the original SP1–SP4 file.
- No live D1/ClickHouse execution is required for this issue — mirrors the "contract-checked, not yet executed live" status the sibling `sweep-facts` artifacts already carry (`sweep-facts-questions.md` §Verification status). Do not block on Cloudflare/SigNoz credentials.

issues.title: Stale-verdict clearing does not disarm GitHub auto-merge — unreviewed heads merge (#8694)
issues.body:
## Problem
When the stale-verdict guard clears `loom:pr` because the head SHA moved (`loom:verdict-stale` comment), it does not disable GitHub's native auto-merge if one was armed earlier (e.g. by `merge-pr.sh --auto`). The armed auto-merge then fires as soon as the ruleset's required checks pass on the *new, unreviewed* head.

## Observed 2026-09-25
- #8694 merged as `528f2971` at 12:34:07Z, 3 minutes after a Doctor rebase force-push, still labeled `loom:review-requested`, with no approval at the merged head (auto-squash armed 09-22).
- #8847 and #8843 merged at 12:06-12:07Z about 2 minutes after `gh pr update-branch` moved their heads and the stale-verdict notice cleared `loom:pr`.
- It also bypasses the #8248 required-check-freshness guard, which only runs inside `merge-pr.sh`.

## Fix
Wherever a verdict is invalidated for a head move (stale-verdict clearing, `loom:changes-requested`, `loom:operator`, `loom:blocked`), also call `disablePullRequestAutoMerge` and record it in the comment. Add a test for this.

issues.title: Observability: real-time token burn for Codex, OpenCode (GLM) and Kimi stores (#8857 phase 2)
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 2 of #8857. Phase 1 exports real-time token burn (`loom.llm.tokens.*` and `loom.llm.requests` delta counters, `provider`/`model` labels) for **Claude only**, via a host-wide interval sampler over `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/**.jsonl`. The sampler attributes each API message (`message.id`) to its first record's timestamp and counts it once.

The other subscription runtimes need the same interval reader. Their existing readers answer a different question: they return a *session's* total for a session **created** in a window (`codex_usage::fold_rollout` filters on `session_meta.timestamp`, and `SessionFilter` matches nothing when empty). So they cannot be reused as they are for time-bucketed burn. Reusing them would double-count long sessions and drop sessions that started before the window.

## Proposal

For each store, add a per-event, host-wide interval fold that feeds the same `ops::quota` burn emitter with `provider` set to the store's provider:

- **Codex** (`~/.codex` and pooled `~/.loom/codex-profiles/*`): attribute each `token_count` event's delta (`Counters::delta`) to that line's own timestamp. One request = one `token_count` event with a non-null `info`.
- **OpenCode** (ZAI/GLM trials): per-message rows in its SQLite store, attributed by message time.
- **Kimi**: `wire.jsonl` usage events.
- **Pi**: blocked on #8594's schema capture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For each store, a fixture test shows that a session spanning two windows is split between them with no double count.
- [ ] `provider` label values match `tokens.snapshot`'s vocabulary (`claude`, `codex`) or the API-key pool's provider directory name (e.g. `zai`, `kimi`).
- [ ] With no OTLP exporter configured, no store is read.

---

## Curator enrichment (sweep, 2026-09-25)

### On-disk formats verified on a real host (no credential files opened)

- **OpenCode (GLM / Z.ai):** the default XDG store `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is live on this host, *not* only `~/.loom/opt/opencode-<ver>/xdg/...` (the only place `opencode_usage::discover_opencode_dbs` looks). Per-request usage is in table **`message`** (one assistant row per API step; 36k `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3-flash` rows here): `data` JSON carries `role`, `providerID`, `modelID`, `tokens.{input,output,reasoning,cache.read,cache.write}` and `time.{created,completed}` (ms). Rows are written at creation with zero tokens and **updated in place** on completion (`time_updated` column bumps), so the incremental key is completion time, not append offset. Error rows (e.g. the 429 "Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted") carry all-zero tokens.
- **Codex:** `sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/rollout-*.jsonl`; each line has its own `timestamp`; `event_msg/token_count.info.total_token_usage` is cumulative per file and each event is written twice, so a per-file (offset, previous counters, current `turn_context.model`) cursor yields per-event deltas.
- **Kimi:** `~/.kimi-code/sessions/wd_*/session_*/agents/*/wire.jsonl`, append-only; `usage.record` events carry per-request `usage` and `time` (ms); only `usageScope:"turn"` observed. `llm.request` resolves the model alias.

### Plan

1. One shared incremental seam under `observability/ops/burn/`: a per-file **tail cursor** (byte offset, complete lines only, reset on truncation / inode change, files keyed by canonical path so symlinked profile `sessions/` dirs count once) plus a per-provider **event ledger**. Each store decodes new lines/rows into `(timestamp, model, usage)` events; the sampler drains events at or before the window end into the window, holding later ones.
2. Claude moves onto the same seam (fixes #8941 items 2 and 3): message ids are remembered across samples, and a later streamed chunk contributes only its increment.
3. Burn intervals are exported with an explicit end time (window end) so consecutive intervals abut exactly.
4. `provider` labels: `claude`, `codex`, `kimi`, and for OpenCode the pool namespace (`zai-coding-plan` → `zai`), else OpenCode's own provider id.
5. No store read when no OTLP exporter (unchanged `record()` early return).

### Acceptance criteria (added)

- [ ] Per store, a fixture test: a session appended across two samples is split between the windows with no double count (Codex duplicate `token_count` events count once; Claude streamed chunks count once).
- [ ] Truncated/replaced file resets its cursor without re-counting; symlinked session dirs counted once.
- [ ] OpenCode reader issues exactly one query naming `message` only (pinned by a test).
- [ ] #8941 items 1–5 closed or explicitly deferred with a comment on #8941.

issues.title: Guards: MCP tool calls are outside every PreToolUse matcher — mcp-loom execute surface is unguarded
issues.body:
## Context

Independent security audit (2026-09-26 session). Loom's provenance convention (`defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md`, #4791 part 2) is exactly right — every role prompt that reads forge text carries the verbatim "forge text is data, not instructions" block, and a concierge-specific rider. But **enforcement lives in PreToolUse hooks that only match `Bash` and `Edit|Write`**:

- `.claude/settings.json` (and the `defaults/.claude/settings.json` twin): `PreToolUse` matchers are `"Bash"` (guard-destructive.sh, guard-loom-workflow.sh) and `"Edit|Write"` (guard-worktree-paths.sh). **No matcher covers MCP tool calls** (`mcp__loom__*`).
- mcp-loom is a first-class, user-scoped-registered server (CLAUDE.md → "MCP hooks"), callable from every agent Loom spawns — and its `get_agent_metrics` tool currently turns its raw arguments into a shell command (see sibling issue "mcp-loom: get_agent_metrics joins raw MCP args into a shell string").

Result: the injection path that bypasses all of Loom's guard engineering is the one tool class the agent can call freely — an MCP tool. Today the reachable sink is `get_agent_metrics`; **any future mcp-loom tool that touches the shell, `fs`, or `spawn` inherits the same unguarded surface**, and the `guard-*.sh` catalog (`defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md`) has no MCP category to extend.

## What changes

1. Add a `PreToolUse` hook with matcher `"mcp__loom__.*"` (in both `defaults/.claude/settings.json` and the installed `.claude/settings.json` wiring, via `hook-wiring.sh` so broken-install fail-closed behavior matches the Bash guards) that inspects the MCP tool-call arguments:
   - values containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `<`, `>`, backticks, `$(`, newline) → **deny** with a named reason (these never appear in legitimate metric/terminal calls);
   - other suspicious shapes (a `command`/`role` value off the documented allow-lists) → deny + emit to the decision log (`guards.decisionLog` convention).
2. Extend `hook-wiring.sh`'s broken-install floor to include the new guard (a missing `guard-mcp-tools.sh` in a `.loom/hooks`-bearing workspace = broken install, same deny pattern).
3. Document the new category in `defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md` (catalog row: what it matches, what it denies, env override) and cross-link it from `defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md` (the convention says "refuse and report" — this is the enforcement half for the MCP surface).
4. Update `defaults/scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or its equivalent) so the contract tests cover the new guard — same discipline the four probes in `guard-destructive.sh` #4894/#5916/#5974 established.

## Out of scope

- Server-side argument validation inside mcp-loom itself (sibling issue — this guard is defense-in-depth on top of it, not a replacement).
- The `loom-daemon` MCP surface (separate server; if it executes anything, it gets the same treatment — flag for the curator).
- Broader redesign of hook wiring.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A simulated PreToolUse event for `mcp__loom__get_agent_metrics` with `role: "x; touch /tmp/mcp-guard-pwn"` is **denied** by the new hook (hook test, same style as `defaults/hooks/tests/`).
2. Clean calls (documented enum values, numeric `issue`) are allowed, with a decision-log entry when `guards.decisionLog` is on.
3. `check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or equivalent) fails CI when the MCP matcher or the fail-closed floor is missing from the settings wiring.
4. `guard-hooks.md` lists the category with its env override; `untrusted-external-content.md` links it.

## Affected Files

- `.claude/settings.json` / `defaults/.claude/settings.json` - add a `PreToolUse` entry with matcher `mcp__loom__.*` wired through `hook-wiring.sh`, mirroring the existing `Bash` / `Edit|Write` entries
- `.loom/hooks/hook-wiring.sh` / `defaults/hooks/hook-wiring.sh` - extend the broken-install fail-closed floor to require `guard-mcp-tools.sh`
- `.loom/hooks/guard-mcp-tools.sh` (new) - the guard script itself: deny on shell metacharacters in MCP tool-call args, deny+log on off-allow-list `command`/`role` values
- `defaults/hooks/tests/test-guard-mcp-tools.sh` (new) - hook test in the style of `defaults/hooks/tests/test-hook-wiring.sh` / `test-guard-worktree-paths.sh`, covering AC1/AC2
- `scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` - extend so CI fails if the MCP matcher or fail-closed floor is missing (AC3)
- `defaults/docs/guard-hooks.md` - new catalog entry (category, denial shape, env override)
- `defaults/docs/untrusted-external-content.md` - cross-link to the new guard-hooks.md entry as the enforcement half of "refuse and report"

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: `defaults/hooks/tests/test-guard-mcp-tools.sh` simulating a `mcp__loom__get_agent_metrics` PreToolUse event with `role: \"x; touch /tmp/mcp-guard-pwn\"` and asserting `deny` (AC1)
- [ ] Automated: same harness with clean/documented-enum args asserting `allow`, plus a decision-log entry when `guards.decisionLog` is on (AC2)
- [ ] Automated: `scripts/check-guard-scan-contracts.sh` (or its test) fails when the MCP matcher or fail-closed floor is absent from settings wiring (AC3)
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm `guard-hooks.md` lists the new category with its env override and `untrusted-external-content.md` links to it (AC4)

issues.title: telemetry: sweep.outcome carries tokens on only ~10% of sweeps — failed/cancelled attempts are token-less, so lifecycle cost is undercounted
issues.body:
## Problem

Only **10.3%** of `sweep.outcome` records carry `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`: 2,707 of 26,260 in the `loom-fleet-telemetry` D1 store, 2026-08-15..09-29, measured 2026-09-29. The rate is flat at ~10% on every host and every week, so it isn't a version cliff. Tokens are present exactly when `config` is present (2,707 of 3,442), meaning only sweeps whose transcripts could be attributed.

This leaves a systematic hole in cost accounting:

- **Lifecycle cost is undercounted.** Failed and cancelled attempts almost never carry tokens. A per-issue "total tokens to land" sum therefore looks almost identical to the single landing sweep's tokens (Spearman 0.996, 96% of landed issues with a ratio of exactly 1.0). That's an artifact, not a finding. On the 20 multi-attempt issues that *do* have complete tokens, lifecycle is a median **1.5×** the landing sweep.
- **"Didn't spawn" and "spawned but we couldn't read usage" look the same.** Both are simply absent today.

Context: the story-points experiment for #9429/#9430 needs two effort views per issue, **full lifecycle** (every attempt) and **clean** (the landing work only). Without per-attempt tokens, only the clean view is measurable.

## Want

1. Every sweep that ran an agent process carries its token counters (`tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `tokens_by_model`) on `sweep.outcome`, whatever the `result`. That includes failed, cancelled, watchdog-killed and reaper-adopted sweeps.
2. A new `tokens_status` attribute separates the absence cases: `measured` | `not_spawned` (preflight or spawn death, a true zero) | `unattributable` (spawned, but usage couldn't be read, with the reason). Absent-vs-zero discipline per `telemetry-schema.md`: a measured zero is emitted only for `not_spawned`.
3. Reuse the existing usage readers (`usage_source::sweep_tokens_by_model`, the #9313 transcript fold); don't add a new scraper. Cross-file `message.id` dedupe is #9315.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a fleet host, ≥95% of `sweep.outcome` records with `result != success` and a non-zero builder/curator phase carry token counters or `tokens_status=unattributable` with a reason.
- [ ] Tests cover spawn death (`not_spawned`, zero), cancellation mid-builder (measured partial usage), and a missing transcript (`unattributable`).
- [ ] `telemetry-schema.md` documents `tokens_status`.

## Evidence / query

D1 (`loom-fleet-telemetry`, table `records`):

```sql
SELECT json_extract(payload,'$.result') r, count(*) n,
       sum(json_extract(payload,'$.tokens_in') IS NOT NULL) with_tokens
FROM records WHERE kind='sweep.outcome' GROUP BY r;
-- failure 16898 / 1479, success 8808 / 674, cancelled 554 / 554
```

Related: #8052 (role×model token report), #8525 (role-attempt spans carry usage), #9315, 2AMLogic/2am#1331.

issues.title: telemetry: PRs aren't reliably linked to their issue (slice PRs lack Closes, pr_number on 2.7% of sweep.outcome, model field is the config arm)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

**Per-issue work can't be summed reliably, because PRs aren't reliably linked to the issue they implement.** Found while building per-issue effort for the story-points experiment (#9429), over 329 landed issues (2026-08-15..09-29):

- **Slice PRs are invisible to GitHub's issue↔PR link.** Slices reuse `feature/issue-N` but often omit `Closes #N`, so `closedByPullRequestsReferences` misses them. 19 of 329 sweep-landing PRs (from D1 `pr_number`) were not in that connection.
- **Some issues land through many PRs.** 20 issues had more than one merged PR on `feature/issue-N`; `2AMLogic/gf180-pll#237` has **47**. Their lifecycle churn is up to 835× the landing PR's size. Without a reliable link, "work delivered for issue N" is either under-counted (landing PR only) or needs branch-name scraping.
- **The sweep record rarely names its PR.** `sweep.outcome.pr_number` is present on 2.7% of outcomes (697 of 26,260), so telemetry can't make the link either.
- **The recorded model is the config arm, not what ran.** `sweep.outcome.model` records the arm ("sonnet" on every record checked), not the model that ran. The real model has to be inferred from the dominant entry in `tokens_by_model`. Tokens per hand-written line differ ~1.5× between Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 landings, so this matters for any token-based measure.

### Want

1. Every PR opened by a Loom role for issue N carries a machine-readable link: `Closes #N` for the final PR, `Refs #N` plus a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer for slices and partial PRs.
2. `sweep.outcome` always carries `pr_number` (and `pr_numbers[]` when a sweep opens more than one) whenever a PR was opened, merged or updated.
3. `sweep.outcome.model` carries the model(s) that actually ran (dominant model + `models_used`); keep the arm under `config.arm`.

### Acceptance (as originally filed)

- [ ] For a week of landings, 100% of Loom-opened PRs resolve to their issue via either GitHub's closing reference or the `Loom-Issue` trailer.
- [ ] `pr_number` is present on every `sweep.outcome` whose sweep opened or updated a PR (contract test).
- [ ] `model` reflects the actual model on a mixed Opus/Sonnet sweep (contract test).

Related: #9441 (disposition), #9446 (sweep_facts rollup), 2AMLogic/2am#1610 (storyline landed-size facts, which need this link to sum per issue).

---

## Verified corrections

- **2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `9135761f6`** (code read of `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs`, `git log`/`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `gh pr view 9481`): **Want items 2 and 3 already shipped today**, in PR #9481 ("feat(telemetry): sweep facts — disposition, token status, lineage, landing size; claim-label safety; retention + rollups", merged 2026-09-29T14:29:28Z, merge commit `31e7fa58`), which its own body lists under "Partially addressed": *"#9465 — telemetry half ships: `pr_numbers[]` (every sampled PR, first-seen order) and `model` = dominant model that actually ran (arm stays `config.arm`). The `Closes #N` / `Loom-Issue:` trailer convention is the role-prompt half, deferred to the role-prompt authoring discipline."* This matches @turian's comment on this issue (2026-09-29). Concretely, in `outcome_journal.rs`:
  - `pr_numbers` (plural, `Vec<u32>`, first-seen order) is now populated from `self.sampled_pr_numbers(sweep_id)` (line ~732) and carried on `SweepOutcomeRecord.pr_numbers` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs:922`).
  - `model` is reassigned (lines 753-764) to the dominant `(input+output)` model in `tokens_by_model`, falling back to the dispatched model only when no transcript was attributed. The comment at line 753 reads: *"Issue #9465: `model` names what actually ran — the dominant model in the per-model breakdown — with the dispatched model as the fallback when nothing was attributed. The dispatch-time arm stays under `config["arm"]` (#4809)."*
  - `config["arm"]` is inferred from the **original dispatched** model (`infer_arm_from_model`, lines 525-541) — this insertion happens *before* the `model` variable is reassigned to the dominant-actual-model at line 757, so arm and actual-model are correctly decoupled, not accidentally re-deriving arm from the post-swap value.
  - **Only item 1 (the PR-body/commit-message linking convention) remains unimplemented.** Revised scope and acceptance criteria below reflect this.

- **2026-09-29, verified by `gh issue list`** (open-issue search for related telemetry work): the still-**2.7%**-style low `pr_number` population rate this issue's own numbers describe is very likely explained by a *different*, already-filed root cause — **#9476** / **#9477** (near-duplicate; both `loom:triage`, unassigned as of this pass), which document that `loom-daemon` has **two independent code paths** emitting `sweep.outcome` for the same `sweep_id` (`observability::collector::terminal_records`, the live event-bus path, which *always* passes `pr_number: None`/`model: None`/every-other-rich-field-absent — see `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs:586-599`; vs. `sweep_registry::outcome_journal::append_outcome_telemetry_journal`, the rich derivation this issue's Verified-correction entry above describes). The dashboard ingests with `INSERT OR IGNORE` against a `(kind, sweep_id)` unique index, so **first writer wins** — and the live/impoverished path is always first, silently discarding the rich journal record for ~87% of sweeps (#9477's own measurement). **This means the rich `pr_number`/`pr_numbers`/`model` derivation already correct per the entry above frequently never reaches the durable store at all** — a data-pipeline/ingest-race bug, not a gap in the derivation logic this issue set out to fix. Fixing that race is out of scope for *this* issue (#9476/#9477 own it); see "Related Open Work" below for how this issue's own AC is narrowed to not duplicate it.

- **2026-09-29, verified by reading `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`** (lines 444, 483-486, 658): the standalone schema doc is now **stale** relative to the shipped code above — its worked example still shows `"model": "opus"` with no `arm` key and omits `pr_numbers` from the field list, and its `models_used` row explicitly asserts the *old*, now-incorrect semantics: *"`model` names the **dispatched** model, so a sweep that escalated to `claude-opus-5` through the Doctor ladder still reports `model: "sonnet"`."* That sentence is false as of PR #9481. This doc fix is in scope for this issue (see Affected Files).

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29)

### Revised Problem Statement

Two of the three original "Want" items shipped today in PR #9481 (see Verified corrections). The remaining, narrower problem: **Loom roles have no convention for reliably referencing the issue they're implementing on non-final PRs of a plain (non-`loom:epic`) issue.** Today's documented convention (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` § "Partial increments (family/epic issues)", lines 738-747) only prescribes a non-closing `Part of #N` / `Contributes to #N` reference for PRs against issues explicitly labeled `loom:epic`/`loom:epic-phase` or whose body declares a family of work. An **ordinary** issue that happens to land through several merged PRs on the same reused `feature/issue-N` branch (Doctor rework, a Judge-rejected-then-fixed cycle that produced a separate PR, a builder that intentionally shipped a first slice without declaring epic status) has **no documented reference requirement at all** for its non-final PRs — this is the actual gap behind the original issue's "19 of 329 sweep-landing PRs missing from `closedByPullRequestsReferences`" and "20 issues landed through >1 merged PR" findings.

### Revised Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` extends the closing-keyword/`Part of #N` convention to cover **any** multi-PR landing of a single issue — not only declared `loom:epic`/`loom:epic-phase` families — and documents a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer (in addition to, not instead of, `Closes #N` / `Refs #N` or `Part of #N`) as the machine-parseable form a script can grep for without depending on GitHub's closing-keyword parser or prose-phrase matching. State plainly whether this trailer is **required** on every Loom-opened PR or **only** on non-final/slice PRs (the original issue's "Want" implies the latter: `Closes #N` alone suffices for a single-PR landing).
- [ ] `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder.md`'s PR checklist (around line 1308, "PR body uses `Closes #N` ... or `Part of #N` ...") is updated to reference the extended convention.
- [ ] A parser or lint (e.g. a `defaults/scripts/tests/test-*.sh` case, following the existing pattern that already tests `merge-pr.sh`'s `Part of #N` parsing for the code-span pitfall at builder-pr.md:749-762) confirms a `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer round-trips correctly and survives the same code-span/backtick pitfall (#8796) documented for `Part of #N`.
- [ ] Add contract tests for the **already-shipped** derivation logic in `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` that PR #9481 did not add tests for: (a) `pr_numbers` reflects every sampled PR in first-seen order (not just the latest), (b) `model` resolves to the dominant `tokens_by_model` entry rather than the dispatched model on a mixed-model sweep (e.g. dispatch `sonnet`, transcripts dominated by `claude-opus-5` via a Doctor escalation), and (c) `config["arm"]` is still derived from the *original dispatched* model, not the post-reassignment `model` value. None of `outcome_journal/tests.rs`'s existing `arm`-focused tests (lines ~98-196, Issue #4809) actually exercise the model-swap path together with a populated `tokens_by_model` fixture — verify this gap is real before writing tests (grep the test file for a fixture combining both an `arm`-eligible dispatch model *and* a differently-dominant `tokens_by_model` row; none was found in this pass, but re-check against current `main` since #9481 may have landed sibling tests after this curation).
- [ ] Update `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (worked example at lines 437-481, and the `models_used` row at line 658) to reflect the shipped semantics: `model` is the dominant actually-run model with dispatch as fallback, `config.arm` (when inferred) carries the original dispatch-time arm, and `pr_numbers` is documented as a top-level field alongside `pr_number`.
- [ ] The original "100% resolution for a week of landings" AC is a **measurement**, not a unit test — defer it to a follow-up Auditor/Guide-style check run *after* both this issue's trailer convention *and* #9476/#9477's ingest-race fix have landed and had a week of real PRs to observe (the trailer convention alone cannot be verified end-to-end without the ingest-race fix, since #9476/#9477 shows the derived data frequently never reaches the durable store). Do not attempt to satisfy this AC synchronously in this issue's own PR — state that explicitly in the PR body instead.

### Out of scope for this issue / Related Open Work (absorbed or disregarded, per curation convention)

- **#9476** ("two paths emit sweep.outcome per sweep and INSERT OR IGNORE keeps the impoverished one") and **#9477** ("the collector's sweep.outcome wins the INSERT OR IGNORE race...") — **absorbed**: these two (themselves likely near-duplicates of each other — flagging for a future Curator/Champion pass, not resolved here) are the real root cause of the low `pr_number` population rate this issue measured. This issue's AC is revised above to explicitly NOT attempt fixing the dual-emission/ingest race — that belongs to #9476/#9477. Cross-link both from this issue's implementation PR (`Refs #9476, Refs #9477`) so a reader lands on the right issue for the ingest-side fix.
- **#9441** (disposition) / **#9444** (attempt lineage, rework) / **#9446** (sweep_facts rollup) — **disregarded** for this pass: all three are either already merged (per #9481's "Closed by this PR" table) or track independent fields this issue's remaining scope (PR-body convention + doc fix + contract tests) does not touch.
- **2AMLogic/2am#1610** (storyline landed-size facts) — **disregarded**: cross-repo consumer, no action needed in this repo beyond what's already delivered.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` — extend the `Closes #N` / `Part of #N` convention beyond declared epics/families; document the `Loom-Issue: owner/repo#N` trailer.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder.md` — update the PR checklist line (~1308) to match.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/tests.rs` — add the missing contract tests described above (no production-logic change expected; PR #9481 already shipped the derivation).
- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` — correct the stale `model`/`arm`/`pr_numbers` documentation (lines ~437-481, ~658).
- Possibly a new `defaults/scripts/tests/test-*.sh` (or an existing one, e.g. a `merge-pr.sh`-adjacent test) for the `Loom-Issue:` trailer's parse/round-trip behavior — check `defaults/scripts/tests/` for the existing `Part of #N` parser test before adding a new file.

All paths above verified present on `origin/main` @ `9135761f6` (2026-09-29).

issues.body:
## Problem

The `session.summary` records that #8714 G3 introduced are reaching SigNoz but **can't be joined to an issue or a repo**. Live SigNoz, 2026-09-26..29, measured 2026-09-29:

- 4,121 `session.summary` rows (service `loom`) with useful counters: `loom.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}`, `loom.turns`, `loom.wall_ms`, `loom.tool_errors`, plus `session.analysis` `loom.cost_usd`.
- `loom.issue` is present on **1** row.
- `loom.repo` is the **cwd basename**, not the forge slug. Values include worktree/workspace names (`wood-reward`, `the-next-milestone-should-be-a`, `Downloads`, `agent-afb133cdd702752a5`) and only 131 rows are named `issue-N`.
- `trace_id` is empty on every row, so there's no join through the sweep or story trace either.

So per-issue session cost is unrecoverable, even though the counters are exactly what the effort-measurement work (#9429/#9430) needs.

## Want

- `loom.repo` = the `owner/name` forge slug resolved from the session's git remote; omitted if there isn't one. Never a directory name.
- `loom.issue` and `loom.pr_number` filled whenever the session ran inside a sweep or an issue worktree (`.loom/worktrees/issue-N`, `feature/issue-N` branch), or under a role tick that names an issue (see #9231 for role ticks).
- `trace_id` / `parent span` set from the sweep's persisted trace context (the `runtime_usage::join` entry), so a session nests under its `loom.sweep` / story trace.
- Interactive (non-sweep) sessions stay issue-less, but carry `loom.session_kind=interactive` so they're excluded deliberately, not by accident.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Over one day on a fleet host, ≥95% of sweep-originated `session.summary` rows carry `loom.issue` and a slug `loom.repo`, and share the sweep's trace id.
