issues.title: merge-pr.sh: no way to choose the merge method (always squashes when squash is allowed)
issues.body:
## Original Issue

Seen with loom-daemon 0.19.338 (d678331b6).

### Problem

`forge_detect_merge_method` always picks `squash` when the repo allows
squash. A caller can't ask for a merge commit on one PR, for example when a PR
carries commits whose SHAs other files reference, such as generated reports
that record the revision they were produced at. Squashing leaves those SHAs unreachable once
the branch is deleted. The workaround today is to disable squash in the repo
settings for the duration of the merge.

**Suggested fix:**

- add a `--merge-method squash|merge|rebase` flag, validated against the repo's
  allowed methods;
- and/or support a repo-level default in `.loom/config.json`;
- and/or support a PR label such as `loom:merge-commit`.

Related: #8191.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Verified: the claim is accurate (2026-09-25, verified against `origin/main`)

`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-merge-method.sh:39-65` (`forge_detect_merge_method`)
has a fixed preference order — squash > merge > rebase — with no parameter or
env var to request a specific method, and `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh:461`
calls it unconditionally:

```bash
REPO_MERGE_METHOD="$(forge_detect_merge_method "$REPO_NWO" "$GH" 2>/dev/null || echo squash)"
```

`REPO_MERGE_METHOD` then flows into both the immediate-merge path
(`forge_merge_pr`, `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:347`) and the
`--auto` path (`forge_auto_merge` / `loom-daemon forge auto-merge`) with no
override anywhere in between. `forge_merge_pr` itself already accepts an
explicit `merge_method` parameter (line 348: `local ... merge_method="${4:-squash}"`)
— the missing piece is entirely at the call site: nothing ever passes anything
other than the auto-detected value.

**No PR-level or config-level override exists today** — confirmed no
`mergeMethod` key anywhere in `.loom/config.json`/`defaults/config*`, and no
`loom:merge-commit` (or similar) label in `.github/labels.yml`.

### Blocking implementation constraint: this repo forbids new shell logic here (read before implementing)

Both files this fix touches are frozen `contract`-category shell
(`scripts/shell-allowlist.txt:204-225`): *"the file's name is consumed by role
prompts, CI, or hooks... **contract is baseline-only**"* — the CI-enforced
Language Policy (`.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` §"contract") **refuses
new logic in a `contract` file outright**, not just growth past a line
threshold. `merge-pr.sh`'s own allowlist entry says it plainly: *"The name
stays; new logic goes behind it into loom-daemon."* This exact class of
mistake — implementing a real feature as new bash in one of these files — is
what stalled #8654 and #8850 in this same repo; do not repeat it here.

**Implication for the fix**: the actual decision logic — "does the repo allow
the requested method; if not, what do we fall back to" — must be a
`loom-daemon` subcommand (e.g. extend `loom-daemon forge auto-merge`'s
existing `--method` handling, or add a new `loom-daemon forge merge-method
--repo <nwo> [--requested <method>]` that returns the resolved method,
validated against the repo's `allow_squash_merge`/`allow_merge_commit`/
`allow_rebase_merge` flags exactly as `forge_detect_merge_method` does today).
`merge-pr.sh` gets only thin CLI-flag wiring — parse `--merge-method`, pass it
to the daemon call, keep today's shell `forge_detect_merge_method` as the
no-daemon/below-version-floor fallback (same "delegate when available, current
behavior otherwise" pattern `loom_daemon_version_preflight` already
establishes elsewhere in this file). This also rides on rather than fights
#8191 (the umbrella epic porting `merge-pr.sh` to a daemon subcommand
entirely).

**Do not add a `loom:merge-commit` label.** This repo's Curator/CLAUDE.md
policy is to never invent new labels — pursue the CLI flag and/or config
default instead; drop that option from scope.

### Suggested precedence (design decision, not fully settled)

Explicit `--merge-method` CLI flag > `.loom/config.json` per-repo default >
today's auto-detect (squash > merge > rebase). Whichever is requested must
still be validated against the repo's actual allowed methods and fail
predictably (error, not silent fallback) if the requested method isn't
permitted — silently falling back to squash would reproduce exactly the bug
this issue reports, just with an extra ignored flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A caller can request `merge` or `rebase` explicitly (CLI flag and/or
      `.loom/config.json` per-repo default) and `merge-pr.sh` uses it instead
      of the auto-detected method, for both the immediate-merge and `--auto`
      paths.
- [ ] Requesting a method the target repo does not allow fails with a clear
      error naming the allowed methods — it does not silently fall back to
      squash.
- [ ] No request (today's behavior) is unchanged: falls back to the existing
      auto-detect preference order (squash > merge > rebase).
- [ ] The validation/resolution logic lives in a `loom-daemon` subcommand, not
      new logic in `forge-merge-method.sh`/`forge-helpers.sh`/`merge-pr.sh`
      (all three are frozen `contract`-category shell) — `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh`
      and `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` both pass.
- [ ] No new label is introduced.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` (`merge-pr.sh:461` where `REPO_MERGE_METHOD`
  is resolved, plus its arg-parsing block around `:493`) - add `--merge-method`
  CLI flag parsing (thin wiring only — delegates to the daemon, falls back to
  today's `forge_detect_merge_method` when no daemon/below version floor)
- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-merge-method.sh` - reference only; the shell
  fallback path stays as today's implementation, not extended with new
  validation logic
- `loom-daemon/src/forge_cmd.rs` - new or extended subcommand: resolve +
  validate a requested merge method against the repo's allowed strategies
  (mirrors `forge_detect_merge_method`'s GitHub/Gitea branches); `--method` on
  the existing `auto-merge` subcommand (`:526`) is the nearest existing
  surface to extend or model this on
- `.loom/config.json` schema / `.loom/config.example.json` (if a config
  default is chosen) - new optional per-repo `mergeMethod` key
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-helpers.sh` (`:504-549` already covers
  `forge_detect_merge_method`'s auto-detect behavior) - add cases for an
  explicit requested method that is/isn't allowed
- New or extended `loom-daemon` Rust test module covering the new
  subcommand's validation logic

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `loom-daemon` unit tests for the new merge-method
      resolution/validation subcommand — requested method allowed, requested
      method not allowed (clear error), no request (auto-detect unchanged)
- [ ] Automated tests: extend `test-forge-helpers.sh` / add a
      `test-merge-pr-*.sh` case exercising `--merge-method` end-to-end against
      a stubbed `gh`/daemon
- [ ] Manual verification: `./.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh <pr> --merge-method merge --dry-run`
      against a repo that allows merge commits shows the requested method, not
      squash
- [ ] Manual verification: requesting a disallowed method fails with a clear
      error rather than silently squashing
- [ ] Edge cases: repo with only one strategy allowed; repo allowing all
      three; no-daemon / below-version-floor host falls back to today's
      behavior unchanged

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `mechanical`**: choosing where the validation logic lives
(new vs. extended daemon subcommand) and the CLI-flag/config precedence order
takes a small design decision, but a wrong choice is caught mechanically by
this repo's shell-budget/file-size CI gates (which already stalled two other
issues for exactly this mistake) — it will not silently pass review. Not
`complex`: no destructive path, no cross-cutting change, and `forge_merge_pr`
already accepts an explicit `merge_method` parameter, so the plumbing gap is
narrow.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: #8248 freshness guard hard-blocks every merge when the rulesets API returns 403 (private free-plan repos)
issues.body:
Seen with loom-daemon 0.19.338 (d678331b6).

## Problem

On a private repository owned by a GitHub Free account or org,
`loom-daemon merge-pr stale-checks` calls
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/<base>`, and GitHub answers:

    HTTP 403: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.

The guard fails closed (exit 2), so `merge-pr.sh` refuses **every** merge on
such repos. No flag bypasses it: `--allow-unapproved` and
`--redate-stale-checks` don't apply, and the only escape is to point
`LOOM_DAEMON_BIN` at a shim.

On these plans, rulesets and branch protection are unavailable, so nothing can
be a *required* check. The guard's question has a definite answer: "no
required checks, nothing can be stale."

**Suggested fix:** treat this specific 403 ("Upgrade to GitHub Pro …") as "no
rulesets / no required checks" and return CLEAN, perhaps with a warning. Keep
failing closed for other errors (network, auth scope, rate limit).
Alternatively, add a documented operator flag such as
`--skip-freshness-guard` that records a bypass comment, the way
`--allow-unapproved` does.

Related: #8191 (port merge-pr.sh to a daemon subcommand).

issues.title: telemetry: per-phase token attribution on sweep.outcome (curator/builder/judge/doctor), so clean-landing and rework cost are separable
issues.body:
## Problem

Tokens on `sweep.outcome` are **per sweep**, not per phase. `phase_durations` breaks down wall time (curator/builder/judge/doctor), but `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`/`tokens_by_model` are a single total. That blocks two things:

- **Clean-landing cost.** #9430 defines effort as the cost of curator + builder + *first* judge. Today that can only be approximated by the whole sweep's tokens, which include doctor and re-judge cost whenever they happened inside the same sweep.
- **Rework cost.** "How many tokens did doctor/re-judge loops burn?" and "what share of cost is curation vs build vs review?" can't be answered per issue. #8052 measured role shares by hand-scraping transcripts (judge 26%, curator 21%, …), and that number should come from telemetry.

## Want

- Each `phase_durations` entry on `sweep.outcome` also carries that phase attempt's usage: `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, and optionally `tokens_by_model`. Keep the existing sweep totals, which equal the sum of the phases plus any unattributed remainder reported explicitly as `tokens_unattributed`.
- Repeated phases (judge #2, doctor #1..N) are separate entries with an `attempt` index, so "first judge" is addressable.
- Same numbers on the `loom.role_attempt` spans from #8525, so the D1 and OTLP paths agree.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A sweep with curator → builder → judge(fail) → doctor → judge(pass) emits five phase entries, each with usage, and sum(phase tokens) + `tokens_unattributed` = sweep tokens.
- [ ] Unknown per-phase usage is absent (not 0) and counted in `tokens_unattributed`.
- [ ] `telemetry-schema.md` updated.

Related: #8525 (role-attempt spans), #8052, #9430, #9434.

issues.title: operator-priority escalations must reach the operator in Matrix, not only as GitHub comments (#9244 follow-up)
issues.body:
## Problem
#9301 (PR #9320) delivers operator-priority escalations as an idempotent GitHub comment, in the health/status/queue surfaces, and in loom-ui. It doesn't send them to where the operator actually is: the team Matrix General room. The operator's complaint (#9244) is that Loom "putzes around" silently when asked to prioritize. A GitHub comment on the stuck issue repeats the #9268 failure mode, where four agents commented for 7 hours and no human saw it.

The Safehouse sink only relays the frozen event-bus topics, so #9320 deferred Matrix delivery.

## Ask
Deliver each **new** `needs-operator` escalation (and each watchdog stall) for a starred issue to the Matrix General room, mentioning the operator. Deduplicate on the same `<kind>:<specifics>` key #9320 uses, so each ask is posted once fleet-wide.

Options, in order of preference:
1. A new event-bus topic `operator_priority.escalation`, relayed by the Safehouse sink. This needs the topic added to the frozen set with a version bump of the contract.
2. A direct matrix.org post via a configured bot credential (2ambot-equivalent), reference-by-name per `.loom/docs/credentials.md`. No secret goes in the repo.

Also decide the recovery message: post "resolved" when the landing state leaves `needs-operator`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A starred issue entering `needs-operator` produces exactly one Matrix post, fleet-wide, with the concrete ask and a link. The watchdog stall does too.
- [ ] No post for non-starred issues. No repeats across ticks, hosts or restarts.
- [ ] Tested with a fake sink. The docs say how to configure it.

Parent: #9244. Depends on #9320 (#9301).

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-29, verified against `origin/main` @ `af6fab77`)

### Dependencies — resolved

Both items originally listed under "Depends on" are done: PR #9320 **merged** 2026-09-28T13:10:13Z, and #9301 is **closed**. The `needs-operator`/dedup-key infrastructure this issue builds on is live on `origin/main` today. No open blocker remains.

### Implementation Guidance

**Escalation source (#9301/PR #9320), `loom-daemon/src/star_liveness/`:**
- Dedup marker/key: `escalate.rs:25` — `pub const MARKER_PREFIX: &str = "<!-- loom:operator-priority-escalation key=";`, with posting/dedupe logic at `escalate.rs:29` (`marker`), `:36` (`already_posted`), `:46` (`comment_body`), `:66`/`:90`/`:100` (`Ledger`).
- `OperatorAsk` dedupe-key type: `types/star_liveness.rs:127`; the `needs_operator()` iterator: `types/star_liveness.rs:216`.
- Escalation emission is called from `star_liveness/task.rs:226`, driven by the `no_progress` watchdog window (`star_liveness/mod.rs:101-102`, `star_liveness/progress.rs` for stall fingerprinting) — this, not `sweep_registry/watchdog.rs` (which is unrelated sweep-process log-silence detection), is the "watchdog stall" this issue's Acceptance criteria refer to.
- No `operator_priority.escalation` string exists anywhere in the repo yet — Option 1 in the Ask above is not started.

**Safehouse sink, `loom-daemon/src/safehouse.rs`:**
- `spawn_sink` at `safehouse.rs:3120`; the bus-subscriber loop `run_sink` at `safehouse.rs:3241`. It maps existing frozen `EventBus` topics to Matrix envelope-v1 messages over a local `AF_UNIX` socket to a peer daemon (`safehoused`, in the separate `rjwalters/safehouse` repo) — `loom-daemon` itself never talks to Matrix directly. Module header (`safehouse.rs:1-36`) documents the wire protocol.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md:2083` already states the gap this issue closes: "Safehouse / Matrix delivery is not wired yet (the Safehouse sink only narrates the frozen event taxonomy)."
- No `matrix.org`/`2ambot`-style direct posting code exists anywhere in the repo — confirmed via repo-wide grep. Option 2 in the Ask would be new code, not a variant of something existing.

issues.title: work finder: build back-off (WIP limit) on review+merge debt with hysteresis (Phase 2b of #9391)
issues.body:
## Summary

Phase 2b of #9391, split out of #9392 during curation (2026-09-28, against `origin/main` `23afd5c0d`). #9392 is now **2a only**: demand-weighted role-runner width (Judge / Doctor / Champion) plus Champion-first ceiling reservation, and the process-wide **demand ledger** that records per-repo PR debt. This issue carries the other half of #9391 §2: the **work-finder build back-off (WIP limit)**. When review and merge debt are high, the work-finder stops admitting new issue builds, and the slots it frees run PR-only work.

**Depends on #9392 (2a) merging.** That issue adds the demand ledger (`loom-daemon/src/role_runner/demand.rs`). This issue reads the ledger and adds no forge query of its own.

## Problem

As of `23afd5c0d` the work-finder admits new issue builds up to `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent(disk, ram, configured_max)` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs:2250`, called per tick at `:2894` in `spawn_multi_work_finder_task`, `:2708`). The default `configured_max` is `DEFAULT_WORK_FINDER_MAX_CONCURRENT = 3` (`:176`). Admission reads no review or merge debt, however deep those queues are. #9391's 2026-09-28 measurement found 28 PRs in `loom:review-requested`, 59 in `loom:pr` and 106 ready issues.

## Proposal

- Compute `review_debt + merge_debt` from the #9392 demand ledger, summed over this host's registered roots. Only fresh entries count. An unobserved root, or an entry older than the ledger TTL, contributes nothing.
- Hysteresis: the back-off engages once the sum is `> W` and releases once it is `< W_low`. Between the two the previous state holds.
- While backed off, the work-finder admits **no new `loom:issue` builds**. Sweeps already in flight are untouched. The wiring point is the per-tick admission call. The back-off is OR'd in the way `saturation_held` / the admission brake (#4903) already is: `tick_multi_with_repo_cap` (`work_finder.rs:1540`) takes a `saturation_held: bool`. Either a new held reason or a distinct flag is acceptable, provided the tick report and log name it separately.
- **PR-only work in the freed slots.** As of `23afd5c0d` the work-finder never dispatches `SweepTarget::PrSet` (`grep -n PrSet loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` returns nothing), so this needs a new candidate source. The curator of this issue should judge whether that part fits this PR or splits again into 2c. The back-off on its own already stops finished work from piling up, and the role runner's Judge/Champion (with #9392's reservation) drain the queue.

## Config keys (proposed defaults, from #9391 §2)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `autonomous.workFinder.buildBackoff.enabled` | `true` | `false` gives exactly today's admission |
| `autonomous.workFinder.buildBackoff.high` (`W`) | `40` | engage when `review_debt + merge_debt > W` |
| `autonomous.workFinder.buildBackoff.low` (`W_low`) | `25` | release when the sum `< W_low`; a config with `low >= high` is rejected and falls back to the defaults, with a WARN |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hysteresis unit tests: sum exactly `W` does not engage; `W+1` engages; while engaged, a value in `[W_low, W]` stays engaged; exactly `W_low` stays engaged; `W_low-1` releases; while released, a value in `[W_low, W]` stays released.
- [ ] While engaged, no new issue build is admitted in a `tick_multi_*` test with fake sources. In-flight sweeps are not cancelled.
- [ ] An unobserved or stale ledger never engages the back-off (fails open, like `is_review_stalled`'s "cannot tell" rule, `health.rs:2036`).
- [ ] One INFO line on each engage and release edge, naming the debt sum, `W` and `W_low`. No per-tick spam.
- [ ] No new forge call per tick. The input is the #9392 ledger only.
- [ ] New keys documented in `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s config table.

## Out of scope

- Before/after operational measurement. It is tracked as a post-merge checklist item on #9392.
- Token-pool-headroom-aware admission (#9391 §2, "optional").

Related: #9391, #9392, #7649 (`PrSet` handoff), #4903 (admission brake).

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-28, verified against `origin/main` `77b6b18db`)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->
<!-- loom:points=8 -->

`77b6b18db` is `5b721e0d6` (the #9413 merge that closed #9392 / Phase 2a) plus a version bump that touches no `loom-daemon/src` code. **Depends on #9392: satisfied.** The ledger is on main. This section **supersedes** the Proposal bullet "PR-only work in the freed slots" and the Acceptance criteria above. Where they disagree, this section wins.

### Citation check (all line numbers as of `77b6b18db`, re-check before relying on them)

| Cited in body | Actual | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `work_finder.rs:2250` `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent` | `:2250-2256` | unchanged |
| `:2894` per-tick call | `:2894`, inside `spawn_multi_work_finder_task` (`:2708`) | unchanged |
| `:176` default | `DEFAULT_WORK_FINDER_MAX_CONCURRENT = 3` at `:176` | unchanged |
| `:1540` `tick_multi_with_repo_cap(.., saturation_held: bool, ..)` | `:1540`. The saturation check is in pass 2 at `:1901-1905`, then the #9244 overflow and cap checks at `:1909-1917` | The **only production call** is `:3139` (`saturation_held` computed at `:3005`). `repo_cap.rs:321` is the `tick_multi_with_sharding` wrapper |
| `SweepTarget::PrSet` | **Wrong name.** The type is `SweepKind::PrSet` (`sweep_registry/dispatch.rs:1757`, `watchdog.rs:2128`) | `git grep -n PrSet -- loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs 'loom-daemon/src/work_finder/*'` returns nothing, so the work-finder never dispatches Mode C |
| `health.rs:2036` `is_review_stalled` | `:2036` | unchanged |

**Axes.** The body says `review_debt + merge_debt`. #9391 §2 defines `review_debt = review_requested + changes_requested` and `merge_debt = loom:pr`. So the back-off input sums **all three** ledger axes: `DebtAxis::Review + Changes + Merge`.

### Data path: how the work-finder reads the #9392 ledger (traced)

- **Same process, shared static.** `daemon_service.rs:1488` spawns `work_finder::spawn_multi_work_finder_task` and `:1907` spawns `role_runner::spawn_multi_role_task`, both inside one `run_daemon`. The ledger is `role_runner::demand::global()` (`demand.rs`, a `static OnceLock<DemandLedger>`). `role_runner.rs:3956` declares `pub mod demand;`, so the work-finder can call `crate::role_runner::demand::global()`. The work-finder already reaches into the role runner this way: `:3010` calls `crate::role_runner::global_active_run_count()`.
- **Read cost.** `DemandLedger::host_debt(stale)` is one mutex lock over an in-memory map. It does no I/O and is safe to call once per work-finder tick. **No new forge call.**
- **Who writes the ledger, and when (traced).**
  - Review and Changes: `concurrent_dispatch.rs:416` (`forge_queue_probe`) records the queue-gate listing. That listing runs only inside an *admitted* judge or doctor run (`run_gated`, `:436-446`). Judge and doctor default to 300s intervals (`role_runner.rs:450-560`).
  - Merge: `concurrent_dispatch.rs:724` (`record_merge_debt`) runs **after** an admitted champion run finishes. Champion defaults to 600s.
  - A failed listing records nothing, so the entry ages out rather than reading as `0`.
- **Staleness.** Pass `demand::read_demand_config(&fallback_root).stale()`, which is `autonomous.roleRunner.demandWidth.staleSecs` (default `1800`) resolved from the daemon's primary workspace. That is the same root the work-finder already resolves its machine-level knobs from (`ConfiguredMaxReloader::new(fallback_root, ..)`, `:2735`). Do **not** add a second TTL knob.
- **Fail-open cases.** Each of these leaves every axis `None`, so the back-off never engages:
  - the role runner is disabled on this host;
  - a root has `demandWidth.enabled: false` (`record_listing` / `record_merge_debt` then record nothing for it);
  - judge and doctor are ceiling-refused for longer than `staleSecs`.
- **Scope is this host's ledger.** `DemandLedger::retain_roots` drops roots that left the registry. Role sharding (#6374) means a host's ledger covers only the roots whose roles it runs. So the back-off is host-local, and two hosts can disagree. That is intended (#9391: "all per host").

**Debt value.** `debt = Σ axis.total over axes that are Some`. `None` (the **unobserved** case) is used only when all three axes are `None`. A partly observed ledger sums what it has, which can only err toward *not* engaging.

### Design decision: option (a), back-off only. No PR-sweep dispatch in this issue.

**Recommendation:** while engaged, the work-finder admits no new issue builds, and nothing else changes. The freed capacity is absorbed by the existing role-runner PR roles, which since #9392 are already demand-weighted: judge and doctor width `clamp(ceil(debt/3), 1, min(4, budget))`, plus the champion-first reservation. The body's "freed slots run PR-only work" becomes an **implicit** effect, not a new dispatch path.

Why not (b), a new `PrSet` candidate source dispatching `/loom:sweep --prs N`:
1. **It needs a new per-tick forge read.** Choosing *which* PRs to hand a Mode C sweep needs PR numbers, and the ledger stores only counts (`LedgerEntries = HashMap<(PathBuf, DebtAxis), (usize, Instant)>`). That breaks this issue's "no new forge call per tick" constraint.
2. **It duplicates the role runner.** A Mode C sweep runs Judge, then Doctor, then Merge on PRs that the role runner's judge, doctor and champion loops are already dispatched at, per repo, sized to the same debt. Per-PR claim locks would dedup the collisions, but only after an agent has spawned.
3. **The pools do not trade slots.** Build admission (`maxConcurrent`, default 3) and the role runner's ceiling (`roleRunner.maxConcurrent`, default 7) are separate budgets. A backed-off build slot is not a role slot. The resources the two actually share are the token pool and host load, and the admission brake counts role runs through `global_active_run_count()`. Stopping builds frees exactly those shared resources for the PR roles, which is the WIP-limit intent.

Why not (c), reusing the #7649 watchdog conversion: that path (`watchdog.rs:2098-2160`) converts **one specific** stalled sweep's recovery into `PrSet([pr])` after a *verified* `OpenPrDispatchError`. It is a recovery mechanism keyed to an existing sweep, not a candidate source. Generalising it would amount to (b) anyway.

**The one thing (b) would buy that (a) does not:** parallelism *within* one repo beyond one run per `(repo, role)`, which Phase 1 enforces. If post-merge measurement shows debt staying above `W_low` on a single hot repo while judge and champion are admitted every interval (that is, per-repo serialisation is what binds), file (b) as Phase 2c then. **No split issue is filed now.** It is a conditional follow-up, listed in the post-merge checklist below.

### Hysteresis and state (exact semantics)

State is `Released` (the initial state) or `Engaged`. It is evaluated once per work-finder tick, before `tick_multi_*`:

| Current | Input | Next |
|---|---|---|
| Released | unobserved | Released |
| Released | `debt > high` | **Engaged** (edge) |
| Released | `debt <= high` | Released |
| Engaged | unobserved | **Released** (edge, reason `unobserved`, fail open) |
| Engaged | `debt < low` | **Released** (edge) |
| Engaged | `debt >= low` | Engaged |
| any | `enabled: false` | Released (edge only if it was Engaged) |

So `debt == high` does not engage, `high+1` does. While engaged, `debt == low` holds and `low-1` releases.

**Config**, read every tick from `fallback_root` via `config_resolver::resolve_effective_config` (the `admission_brake::read_admission_brake_config` pattern, `admission_brake.rs:249`), under `autonomous.workFinder.buildBackoff`:

| Key | Default | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | non-bool: default |
| `high` (`W`) | `40` | positive integer, else default |
| `low` (`W_low`) | `25` | positive integer, else default. **`low >= high` rejects the pair**: both fall back to `40/25`, with one WARN per distinct bad config (not per tick). `low = 0` is rejected as non-positive, because `debt < 0` can never release |

No env tier: none of the `demandWidth` keys has one either.

**Logging.** Log one INFO line per edge, naming the debt, its per-axis split, `high`, `low` and the reason. Example:
`work_finder: build back-off ENGAGED — review+changes+merge debt 87 (review=28 changes=0 merge=59) > high=40; new issue builds held until < low=25 (#9410)`.
Release lines follow the same shape; the unobserved variant says `debt unobserved — failing open`. Steady state logs nothing above DEBUG. Also add `build_backoff_held={}` to the existing `axis_line` (`:3117`), which is already INFO-on-change and DEBUG otherwise.

### Which candidates bypass the back-off

- **`loom:operator-priority` (starred): bypass.** A star is an explicit operator instruction to do this now (#9244). The back-off is an autonomous throughput policy, and it must not overrule a human. The saturation brake does hold starred work (`:1901` runs before the overflow check), but that brake is a physical host-safety guard. This is a policy guard, so the precedents differ on purpose. Starred candidates still go through the global cap, the #9244 overflow slot, the ramp cap and the per-repo cap as they do today.
- **`main_red_fix` candidates: bypass.** `PriorityCandidate::main_red_fix` (`work_finder/ordering.rs`) is set only while that repo's `main` is verified red. A red main blocks merges, so the fix *reduces* merge debt. Holding it would make the back-off keep itself engaged.
- Everything else is deferred.

### Implementation guidance

1. **New module `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/build_backoff.rs`.**
   - `BuildBackoffConfig` holds `{enabled, high, low}`, with `parse(&Value)` and `read(root)`.
   - `BuildBackoff` holds `{engaged: bool}`, with a **pure** `observe(&mut self, debt: Option<DebtReading>, cfg) -> Option<Edge>` and a `held()` accessor. `DebtReading` carries the total plus the per-axis split for the log line.
   - `fn debt_from(host: &HostDebt) -> Option<DebtReading>` sums the Some axes and returns `None` when all three are None.
   - Keep the ledger read in the loop, not in the pure function, so tests inject a `HostDebt` directly.
2. **Loop wiring** (`spawn_multi_work_finder_task`). Hold one `BuildBackoff` across ticks, next to `was_halted` and similar state. Each tick:
   - read the cfg;
   - compute `demand::global().host_debt(demand::read_demand_config(&fallback_root).stale())`;
   - call `observe` and log any edge;
   - pass `build_backoff_held` into the tick.
3. **Tick function.** Follow the existing layering (`tick_multi` → `_with_admission_cap` → `_with_saturation_brake` → `_with_repo_cap`) rather than adding a 10th positional argument to every caller and test. Add an outermost `tick_multi_with_build_backoff(.., build_backoff_held: bool)` that holds the body, and make `tick_multi_with_repo_cap` delegate with `false`.
   - In pass 2, insert the check **after** the saturation check (`:1901`) and **before** the overflow and cap checks:
     `if build_backoff_held && !(cand.operator_priority || cand.main_red_fix) { report.deferred_build_backoff += 1; resolve(.., Qd::DeferredBuildBackoff, None); continue; }`
   - The single-workspace `tick_with_lanes` (`:1229`) is test/reference only ("retained for reference/tests", `:2286`). Leave it untouched.
4. **Report and wire types.** These changes follow the `deferred_saturation` / `saturation_held` pair exactly:
   - `TickReport`: add `deferred_build_backoff: usize` and `build_backoff_held: bool`.
   - `WorkFinderTickSummary` in `types/work_finder_tick.rs`: add both fields, with `#[serde(default)]` for older readers, and add them to the summary tallies at `:153` and `:166`.
   - `QueueDisposition::DeferredBuildBackoff`: wire name `deferred_build_backoff`, `state()` = `"ready"`, reason `"waiting: build back-off (review/merge debt high)"`. Add it to `ALL`, which grows from 23 to 24.
   - Handle the new variant everywhere the compiler flags it: `dispatch_plan.rs:90`, `observability/ops/dwell.rs:79`, `observability/ops/dispatch.rs` (the `:58` reasons list and the `:87` tick-result precedence), `observability/ops/turnaround.rs:138`, and `star_liveness/collect.rs:305`.
   - Older clients already parse an unknown disposition as `Unknown` (`#[serde(other)]`).
5. **Explicit dispatch is unaffected.** IPC `dispatch_sweep` does not go through `tick_multi_*` (`git grep -n tick_multi -- loom-daemon/src/ipc.rs` is empty on `77b6b18db`). As with the brake, "an operator asking by hand is not autonomous admission".

### Acceptance criteria (these replace the list above)

- [ ] **AC1, hysteresis (pure unit tests on `BuildBackoff::observe`, defaults 40/25).**
  - From Released: 40 stays Released; 41 goes to Engaged.
  - While Engaged: 40, 25 and 30 stay Engaged; 24 goes to Released.
  - From Released: 30 stays Released; 25 stays Released.
  - `observe` returns `Some(edge)` exactly on the two transitions, and `None` otherwise.
- [ ] **AC2, fail open.**
  - An all-`None` `HostDebt` never engages from Released.
  - An all-`None` `HostDebt` while Engaged releases with reason `unobserved`.
  - A ledger whose entries are all older than `staleSecs` gives the same results as all-`None`. Test this through `DemandLedger::record_at` + `host_debt_at` on a test-local ledger.
  - A partly observed ledger (for example, only Merge fresh) sums only that axis.
- [ ] **AC3, axes.** The debt is Review + Changes + Merge. A test records 20/10/15 on one root and asserts `45 > 40` engages.
- [ ] **AC4, admission while engaged** (a `tick_multi_with_build_backoff` test with fake sources and dispatchers, following `work_finder/tests/operator_priority.rs`):
  - no plain candidate is dispatched, and each is resolved `DeferredBuildBackoff`;
  - `report.deferred_build_backoff` equals the number deferred;
  - in-flight sweeps are untouched: occupancy is unchanged and nothing is cancelled.
- [ ] **AC5, bypass.** In the same engaged tick:
  - a `loom:operator-priority` candidate **is** dispatched, still subject to the global cap and #9244 overflow;
  - a `main_red_fix` candidate **is** dispatched;
  - with `build_backoff_held = false`, the tick is byte-for-byte identical to `tick_multi_with_repo_cap` (the existing tests pass unchanged).
- [ ] **AC6, config.** Parse tests cover:
  - the defaults;
  - `enabled: false` (never engages, and releases if engaged);
  - a valid custom pair;
  - `low >= high`, which falls back to 40/25 and returns a WARN-worthy flag;
  - `low: 0`, negative values and non-integers, each of which falls back per key.
- [ ] **AC7, logging.**
  - Exactly one INFO line per edge, naming the debt total, the per-axis split, `high` and `low`.
  - No INFO line on non-edge ticks. Assert this through `observe`'s return value, not by capturing logs.
  - `axis_line` carries `build_backoff_held=`.
- [ ] **AC8, no new forge call.** The only input is `demand::global().host_debt(..)`. The new module makes no `forge_listing` or `gh` call; a builder self-check with `git grep -n "forge_listing\|gh_bin" loom-daemon/src/work_finder/build_backoff.rs` should return nothing.
- [ ] **AC9, wire compatibility.** A `QueueDisposition` round-trip test covers `deferred_build_backoff`, and `ALL.len() == 24`. A `WorkFinderTickSummary` JSON with no new fields still deserialises.
- [ ] **AC10, docs.**
  - `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` gets a `buildBackoff` subsection near the saturation-brake one (`:3456`), with a config table and the edge semantics above. It must state that the ledger comes from the role runner and that with the role runner off, the back-off is inert.
  - The disposition list at `:2118` gains `deferred_build_backoff`.
  - `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (`:1221` disposition enum) and `defaults/docs/observability.md` (`:485` mapping table) are updated.
- [ ] **AC11.** `cargo test -p loom-daemon` and `cargo clippy -p loom-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

### Test plan

- Automated: `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/build_backoff.rs` (inline `#[cfg(test)]` for AC1-3, AC6 and AC8) and **new** `loom-daemon/src/work_finder/tests/build_backoff.rs`, registered in `work_finder/tests.rs` beside `mod operator_priority;` (`:2521`), for AC4-5.
- Manual (post-merge, on one host): with `buildBackoff.high` temporarily set below the host's current debt, confirm one `ENGAGED` INFO line, confirm `loom-daemon queue` shows `deferred_build_backoff` rows for unstarred issues, then restore the config and confirm one `RELEASED` line.

### Deploy consequence (read before merging)

On 2026-09-28, #9391 measured about 106 open PRs in debt (28 + 19 + 59) across 2AMLogic + loom, against `high = 40`. Any host whose owned slice carries that debt will **engage at the first tick after deploy and stop admitting unstarred builds** until its debt falls below 25. That is the WIP-limit behaviour #9391 asked for, not a bug. `loom:pr` includes PRs held for operator merge, which champion cannot drain, so a host can stay engaged for a long time. The two escape hatches are `buildBackoff.enabled: false` and starring an issue.

### Post-merge checklist (not builder ACs)

- [ ] Before/after measurement per #9391: `loom:reviewing` concurrency, median dwell in `loom:review-requested` / `loom:pr`, tokens per merged PR, and hours engaged per day.
- [ ] If a host stays engaged longer than about 24h with judge and champion admitted every interval on the hot repo, file Phase 2c: work-finder `SweepKind::PrSet` (Mode C) dispatch for intra-repo PR parallelism, option (b) above.
- [ ] If merge-held PRs keep a host engaged, decide whether the Merge axis should exclude operator-held PRs. That would be a `demand.rs` change on the champion probe, not here.

issues.title: Observability & Tuning: Fleet-wide token burn rate (TPM/RPM), account exhaustion downtime, and worker concurrency scaling
issues.body:
## Problem

To optimize throughput and maximize token utilization across LLM subscriptions (Claude, Codex, etc.), operators need visibility into whether the fleet is hitting quota ceilings, idling due to account exhaustion, or constrained by static per-host concurrency limits.

## Proposal

1. **Fleet-Wide Token Burn Tracking:**
   - Export aggregate and per-provider/model TPM and RPM metrics to SigNoz.
   - Compare actual consumption against theoretical subscription/tier limits.
2. **Account Exhaustion & Rotation Downtime:**
   - Measure duration and frequency of account backoffs, 429s, and proxy account rotations.
   - Alert/report when all accounts in a pool are exhausted simultaneously.
3. **Worker Concurrency Profiling & Headroom Tuning:**
   - Profile RAM, CPU, and disk headroom per worker to determine if builder/judge concurrency can safely scale up (e.g. from 1–2 to 4–6 parallel jobs per host).
   - Measure useful vs wasted tokens (landed PRs vs timed-out / aborted / `skipped_load` attempts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Real-time TPM/RPM metrics aggregated across accounts visible in SigNoz.
- [ ] Account exhaustion downtime tracked.
- [ ] Concurrency limits per host configurable and observable relative to host resource pressure.

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-25, against `main` @ `277db2ce`)

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

### Scope decisions

- **Proposal 3 (concurrency scaling) is split out to #8928** (`loom:operator-decision`). The cap is already configurable (`autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrent`) and already observable: `loom.dispatch.max_concurrent`, plus the host memory/swap/volume gauges from #8909. What remains is operator judgement. "Useful vs wasted tokens" needs per-run attribution, so it belongs to #8908 and #8052.
- **#8908 stays open, with a clean boundary.** #8908 attaches *per-execution* token counts to `loom.runtime.run` spans (a trace join). This issue exports *host-wide, time-bucketed* burn and pool state, independent of any run. The triage note called #8908 a prerequisite; that no longer holds, because phase 1 samples the Claude transcript store by time window directly and never joins to a span.
- **#8058 does not have to land first.** The pool gauges measure the `exhausted` flag that actually gates selection today. That is the true "dispatch is starved" signal, even though it is over-broad per model class. A `model` label can follow #8058.
- **#8052** is the offline `activity.db` report and has no code overlap.
- **#8856 (dwell/starvation)** is being built in parallel. Keep new `MetricName` variants in one contiguous block and rebase before merging.

### Phasing

- **Phase 1 (this issue):** Claude real-time burn, pool gauges for every pool (Claude, Codex, and API-key providers such as ZAI/Kimi), snapshot-derived exhaustion counters, and the four #8909 Judge carry-overs.
- **Phase 2, #8930:** per-event interval readers for Codex, OpenCode (GLM) and Kimi. Their existing readers fold whole sessions by creation time, which is wrong for rates.
- **Phase 3, #8931:** reason-classified account marks (429 / exhausted / session limit) at the provider-health-feedback seams, plus pool-hold spans.

### Phase 1 design

Everything goes through `observability::ops`, the path added in #8909. Nothing runs when no OTLP exporter is registered.

A new `observability/ops/quota.rs` is called from `collector::sample_snapshots` on the existing 5-minute snapshot cadence:

1. **Claude burn.** Walk `claude_projects_dir()` for `*.jsonl` files (including `subagents/`) whose mtime is on or after the window start. Decode records with `script_helpers::transcript_usage::usage_from_record`. Group by `message.id`, keeping the first timestamp and the per-counter max, the same dedupe `activity::transcript_parse` uses. Count a message only when its first timestamp falls in `(prev_end, now − 60s]`. The lag lets streamed chunks finish.
   - Emit delta counters with `interval_start = prev_end`, labels `provider=claude` and `model`: `loom.llm.tokens.input`, `.output`, `.cache_read`, `.cache_write` (unit `{token}`), and `loom.llm.requests` (distinct message ids, unit `{request}`). TPM and RPM are rates over these counters in SigNoz.
   - Skip `<synthetic>` records. The first sample after start only initialises the window, so history is never replayed.
2. **Pool state**, per provider. Sources: the `tokens.snapshot` accounts (Claude, Codex) and `api_keys_pool::list_accounts` for enabled accounts (ZAI, Kimi, …).
   - `loom.pool.accounts{provider,state=usable|exhausted}` gauge.
   - `loom.pool.exhausted{provider}` gauge: 1 when at least one account is exhausted and none are usable.
   - `loom.pool.exhaustions{provider}` delta: accounts newly exhausted since the previous sample.
   - `loom.pool.exhausted_seconds{provider}` delta: seconds since the previous sample while the pool reads as exhausted (sample-and-hold). This is the downtime number.

No new label keys are needed; `provider`, `model` and `state` are already allowlisted.

### Required carry-overs from #8909's Judge

issues.title: Fleet singleton jobs: first-class captain placement so fleet hosts can be identical
issues.body:
<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

## Problem
A multi-host Loom fleet has two kinds of scheduled job:
- **Per-host jobs** watch *this* host: the daemon watchdog, clean, resync, drift. Every host runs them.
- **Singleton jobs** watch *one shared thing*: a forge-wide queue check, a public feed staleness check, a shared edge queue pull, a token-pool anomaly check. Exactly one host may run each one, because `gh-alert`-style dedup is read-then-write with no lock (the #6714 race class), so two hosts file duplicate alerts.

Loom has no concept of the second kind. Operators (2AMLogic/2am) place singletons by hand-installing a timer on a chosen host and documenting it in prose. Three consequences follow:
- Hosts that should be identical aren't. 2AMLogic/2am#1125 found `loom-worker-2` carrying two singleton timers that `loom-worker-1` lacks.
- An image-built or rebuilt worker silently loses the singletons, or duplicates them.
- Nothing enforces "exactly one". Wrappers each reinvent a fail-closed host gate: 2am's `batch-fleet-reconcile-schedule.sh` and `loom-wake-pull-schedule.sh` do it by hand, and others don't.

## Proposal
- **A fleet-level designation of which host runs singletons**, e.g. `fleet.captain: <host id>` in the machine or host config tier, compared against `host_identity()` (LOOM_HOST_ID). Assigned by the operator, with no election. 2am's vocabulary is "captain" (2AMLogic/2am FLEET.md §Host topology), meaning assigned rather than elected.
- **Declared singleton jobs** that the daemon, or the schedule helper Loom ships, arms **only** when this host is the captain, and refuses on any other host (fail closed, with a message naming the captain). Per-host jobs are unchanged.
- **Observability:** `host.health` reports `is_captain` plus the singleton jobs armed here. The dashboard flags any singleton armed on a non-captain, and a fleet with no captain reporting.
- **Optional later:** a lease, so a captain that is down for longer than N hours can be noticed. Not failover; just an alert.

## Why upstream
Identical fleet hosts (golden image, `fleet add-worker`) are a Loom-level goal. Hand-placed singletons are the part that currently can't be made identical. Downstream tracking: 2AMLogic/2am#1132 (move 2am's singletons to the captain), 2AMLogic/2am#1125 (identical workers).

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-09-25)

Problem statement, proposal, and rationale are already clear and well-argued. Adding the required sections, a scope clarification, and precise pointers into this repo's existing code that the Proposal builds on.

### Scope clarification: `gh-alert`, `batch-fleet-reconcile-schedule.sh`, `loom-wake-pull-schedule.sh` are 2AMLogic/2am tooling, not loom's

Verified against this repo (`rjwalters/loom`) — none of these three exist here (`grep -rn` for each returns zero hits; `find` for the two script names returns zero hits). They're referenced correctly as *consumer-repo* precedent (2AMLogic/2am hand-rolling the fail-closed gate this issue wants to make first-class), not as something already present in loom to extend. A Builder should not go looking for them in this tree.

### `host_identity()` / `LOOM_HOST_ID` — already exists, this is what `fleet.captain` compares against

`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/mod.rs:807` (`pub fn host_identity() -> String`), precedence `LOOM_HOST_ID` env (`HOST_ID_ENV` const, `mod.rs:189`) > `$HOSTNAME` > the `hostname` binary > `UNKNOWN_HOST` sentinel. This is the "operator-controlled, stable across launch contexts" identity issue #5063 already established fleet-wide — `fleet.captain: <host id>` is compared against this, not a new identity concept.

### Where `fleet.captain` belongs: tracked `.loom/config.json`, not a host-local env var

`.loom/config.json` has no `fleet` key today (top-level keys: `version, offlineMode, autonomous, buildGate, guards, branchProtection, terminals, safehouse, sweep, guide, runtimes, observability`). The existing precedent for *which config tier a fleet-wide knob belongs in* is the role-runner sharding table at `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md:5315-5327`: a value that must be **identical fleet-wide** belongs in the **tracked** `.loom/config.json` (a committed file is identical fleet-wide by construction) — e.g. `shardCount`/`shardKey` — while a value that must **differ per host** stays host-local-only (env var), e.g. `shardIndex`. Since every host must agree on who the captain is, `fleet.captain` follows the `shardCount`/`shardKey` precedent: tracked `.loom/config.json`, not an env var. (There is a separate, weaker-fit candidate — the untracked, operator-provisioned `~/.loom/fleet.json` / `FleetRegistry` in `loom-daemon/src/fleet/mod.rs:679` — but that's SSH/drain-state bookkeeping, not a config-value store, and isn't distributed to every host the way a tracked repo file is.)

### Closest existing fail-closed pattern: `host_affinity.rs` (#7456) — issue-scoped, not fleet-config-scoped, but the shape to mirror

`loom-daemon/src/host_affinity.rs` (416 lines) already implements the exact shape this issue wants at fleet-config scope: a `HostConstraint` struct (`required: BTreeSet<String>`), `matches(host_id)` — empty set = runs anywhere, non-empty = exact membership only, **no partial/case-insensitive fallback** (its own "Fail-closed semantics (load-bearing)" doc block). Two enforcement points: `work_finder`'s autonomous tick (via `IssueLike::host_constraint()`, `mod.rs:393`) and `loom-daemon dispatch <issue>` CLI (`cli/dispatch.rs:145,161-185`, refuses naming the required host(s) unless `--ignore-host-constraint` is passed, wired at `main.rs:388-392` / `daemon_service.rs:184-193`). This issue's captain-gate is a **new, separate mechanism** (fleet-config-scoped, not issue-scoped) — cite `host_affinity.rs` as the pattern to mirror stylistically (fail-closed match, named-host refusal message, explicit override flag), not as code to extend directly.

### Contrast, not precedent: #6714's filing lock is deliberately fail-*open*

The issue's own "#6714 race class" reference is this repo's fleet-wide issue-filing lock (`loom-daemon/src/peer_claims.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/filing_lock.rs`) — a cross-host TTL mutex via peer-claim ads. It explicitly **degrades open** (`filing_lock.rs:109`; disabling it makes every acquire degrade open) rather than fail-closed, and it's a distributed lock, not an election/assignment. Worth noting so a Builder doesn't mistake it for prior art to extend — it solves a different problem (mutual exclusion under uncertainty) with the opposite failure direction from what this issue wants (fail-closed captain gating).

### `host.health` already exists — this is what gains `is_captain`

`HostHealthRecord` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs:961`, variant `TelemetryRecord::HostHealth` at `mod.rs:259`) already ships with fields including `dispatch_halted`/`halt_reason` — the nearest existing analog to the boolean-plus-reason shape `is_captain` needs. Constructed in `sample_host_health()` at `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs:704-753`, where the new field(s) would be populated. Every optional field on this struct follows an established `#[serde(default)]`, omit-when-unmeasurable contract; `is_captain` (and an armed-singleton-jobs list) should follow the same pattern.

### Dependencies

None. This is a self-contained design-and-build issue; nothing else in the open queue blocks it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fleet.captain: <host id>` is a recognized key in the tracked `.loom/config.json` schema, documented in `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md`'s canonical config-knob table (mirroring the `shardCount`/`shardKey` "identical fleet-wide, tracked" precedent, not the `shardIndex` "host-local" one)
- [ ] A declared-singleton-job mechanism (daemon-side, or the schedule helper Loom ships) compares its own `host_identity()` against `fleet.captain` and arms **only** on a match; on a non-match it refuses with a message naming the current captain (mirroring `host_affinity.rs`'s named-host refusal message style, e.g. `cli/dispatch.rs:145`)
- [ ] Per-host jobs are provably unaffected — no existing per-host cron/timer/tick gains a captain check
- [ ] `HostHealthRecord` (`telemetry/mod.rs:961`) gains an `is_captain` field (and an armed-singleton-jobs list), populated in `sample_host_health()` (`observability/collector.rs:704-753`), following the struct's existing `#[serde(default)]` contract
- [ ] The dashboard (`dashboard/src/redaction.ts` allowlist + `dashboard/src/publicPage.ts` or the `dashboard/web/src` frontend) flags (a) a singleton armed on a non-captain host, and (b) a fleet with no host reporting `is_captain: true` at all
- [ ] No `fleet.captain` declared at all leaves today's behavior fully unchanged (no singleton mechanism exists yet, so this is mostly forward-looking, but the config parse itself must degrade gracefully on an absent key)
- [ ] The "optional later" lease/alert-on-down-captain item is explicitly out of scope for this issue's acceptance — do not implement it here; a follow-up issue can pick it up once the base mechanism ships

### Affected Files

- `.loom/config.json` schema / parsing (wherever the top-level config struct is defined in `loom-daemon/src/`) — add the `fleet.captain` key
- `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` — canonical config-knob table, new `fleet.captain` row citing the `shardCount`/`shardKey` tier precedent (§ near line 5315)
- `loom-daemon/src/telemetry/mod.rs` (`HostHealthRecord`, line 961) — add `is_captain` (+ armed-jobs list) field(s)
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/collector.rs` (`sample_host_health()`, lines 704-753) — populate the new field(s)
- New module or function near `loom-daemon/src/host_affinity.rs` / `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/mod.rs` (near `host_identity()`, line 807) — the captain-match/fail-closed-refusal logic itself
- `dashboard/src/redaction.ts` (line 125, `host.health` allowlist) — allow the new field(s) through to the public dashboard
- `dashboard/src/publicPage.ts` or `dashboard/web/src` views — render the two flag conditions (singleton on non-captain; no captain reporting)
- Whichever schedule-wrapper surface Loom ships for declared jobs (if one doesn't exist yet, this issue may need to introduce a minimal one — scope this explicitly during implementation rather than assuming a specific existing file)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a captain-match/no-match unit test mirroring `host_affinity.rs`'s `HostConstraint::matches` coverage — declared captain matches `host_identity()` (arms), does not match (refuses with the captain named), and no `fleet.captain` declared at all (behavior explicitly defined, not merely "whatever falls out")
- [ ] Automated tests: reuse the `RecordingDispatcher.current_host_id`-style injection pattern from `work_finder/tests.rs:216-224` (inject host identity as a test double rather than mutating process env) for any test touching the new captain-gate logic, to avoid the cross-test env races `host_identity_env_precedence` (`sweep_registry/mod.rs:1698`) already guards against with its RAII env guard
- [ ] Automated tests: `HostHealthRecord` serialization round-trips `is_captain` correctly and omits/defaults sanely when unset
- [ ] Manual verification: on a two-host test/staging setup, declare one as `fleet.captain`, confirm a declared singleton job arms there and refuses (with the captain named in the message) on the other
- [ ] Manual verification: dashboard correctly flags a synthetic "singleton armed on non-captain" and a synthetic "no captain reporting" state
- [ ] Edge cases: `fleet.captain` naming a host id that never reports `host.health` (typo, decommissioned host) — confirm this surfaces as "no captain reporting" rather than silently leaving every singleton unarmed with no signal

issues.title: forge_get_check_runs reads only the first 30 check-runs; merge-pr --auto's settle-wait cannot see the rest
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #8426 (#8410). Once that lands, `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait is the **only** check-settling mechanism: the server-side arm is gone.

## Observed

`forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh`, the `gh api "repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs"` call) passes no `per_page` and no `--paginate`, so GitHub's default page size of 30 applies:

```
$ gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/commits/c53dcaa85860fe090be88d6c1d374cd59e5439b5/check-runs --jq '"\(.total_count) \(.check_runs|length)"'
39 30
```

This repo's CI produces 39 check-runs per head, so 9 are invisible to the settle-wait, both to its pending count and to its failed-required classification.

## Suspected impact (unverified)

The rows appear to come back newest first, so the long-running test suites are probably visible and the missing rows are early structural gates. The forge's own ruleset should still refuse a synchronous merge whose required checks have not passed, unless the merging identity has a bypass. That needs checking. This is present on `main` today; #8426 makes it load-bearing.

## Suggested fix

Add `per_page=100` and/or paginate. Also fail closed (treat as pending) when `total_count` exceeds the number of rows returned, so a future growth past any page size cannot silently shrink the checked set. Pin it with a test fixture where `total_count > len(check_runs)`.

Measuring that the missing rows never include a required check, and closing this with that evidence, is a valid outcome.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Confirmed on `origin/main` @ current head: PR #8426 ("merge-pr --auto settles checks and re-validates in-process instead of arming a server-side merge") **merged 2026-09-25T14:34:02Z** — so the scenario this issue flags as "once that lands" is now live, not hypothetical: `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait (`_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge`, `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` ~line 2035) is the only check-settling mechanism today, and it relies entirely on `forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:652`), which still passes no `per_page`/`--paginate` to `gh api repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs` (line 690). Marking `loom:urgent` — this is a live gap in the mechanism this repo relies on to avoid merging PRs whose required checks have not actually passed (see CLAUDE.md § "CI is dumb and reliable, on purpose").

No duplicates found (`check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 8895`).

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `forge_get_check_runs` retrieves every check-run for a commit, not just the first page (add `per_page=100` and/or `--paginate` to the `gh api` call at `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:690`).
- [ ] When the fetched row count is less than `total_count`, the caller fails closed (treats settlement as not-yet-reached / still pending) rather than silently trusting a truncated set.
- [ ] A regression test fixture exercises `total_count > len(check_runs)` and confirms the fail-closed behavior (per the issue's own Suggested fix).
- [ ] Existing `test-forge-helpers.sh` / `test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` / `test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` suites stay green.
- [ ] Alternative closing condition (also acceptance-satisfying per the issue body): if investigation shows the missing rows can never include a required check (e.g. GitHub's check-runs endpoint is confirmed to always return required checks in the first page), document that finding with evidence and close without a code change.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` — `forge_get_check_runs` (GitHub branch, ~line 690): add pagination and/or a fail-closed total-count check.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-helpers.sh` — existing `forge_get_check_runs` coverage; extend or add a case for `total_count > len(check_runs)`.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` — exercises `forge_get_check_runs`'s distinguished exit codes; verify pagination changes don't disturb the 404/500/network-error paths.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` — exercises the settle-wait loop's trust of a `forge_get_check_runs` read; extend for the truncated-page case if the fail-closed behavior needs loop-level coverage.
- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — `_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge` (~line 2035), the sole caller now that #8426 removed the server-side arm; reference only unless the fail-closed check needs to live here instead of inside `forge_get_check_runs`.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: new fixture in `test-forge-helpers.sh` (or a new dedicated test file) pinning `total_count > len(check_runs)` → fail-closed/pending, per Acceptance Criteria.
- [ ] Automated tests: existing forge-helpers and merge-pr check-runs/settle-wait suites stay green.
- [ ] Manual verification: `gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/commits/<head>/check-runs --jq '"\(.total_count) \(.check_runs|length)"'` against a commit with >30 check-runs, before and after, confirming the fetch now returns the full set.
- [ ] Edge cases: a repo/commit with exactly 30, and with >100, check-runs (page-boundary and multi-page cases).

issues.title: merge: re-run stale required checks in place (grant fleet App Actions: write) so approved PRs stop losing loom:pr to re-date commits
issues.body:
## Problem

Approved PRs with green CI get stuck in a loop just before merging, and when several merge close together the loop may never end:

1. A PR is Judge-approved (`loom:pr`) and its CI is green.
2. Another PR merges, and `main` gets new commits (at least the post-merge version bump).
3. `merge-pr.sh`'s required-check freshness guard (#8248) refuses the merge, because the green checks started before the new base tip.
4. The fleet merge identity (`loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]`, a GitHub App) has no **Actions: write** permission, so it can't re-run the stale checks. As its fallback (#8508, `--redate-stale-checks`), it pushes a tree-identical no-op commit.
5. The head SHA moves, so the stale-verdict guard clears `loom:pr` and puts the PR back to `loom:review-requested`.
6. The PR waits for another Judge pass. Meanwhile something else merges, and the loop starts again at step 2.

Each lap costs a full CI run plus a Judge pass, and it resets whenever `main` moves.

## Evidence (2026-09-25)

- **PR #8909** was approved at `6f77b070`. The bot pushed the re-date commit `efb141c5` ("chore: re-date required checks for PR #8909 (#8248 guard, automated by #8508)"), and the stale-verdict guard then cleared `loom:pr`. The git tree is **identical** on both commits (`89d2e775fdb4abe54dbfe3111c6bcc77502d31c8`), so a review of the same code was thrown away.
- **PRs #8426 and #8471** each needed two separate Judge re-reviews that afternoon, both of which found no changes (a clean rebase, then another stale-check refusal), before they could merge. **#8906** is in the same queue.
- **An operator token with `repo` + `workflow` scope *can* re-run a job in place** (`POST /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`), keeping the head and the approval. So the missing piece is only the App's permission.

## Proposed fix

1. **Permission (human/admin action):** add **Actions: Read and write** to the `loom-fleet-dispatch` GitHub App, then accept the updated permission on each installation (rjwalters/loom first). GitHub has no API for changing an App's permissions; it has to be done in the App settings UI by the App owner.
2. **Code:** in `merge-pr.sh`'s freshness-guard path (`loom-daemon merge-pr redate-checks`), try re-running the stale required-check jobs **in place** first, then wait and retry the merge. Fall back to the tree-identical no-op push only if the re-run is refused (403, missing permission). The head never moves on the happy path, so `loom:pr` survives.
3. **Optional, separate decision:** when a push is tree-identical to the head that was approved (same git tree SHA), the stale-verdict guard could keep `loom:pr`. That removes the loop even for installs without Actions: write. It changes the "a verdict is about a specific tree" invariant only in the case where the tree really is the same, but it needs a deliberate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On an installation with Actions: write, a freshness-guard block on an approved PR is resolved by re-running the jobs in place: no new commit, the head SHA is unchanged, `loom:pr` is kept, and the merge completes on the next attempt once the re-run is green. Verified on a live PR.
- [ ] On an installation without Actions: write, the behaviour is unchanged: the existing #8508 tree-identical re-date plus one-push bound and escalation still applies. Covered by a test with the rerun endpoint returning 403.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md` and the GitHub App setup / authentication docs list Actions: write as a recommended App permission and explain why.

## Related

#8248 (freshness guard), #8508 (re-date fallback, closed), #5686 (fresh Judge after head move).

---

## Curator enhancement (2026-09-25)

### Scope split
| Item | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| 1. Grant `loom-fleet-dispatch` **Actions: Read and write** | **Operator step**, below. The code work does not wait for it: without the grant the new code falls back to today's #8508 behaviour. |
| 2. Re-run stale required jobs in place (code) | **This issue.** |
| 3. Keep `loom:pr` on a tree-identical push | **#8918** (`loom:operator-decision`). It changes a verdict invariant, so a human decides. |
| Comment finding: a busy `main` beats even in-place re-runs | Partly handled here (required-only re-runs, then an immediate merge). Input-aware staleness and a fast required-checks workflow move to **#8919**. |

### Operator step (human/admin, cannot be done from code)
1. GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → `loom-fleet-dispatch` → Permissions → Repository → **Actions: Read and write** → Save.
2. On each installation (rjwalters/loom first), accept the updated permission request.
3. Check: on the next freshness-guard block, the merge-pr output says `LOOM-RERUN-…` and no `chore: re-date required checks` commit appears.

### Platform fact the design depends on (verified 2026-09-25, twice)
GitHub runs **one re-run per workflow run at a time**. After one `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`, the run is `in_progress`. Any further job re-run in the same run returns `403 {"message":"The workflow run containing this job is already running"}`. I reproduced this on `ci.yml` run 36152790007, and the comment above (PR #8692) records the same result. Jobs that are not re-run are carried into the new attempt with their **original** `started_at`, so per-job re-runs cannot refresh several stale required checks. All 19 required contexts on `main` are in the single `ci.yml` run.

**Decision: re-run the whole workflow run** (`POST /actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun`, the same call as `gh run rerun <id>`), issuing one call per workflow run that holds a stale required check. The required jobs are fast and run in parallel, so they come back fresh in about a minute even though the full run takes about 8. The cost is a full CI cycle's compute. Moving the fast required checks into their own small workflow, so that re-running it is cheap, is a CI restructuring and is tracked in **#8919**.

### Implementation plan (Rust, `loom-daemon merge-pr redate-checks`; no new shell)
- New module `loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/rerun.rs` plus its tests. `redate::remedy` calls it **first**, after the existing head-moved check.
  - Read the live inputs: base tip, required contexts and the head's check runs. The check-run projection gains the job id, the app slug and the workflow run id (parsed from `details_url` `/actions/runs/<run>/job/<job>`). The base ref comes from the PR itself (`pulls/{n}` `.base.ref`), so no new CLI flag is needed and a new shell cannot break against an old binary.
  - List **every** stale required context (green, `started_at` < base tip), not just the first. If any stale context is not a GitHub Actions job, in-place re-run cannot produce complete evidence, so fall back to the push path.
  - Loop until a bounded deadline:
    - Re-read the inputs. If the head has moved, return `HeadMoved` (exit 3).
    - For each workflow run that holds a stale required job and has not yet been re-run by this call, `POST actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun`.
    - On `201`, that run is in flight.
    - On `403` with "already running", **wait**. This is not a missing permission, so never push.
    - On any other `403`, or a `404`, while **nothing has been re-run yet**, the result is `Refused`. Fall through to the existing #8508 tree-identical push, with its one-push-per-head bound and escalation unchanged.
    - On any other error, the result is `Failed` (exit 1, the refusal stands).
  - A re-run required job that concludes non-green is a failed re-run, and the refusal stands (exit 1). This is real red evidence, for example a tightened ratchet.
  - When every required context is fresh and none is pending, the result is **fresh**.
  - When the deadline passes first, the result is **pending**. The head is unchanged, `loom:pr` is kept, and the next pass continues.
- Exit contract (skew-safe in both directions):
  - `0`: pushed (unchanged), **or** re-ran in place and still pending, **or** fresh without the proceed opt-in. `merge-pr.sh` maps this to exit 4 (re-queue), which is what champion-pr-merge.md already expects.
  - `5` (new): re-ran in place and now fresh. Returned **only** when the caller sets `LOOM_REDATE_ALLOW_PROCEED=1`. This is an environment variable rather than a flag, so an old binary ignores it and still pushes. On exit 5 the new `merge-pr.sh` returns 0 from the freshness guard and merges straight away, which shortens the race described in the comment.
  - `1`/`3`/`4`: unchanged.
- Wait budget: `--rerun-wait-secs` (env `LOOM_REDATE_RERUN_WAIT_SECS`, default 600), polling about every 10 s.
- `merge-pr.sh`: an edit within the existing line of the one-line `_check_required_check_freshness`. It sets the env opt-in, handles `rd==5`, and fixes the exit-4 wording, which currently always claims a fresh Judge review is needed. **No line-count growth**: the file is frozen by the ratchet.
- Docs: `defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md` (the exit-4 row and the #8508 section) and the GitHub App setup/auth docs, which should list Actions: write as a recommended permission and say why. Also update the `redate.rs` and `cli/merge_pr_redate.rs` headers.

- [ ] Unit tests with a stub `gh` cover these cases:
  - The workflow runs holding stale required jobs are re-run in place (one call per run) and nothing is pushed.
  - A 403 for a missing permission falls back to the #8508 push, with its bound and escalation unchanged.
  - A 403 for "already running" waits and does not push.
  - A red re-run is `Failed`.
  - A head move is `HeadMoved`.
  - A passed deadline is `Pending`.
  - Fresh returns exit 5 only with the opt-in.
- [ ] A stale required check that is not a GitHub Actions job goes straight to the push fallback.
- [ ] Existing `redate` and `stale_checks` tests pass unchanged, apart from the mechanical update to the `CheckRun` constructor.
- [ ] The `merge-pr.sh` line count is unchanged, and the shell suites covering `--redate-stale-checks` pass.
- [ ] The docs list Actions: write as a recommended App permission.
- [ ] Live verification of AC1 (a freshness block resolved by an in-place re-run on a real PR) happens once the operator grants the permission. It can be checked with an operator token in the meantime.

issues.title: Observability: Pipeline stage dwell time, queue turnaround latency, and dispatch starvation metrics
issues.body:
## Problem

Operators cannot easily determine whether Loom workers are starved for work, blocked on upstream stages, or idling between orchestrator ticks. While raw role durations exist in SigNoz, end-to-end pipeline velocity and queue wait times are unmeasured.

## Proposal

Add telemetry and metrics for pipeline throughput and feeder velocity:

1. **Worker Turnaround / Idle Gap:** Measure latency between a worker finishing a sweep/role and the next sweep being dispatched/started.
2. **Stage Dwell Time Distribution:** Track duration spent in each stage across the lifecycle:
   - `Issue Created` → `loom:curated`
   - `loom:curated` → `loom:issue` (Approval latency)
   - `loom:issue` → `loom:building` (Queue dispatch latency)
   - `loom:building` → `loom:review-requested` (Build duration)
   - `loom:review-requested` → `loom:pr` / Merged (Judge & merge queue latency)
3. **Dispatch Admission & Starvation Signals:** Export counters/spans when a sweep attempt exits prematurely due to worktree locks, lease collisions, or no eligible work found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Stage dwell time metrics exported to OTLP / SigNoz.
- [ ] Worker idle-between-jobs time tracked per host.
- [ ] Admission failure reasons (lock contention, lease conflict, empty queue) visible in telemetry.

issues.title: dashboard: show a sweep's live Spot compute jobs as nested subprocesses
issues.body:
## Goal
On dashboard.2amlogic.com, show each active sweep's live Spot batch jobs (SPICE grids submitted by `klt sim --backend batch`) **nested under that sweep** as subprocesses, instead of only in the separate "running compute" list (#8305). The operator asked for this on 2026-09-24, after ruling that the AWS workers send SPICE to Spot (2AMLogic/2am#1004). Once that ruling is live, a worker's sweeps spend most of their SPICE time off-host, and the dashboard should show which sweep is paying for which instance.

## Today
- The `ephemeral_compute` launch record is emitted from the **submitting host**, by 2am's `batch-fleet-provision.sh launch`, which inherits the environment of klt, and klt inherits the sweep's.
- D1 already indexes `sweep_id` on any record kind (`telemetry.ts` `extractRecordFields`), but nothing sends one.
- The link breaks at three points:
  1. The daemon sets no `LOOM_SWEEP_ID` on the sweep child. Only `LOOM_TERMINAL_ID=daemon-<id>` carries the id (`sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs`).
  2. 2am's `report_record` drops string extras other than `instance_id` and `instance_type`.
  3. The Durable Object's `ActiveComputeState` and the web `ActiveComputeJob`/`parseActiveComputeJob` whitelist fields, and `sweepId` isn't among them.

## Plan
1. **Daemon:** `cmd.env("LOOM_SWEEP_ID", sweep_id)` on the sweep child.
2. **2am** (`batch-fleet-provision.sh`): stamp `sweep_id` on both launch-record emissions. Read it from `$LOOM_SWEEP_ID`, falling back to a `$LOOM_TERMINAL_ID` of the form `daemon-<id>` for daemons that predate step 1. Allow it as a string extra restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.
3. **Backend** (`fleetState.ts`): carry `sweepId` on `ActiveComputeState`.
4. **Web:** add `sweepId` to `ActiveComputeJob`; `buildFleetView` joins jobs to sweeps **by `sweepId` alone**. The compute entry's `hostId` is the submitter's ingest identity, and it doesn't always match the sweep's host.
   - Render a nested "subprocesses" list under the sweep in the fleet overview card and in the host-detail sweep row: instance type, Spot, elapsed time, and the leaked flag.
   - Jobs with no matching live sweep stay in the "running compute" section, so an orphaned instance is never hidden.

## Redaction
No change to what's public. `ephemeral_compute`'s public allowlist stays `["kind"]`, and `activeCompute` stays empty for unauthenticated viewers, so the nesting only renders for Access-authenticated viewers.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A sweep that submits a batch job shows it nested under the sweep, both on the fleet card and in host detail, while the job is live.
- [ ] The job disappears from under the sweep when its completion record retires it.
- [ ] A job whose sweep isn't in `activeSweeps` still appears in "running compute", and a leaked job is still flagged.
- [ ] The public snapshot is unchanged.

issues.title: ci-telemetry: a never-completing workflow run pins a repo's watermark indefinitely
issues.body:
Split out of #8898 (the "smaller gaps noted in the same review" list). #8898's PR
fixed the re-run gap only and deliberately left this one alone — confirmed still
present on that branch.

## Problem

`poll_repo` (`loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/poll.rs`) advances a repo's watermark
to `oldest_incomplete.unwrap_or(newest).max(watermark)`. A run that never reaches
a completed state (cancelled-but-stuck, a workflow abandoned mid-flight, a
`queued` run whose runner never arrives) is `hold()`-ed every cycle, so
`oldest_incomplete` stays at that run's `created_at` and the watermark never moves
past it — forever.

#8898's `.max(watermark)` clamp does **not** fix this: the clamp only stops the
watermark moving *backwards*. When the watermark is already older than
`oldest_incomplete`, `max` picks `oldest_incomplete`, which is the pinned value.

Consequence: the repo's listing floor (`runs_floor` = the older of the watermark
and the trailing 24h rescan window) is the pinned watermark once it is more than
24 hours old, so every cycle re-lists a window that grows without bound — one
extra runs page per 100 runs, per repo, per `intervalSecs`, indefinitely. It also
makes `ci-telemetry status`'s per-repo watermark misleading as a freshness signal.

## Suggested fix

Bound the hold: stop holding for an incomplete run once it is older than some
age (the rescan window is the natural bound, since anything inside the window is
re-listed regardless of the watermark), and/or treat a run that has been
incomplete across N cycles as abandoned. Either way, the run stays visible for as
long as the rescan window covers it, and the watermark is free to advance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run that never completes does not hold a repo's watermark past some
      bounded age; the watermark advances to the newest completed run.
- [ ] A run that is merely slow (completes within the bound) is still held and
      still exported exactly once — `an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes`
      keeps passing.
- [ ] A fixture test pins the behaviour: an in-progress run older than the bound,
      several cycles, and the watermark is past it while the run is still exported
      if it completes inside the rescan window.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` — the watermark/in-progress paragraph
      (~line 225) and the "Re-runs" bullet describe the new bound.

## Not in scope

The other three gaps from the same review, each worth its own issue if it
matters: a renamed repo re-emits its runs; the runs list is not ETag-cached; a
crash between export and ledger write can emit duplicate histogram points.

---

## Curator Enhancement

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/poll.rs` - bound `hold()`/`oldest_incomplete` by age (or cycle count) so a never-completing run stops pinning the watermark past the rescan-window bound; likely changes `hold`'s signature to take `ctx.now`/`ctx.rescan_window` (or `ctx.initial_lookback`) so it can decide whether to hold at all.
- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs` - add a fixture test for the bounded-hold behavior alongside the existing `an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes` (line 583).
- `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` - the "Runs that are still in progress are not recorded yet" paragraph (currently ~line 304-307) and the "Re-runs" bullet (currently ~line 409-420) both describe the watermark hold as unbounded today; both need updating. (Line numbers as of 2026-09-27 — re-verify before editing.)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: new fixture test in `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/tests.rs` — an in-progress run older than the bound, several cycles, watermark advances past it; a separate case confirms a run that completes within the bound is still held and still exported exactly once (`an_in_progress_run_holds_the_watermark_and_is_emitted_once_it_completes` must keep passing unmodified or be extended consistently with the new bound).
- [ ] Manual verification: `cargo test -p loom-daemon ci_telemetry::` passes locally.
- [ ] Edge cases: a run exactly at the bound boundary; multiple never-completing runs at different ages in the same cycle.
