issues.title: Investigate and reduce PR latency: the review queue is 4h deep, but approved-awaiting-merge is 68h and changes-requested is 90h
issues.body:
## Problem

PR time-to-merge is strongly bimodal, and the slow mode is not where it is commonly assumed to be.

**Merged-PR sample** (last 40, 2026-09-23 22:18Z → 2026-09-25 16:11Z, ~0.96 PRs/hour into `main`):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Median merge latency | 0.69h (41 min) |
| p90 | 16.4h |
| Max | 32.0h |
| PRs force-pushed at least once | 8/40 |
| `loom:merge-conflict` applied | 0 |
| `loom:changes-requested` / `loom:ci-failure` events | 9 / 5 |

That sample suffers survivorship bias — the genuinely stuck PRs have not merged, so they are absent from it. **The open-PR queue is where the latency actually lives** (ages as of 2026-09-25 ~16:40Z):

| Queue | Count | Median age | Oldest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loom:review-requested` | 4 | **3.9h** | 22.3h (#8823) |
| `loom:pr` (approved, awaiting merge) | 5 | **68.5h** | 91.2h (#8531) |
| `loom:changes-requested` | 10 | **89.6h** | 183.1h (#8131) |
| held/other | 1 | 105.0h | #8486 |

So: **Judge throughput is not the bottleneck.** The review queue is four PRs deep with a median age under four hours. Two other queues are.

### Queue A — approved but unmerged (median 68.5h)

Four of the five `loom:pr` PRs carry an operator gate: #8531 (`loom:operator`), #8613 (`loom:operator`), #8680 (`loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator-decision`), #8893 (`loom:operator`). Only #8695 is a plain `loom:pr`. `WORK_PLAN.md` already names this as "Operator Attention: Merge-Risk-Hold Pileup" — implementation is finished and only a human merge decision is missing. These PRs age while fully built.

### Queue B — changes-requested that never come back (median 89.6h)

Ten PRs, and the oldest four are all also `loom:blocked`, mostly with a companion failure label: #8131 (`loom:merge-conflict`, 183h), #8314 (`loom:ci-failure`, 155h), #8351 (`loom:ci-failure`, 147h), #8440 (114h). Doctor is not clearing these, and `loom:blocked` means nothing re-queues them on its own. rjwalters/repo#192 (cited in `daemon-reference.md`) documents the adjacent stall mode: a verdict label with nothing to re-queue it.

## Proposal

This is a **research + improvement** task. Measure first, then act; do not assume a mechanism.

**Phase 1 — measure.** Decompose time-to-merge into its real segments rather than PR-open→merge:

- `loom:review-requested` → first Judge verdict (queue wait)
- verdict → `loom:pr` (approval path)
- `loom:pr` → merged, **split by whether an operator gate label is present** (this is the suspected dominant term)
- `loom:changes-requested` → next Doctor push, and the fraction that never get one
- count of verdict invalidations via `reconcile_pr_verdicts` (a re-review is a full extra lap)

Ideally this lands as a queryable artifact rather than a one-off script — PR #8692 (`loom:pr`) already commits cycle-time question/rollup/extract SQL for the shipped-work side, and this is the natural companion question set for the *unshipped* side.

**Phase 2 — mediate.** Candidate levers, to be chosen by what Phase 1 shows, not now:

- Surface queue ages where the operator sees them (`loom-daemon queue` landed in #8906 for the *issue* ready-queue; the PR queues have no equivalent view).
- Alert when a `loom:pr` PR exceeds an age threshold under an operator gate — the hold is legitimate, the silence is not.
- Give `loom:changes-requested` + `loom:blocked` PRs an explicit aging/escalation path so they cannot sit for 183h with no owner.
- Decide whether some operator-gate classes can be narrowed so fewer finished PRs need a human.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-segment latency is measurable on demand, not by hand-written one-off queries.
- [ ] The `loom:pr` → merged segment is reported split by operator-gate presence.
- [ ] The count and age of `loom:changes-requested` PRs with no subsequent Doctor push is reported.
- [ ] At least one mediation is implemented, chosen by the Phase-1 numbers, with the reasoning recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Verdict invalidations (stale-SHA re-reviews) are counted, so re-review cost is visible.

## Notes

Filed from a triage pass over PR/queue state, not a Builder run. All figures above are reproducible from `gh pr list` / the issue timeline API at the stated timestamps and will drift; re-measure before acting on any single number.

Related: the companion issues on telemetry record-kind registration contention and on the missing `loom:merge-conflict` signal for `loom:review-requested` PRs — both describe ways a PR makes an extra, avoidable lap through these queues.

issues.title: forge-helpers: forge_get_required_status_check_contexts still fails closed on the plan-gated 403 (follow-up to #8844)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #8844 / PR #8871.

#8871 taught `loom-daemon merge-pr stale-checks` to read the one plan-gated
403 —

    HTTP 403: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.

— as "this repository's plan has no rulesets/branch protection, so nothing can
be a *required* check", instead of failing the #8248 freshness guard closed on
every merge.

The **shell twin of that lookup was deliberately left alone**:
`forge_get_required_status_check_contexts` in
`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` still treats the same 403 as a lookup
failure (`ruleset_rc=1` → `return 1`).

### Why it was out of scope for #8844

Its three call sites in `merge-pr.sh` (the UNSTABLE fallback, the
no-required-checks fallback, and the stacked/auto path around lines 1998 /
2314 / 2532) only run when checks are **already failing or the PR is not in a
clean mergeable state**. So on a private free-plan repo it does not block an
otherwise-clean merge the way the freshness guard did — it refuses a merge
that something else was already refusing. The #8844 report's actual symptom is
fixed without it.

### Why it is still worth fixing

On such a repo *no* check can be required, so "one informational check is red"
is precisely the case the UNSTABLE fallback exists to unblock — and there it
fails closed for a reason that cannot be true. The operator sees a refusal
whose stated cause ("could not determine the required checks") is unanswerable
on that plan.

### Shape of the work

- Mirror `stale_checks::fetch::is_plan_gated`'s predicate: match the **message**
  (`upgrade to github` **and** `make this repository public`), never the status
  code — a missing token scope, SSO enforcement and a rate-limit refusal are all
  403s where required checks may genuinely exist.
- The lookup currently discards stderr (`2>/dev/null`) on both the ruleset and
  the GraphQL call, so the signature is not even visible to it; capturing it
  needs care because `defaults/scripts/lib/` is `contract` in
  `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`, i.e. inside the portable-shell pool
  `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` ratchets (comments are free, code lines are
  not).
- Per-source, like #8871: a gated source configures nothing; a source that
  answered normally stays authoritative.
- Emit a visible warning on the same principle — a relaxation nobody can see is
  how a fail-open ships unnoticed.
- Extend `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-unstable-fallback.sh` (it already
  stubs `gh api repos/*/rules/branches/*`) with the plan-gated 403 → "no required
  checks" case and an other-403 → still-fail-closed case.

### Alternative worth weighing first

#8191 is porting `merge-pr.sh` to daemon subcommands. If the required-contexts
lookup is due to move to Rust soon, the right move may be to reuse
`stale_checks::fetch`'s union (now plan-gate-aware) from that port rather than
grow the shell helper — one implementation instead of two that must agree.

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: warn when a partial-increment trailer is backticked (the #3667 reset silently no-ops)
issues.body:
## Summary

`merge-pr.sh`'s partial-increment parser deliberately blanks inline code spans
before matching (#5234 — a backticked `Part of #N` is a hypothetical mention, not
a declared intent). That exclusion is correct. The gap it leaves is that a Builder
can write the convention's **exact** trailer text inside a code span — it reads as
"a literal piece of syntax, so put it in backticks" — and the PR then looks
completely right to a human reviewer and to Judge while silently defeating the
automation: `_partial_increment_refs` returns nothing, so the #3667
`loom:building` -> `loom:issue` reset no-ops with **no log line anywhere** and the
family/epic issue is stranded at `loom:building` indefinitely.

## Incident

Downstream on `rjwalters/kicad-tools`: merging PR #5686 into issue #5240, whose
body carried `` `Part of #5240` `` on its own line. The reset never fired; the
label swap and an explanatory comment had to be applied by hand. Filed there as
rjwalters/kicad-tools#5690; fixed there in PR #5692 (merged 2026-09-23) against
the **vendored** `.loom/` copies, pinned with a `.loom/resync-ignore` block whose
own comment says "unpin once the equivalent fix lands in rjwalters/loom's
defaults/ tree". Tracked there as rjwalters/kicad-tools#5693.

Two prior partial-increment merges on that same issue (#5649, #5488) used the
plain-text form and reset correctly — this is a body-shape trap, not a regression.

## Fix (detection, not a parser change)

Port the downstream fix into `defaults/`, so every consumer gets it and the pin
can be retired:

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — a non-blocking pre-merge warning
  (`_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` plus two text helpers), in the
  same advisory style as the #4569/#4595 conflict warnings, called from
  `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` **before** its empty-refs early
  return (the case it exists for is precisely the one where the ref list is
  empty). Pure text analysis, no extra forge calls.
- The matched shape is deliberately much narrower than the declaration anchor:
  the backticked trailer must be the **entire line** (modulo an optional
  list/blockquote marker, whitespace and one trailing punctuation mark), so the
  #5234 mid-sentence mention and a docs line listing trailers as examples stay
  silent, and fenced blocks are stripped first.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` — regression cases
  for the incident shape, the plain-text control, the #5234 prose control, docs
  prose, fenced blocks, the both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, and the
  `--dry-run` prefix.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` — a "write the trailer as plain
  text, never backticked" caution next to the existing trailer example.

The `loom-daemon merge-pr-refs` parser is **not** touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_partial_increment_refs`' answer for a backticked trailer is unchanged
      (still not a declaration)
- [ ] A whole-line backticked trailer emits a non-blocking warning naming the
      issue and quoting the offending line, and mutates nothing
- [ ] Plain-text trailers, mid-sentence backticked mentions, docs example lines
      and fenced blocks do not warn
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` passes

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` - add `_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` (plus its two text helpers), called from `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` before the `[[ -n "$partial_refs" ]] || return 0` early return (~line 1303)
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` - add regression cases: incident shape, plain-text control, #5234 prose control, docs prose, fenced blocks, both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, `--dry-run` prefix
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` - add a "write the trailer as plain text, never backticked" caution next to the existing `Part of #N` trailer example (~line 646)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` covers all cases listed in the Fix section and passes
- [ ] Manual verification: construct a PR body whose only partial-increment trailer is a whole-line backticked `` `Part of #N` `` and confirm `merge-pr.sh` (or its `--dry-run` path) prints the new non-blocking warning naming the issue and quoting the offending line, while `_partial_increment_refs` still returns nothing for it (AC #1 unchanged)

issues.title: feat(config): consolidate all Loom operational hyperparameters into a unified, structured config file
issues.body:
### Problem Statement
Currently, operational hyperparameters governing Loom's execution, scheduling, thresholds, and worker dynamics are scattered across codebase constants, CLI flags, role definitions, and disparate configuration fragments (e.g. comparator priority weights, timeout bounds, retry ceilings, token budgets, merge-train batch sizes, and backoff multipliers).

This dispersion creates two major bottlenecks:
1. **Lack of Run Provenance:** It is difficult to record and audit the exact point-in-time hyperparameter configuration under which a particular fleet run, sweep, or benchmark was executed.
2. **Barrier to Automated Tuning:** Systematic hyperparameter optimization (e.g., CMA-ES / Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy, Bayesian optimization, or automated sweep search) cannot easily tune, sample, or mutate parameters against fleet cycle time and token-efficiency metrics.

### Proposed Solution
Create a centralized, typed, and structured hyperparameter configuration schema (e.g. `hyperparameters.yml` or a structured `hyperparameters` block within Loom fleet config) consolidating all operational tunables into one place.

#### 1. Consolidated Hyperparameter Scope
- **Dispatch & Scheduling:**
  - Candidate comparator scoring weights (tier weight, repo priority multiplier, age decay factor, dependency depth weight).
  - Tick intervals, idle turnaround duration, and per-host concurrency limits.
- **Timeouts & Lifecycle Limits:**
  - Sweep timeouts, skipped-load admission brake duration, worker lease TTL, and shell budget execution bounds.
- **Rework & Review Bounds:**
  - Max rework / retry attempt ceilings, re-review backoff multipliers, and stale base-branch staleness window.
- **Merge Trains & Batching:**
  - Merge-train batch sizes, speculative merge queue timeouts, and path-filter invalidation thresholds.
- **Model / Role Execution Budgets:**
  - Token budget caps, temperature settings, and max generation tokens per role (`curator`, `builder`, `judge`, `doctor`).

#### 2. Optimization & Provenance Features
- **Snapshot / Span Stamping:** Stamp the active hyperparameter config hash (or vector) onto `loom.story` and `loom.dispatch` OTLP telemetry spans for run-level provenance.
- **Tuning Interface:** Ensure the config can be programmatically injected/overridden via CLI flags or parameter vector files to support external optimizer loops (like CMA-ES).
- **Validation & Defaults:** Comprehensive schema validation (types, range bounds) with well-documented baseline defaults.

### Acceptance Criteria

issues.title: Prefer human-directed PRs throughout landing with a disableable planning policy
issues.body:
## Problem

Human-directed PRs should reach landing promptly while autonomous fleet work continues. Today an explicit `loom:operator-priority` star accelerates work, but ordinary PR scheduling does not distinguish an interactive human-driven session from autonomous execution; unlabeled PRs can wait behind the entire labeled review queue.

This issue records the operator's agreed design and request to implement it.

## Agreed behavior

**A human-directed PR gets the next available opportunity to move toward landing, at every stage.** An agent producing a PR in an interactive session counts as human-directed because a human drove that session. AI authorship is irrelevant.

Record work origin explicitly:

| Origin | Meaning | Default planning preference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interactive` | A human drove the working session, including an agent used interactively | Goes first |
| `autonomous` | The fleet independently executed the work | Ordinary queue |
| `unknown` | Origin was not reliably recorded | Ordinary queue; an operator can star it |

Origin is set at work/session creation and carried onto the PR. It persists through Doctor fixes, re-review, and merging; a later autonomous worker does not rewrite an interactive PR's origin. Approving a backlog issue for autonomous execution does not make its resulting PR interactive. Do not infer origin from GitHub usernames, bot flags, AI coauthor trailers, branch names, or the absence of a fleet marker.

Keep three separate concepts: origin (historical fact), planning preference (configurable policy), and the operator star (explicit stronger override).

### Scheduling contract

- Prefer interactive PRs at review, fixes, re-review, and merge, not merely the first review.
- Preserve existing explicit operator priority and applicable verified-red-main recovery precedence; interactive work precedes ordinary autonomous/unknown work.
- Finish work already running. Do not interrupt agents, cancel CI, or consume the operator star's overflow slot merely for being interactive.
- Prefer only work eligible for the next action. Drafts, holds, live claims, CI/dependency waits and required human responses continue to use existing gates. Fleet work proceeds while a preferred PR cannot advance.
- Preserve existing relative ordering inside each class. The preference must affect actual work selection, not only a displayed queue.
- Review/merge standards and eligibility for automated landing are independent of priority. Human origin grants no approval or permission to modify an arbitrary contributor branch.
- Discover eligible interactive PRs without relying on the labeled fleet queue first becoming empty. Reuse the existing admission/ownership rules rather than silently enrolling arbitrary unlabeled PRs for auto-merge.
- Start with non-preemptive preference. New quota systems, aging/burst tuning, extra concurrency, fleet-wide pauses, and human-first issue/build scheduling are out of scope.

### Configuration

Add the planning setting `planning.preferHumanPrs`, default `true`. Setting it to `false` restores the ordinary PR ordering/admission behavior and retains origin metadata. Explicit operator stars continue to work. Use the normal effective configuration layers so fleet defaults and repository overrides work consistently.

## Implementation direction (to verify during Curator)

- Reuse Loom's provenance/PR creation and session/sweep launch surfaces for origin capture and propagation. Old records remain readable and classify as `unknown` unless explicit reliable origin exists.
- Introduce one shared origin parser and PR ordering policy, used by the actual Judge/Doctor/Champion selection paths and any rendered explanation; avoid three independent prompt heuristics.
- Use trustworthy source metadata; malformed, conflicting, missing, or untrusted origin declarations must not earn automatic priority.
- Update documentation with the definition, handoff persistence, scope, ordering, config disable behavior, and how manual/interactive callers record origin.

Relevant current seams: `loom-daemon/src/provenance/`, `defaults/scripts/create-pr.sh`, daemon sweep/role launch, `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/`, `defaults/roles/{judge,doctor,champion}.md`, their canonical command sources, and the existing operator-priority ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interactive agent sessions can explicitly record `interactive`; autonomous launch paths reliably record `autonomous`; unrecorded work remains `unknown`.
- [ ] PR origin round-trips and survives autonomous repair/re-review without being overwritten.
- [ ] One consistent ordering selects an eligible interactive PR before ordinary fleet PRs through review, repair and merge, preserving stronger explicit priority and stable class order.
- [ ] Turning `planning.preferHumanPrs` off restores baseline behavior without deleting origin or changing stars.
- [ ] A full fleet queue does not hide an eligible interactive PR; existing admission/authorization boundaries remain intact.
- [ ] Holds, drafts, active claims, failing/pending checks and dependencies cannot be bypassed by origin; waiting human work does not idle other actionable work.
- [ ] Missing, invalid, conflicting and untrusted origin records receive no implicit preference; author identity alone never implies human-directed work.
- [ ] Tests exercise actual creation/launch/selection integration as well as policy, including the same PR passing from interactive creation to autonomous Doctor and back to Judge.
- [ ] User documentation explains all three concepts and the enabled-by-default disable switch; prompt changes are pressure-tested against a resisting queue scenario and audited for rule conflicts.

## Authorization

The operator explicitly requested: document this discussion in an issue, then implement it. Run Curator → Builder → Judge → Doctor if needed → Merge under the repository workflow.

## Curator implementation findings

Curated per the operator's explicit request against checkout `d6dd1941b`. Premise gate: out of scope (exit 0). Duplicate/related-work scan: no duplicates found (exit 0); no sibling micro-issues or open numbered dependencies identified. Keep this as one cohesive policy change: origin capture without actual role selection would not fulfill the request.

- **PR selection is not the work-finder issue queue.** Judge and Doctor select PRs through their role instructions; Champion drains `loom:pr` through `champion-pr-merge.md`. Sorting `work_finder::candidate_cmp` or its dashboard projection alone would not change those choices and would expand scope into issue/build scheduling.
- **Implement a shared executable queue policy.** A Rust module plus a `loom-daemon` CLI port can expose ordered PR candidates and origin/reason to every role. Use the existing executable-extension surface (`src/cli/script_ports.rs`) rather than growing the frozen `main.rs`. Keep normal role-specific actionable-work checks at claim/action time and continue past skipped rows. Preserve existing queue order as the stable tie-breaker within each preference class, including Doctor's conflict/changes-requested baseline and Champion's oldest-first merge order.
- **Unlabeled discovery has two independent gates.** `role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs::forge_queue_probe` only sees the configured label queues; Judge's fallback additionally runs only when the labeled queue is empty. With the preference enabled, a trusted explicit interactive PR eligible for fallback review must be discoverable alongside labeled PRs and must open the Judge role-runner gate when it is the only pending work. With the preference disabled, preserve the current admission behavior. Continue to run `judge-fallback-guard.sh` for bot exclusion, lifetime cap, and SHA dedup; fallback review does not add workflow labels or authorize automated landing.
- **Trust is separate from origin.** Use `comment_trust::TrustPolicy` on a forge response carrying `user`/author association (a pull-list response has these). `forge_listing::RestIssue` currently loses association/type, so its author login alone is insufficient. A trusted bot can carry explicit interactive origin; a human username without a valid declaration remains unknown. Reject duplicate/conflicting origin declarations rather than choosing whichever appears first.
- **Provenance is a compatible persistence seam.** `provenance/marker.rs` has a v1 parser accepting unknown fields and one existing optional field (`installs`). An optional typed `origin` field can preserve old markers as unknown without inventing a second body-parser convention. `create-pr.sh` already adds exactly one provenance marker, preserves an existing marker, and adopts an existing PR before creation. Explicit interactive context must reach this path; repair/adoption must retain the PR's existing origin rather than restamping it from the current Doctor process.
- **Autonomous launchers must pin their context.** `sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs` and `role_runner/launch.rs` assemble child environments; explicitly stamp autonomous work there so an interactive value inherited by a long-running daemon cannot promote every future fleet PR. Use an explicit documented interactive session/creation argument or environment entry point; absence of an autonomous marker is never evidence of interactivity.
- **Use the effective config resolver.** `config_resolver::resolve_effective_config` supplies shared/private defaults, legacy repository config, project config and local overrides. Resolve `planning.preferHumanPrs` from that output with a true default; do not add a second direct `.loom/config.json` reader.
- **Preserve role-specific safety semantics.** Doctor deliberately allows `loom:operator` on changes-requested PRs for the existing stale-diff refresh route (#7660), while merge remains held. Pending/failing checks may block merge while still yielding actionable Doctor work. The preference must neither blanket-filter away these valid repair paths nor relax their existing authorization/claim checks.

Related implementation precedents: #9244 (operator priority), #9027 (provenance), #9391/#9392 (role-runner queue gate/demand), #5455 (fallback review guard), #7660 (Doctor hold semantics).

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/provenance/marker.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/cli/provenance.rs` — explicit typed origin capture, compatibility and round-trip handling.
- `defaults/scripts/create-pr.sh` — pass explicit creation context into provenance while preserving adoption and existing-marker behavior.
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/spawn_process.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/launch.rs` — autonomous child context, tested under inherited interactive environment.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/concurrent_dispatch.rs` — Judge admission for eligible interactive fallback work; preserve disabled behavior.
- A focused new Rust PR-planning module and `loom-daemon/src/cli/script_ports.rs` — shared trust-aware origin classification, effective configuration and stable ordered candidate output; reuse `comment_trust.rs` and forge listing/cache utilities.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/{judge,doctor,champion}.md`, `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` and corresponding `defaults/roles/` sources/copies — actual queue selection and fallback integration. Regenerate managed agent skills with the existing generator; do not hand-edit generated `SKILL.md` files.
- `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` or a focused linked planning document, plus relevant provenance/session documentation — definitions, configuration, creation entry point, persistence and admission distinction.
- Rust unit/integration tests and `tests/test-create-pr.sh` (existing creation harness, if applicable) — creation, launch, selection, disabled baseline and handoff regressions.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Policy fixtures cover explicit stars, existing red-main priority where applicable, trusted interactive, autonomous and unknown PRs; stable order is retained within each class and disabled policy reproduces each role's baseline order.
- [ ] Parser/trust fixtures cover old markers, malformed/duplicate/conflicting records, absent author metadata, untrusted declarations, trusted bots declaring interactive, and trusted humans with no declaration.
- [ ] Launch tests begin with an inherited interactive environment and demonstrate that autonomous role/sweep children receive autonomous context; direct interactive creation emits interactive origin.
- [ ] Creation/adoption/repair integration carries the same interactive PR through an autonomous Doctor handoff and re-review with unchanged origin. Existing provenance and old PR bodies remain readable.
- [ ] Actual Judge/Doctor/Champion selection entry points consume the shared ordered candidates, including enough fleet work to keep the ordinary queue nonempty. An interactive-only fallback case opens the Judge launch gate when enabled and preserves the old closed-gate behavior when disabled.
- [ ] Guard fixtures exercise held, draft, claimed and non-actionable preferred work followed by actionable fleet work; no extra agent slot, CI cancellation, fallback workflow enrollment, or origin-based merge permission occurs. Include Doctor's authorized held stale-diff repair case.
- [ ] Configuration tests cover default true, explicit false, shared-default false with repository true override, and retention of origin metadata and operator-star behavior after disabling.
- [ ] Run focused Rust/creation tests, prompt synchronization and documentation checks. Pressure-test changed role prompts with a full fleet queue, one eligible interactive PR and one blocked interactive PR; verify the shared queue is used and existing action gates remain authoritative.

issues.title: Route Claude Code's contained dispatch through the credential egress proxy (follow-up to #8674)
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8674 (credential egress proxy, epic #6896). The first increment shipped the
proxy mechanism (`loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/`) and wired it into the
**native-harness** contained dispatch (`worker_spawn::run` -> `containment::docker_command`).
**Claude Code's own per-sweep container is not routed through it yet.**

Claude's container is built by `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` (the `#7429`/`#7430`
re-exec-into-`docker run` path), which resolves and forwards the Claude credential itself and
never calls into `loom-daemon`'s dispatch code. So a contained Claude sweep still puts a real
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (or a pooled key) inside the container's environment, readable by
`env` / `/proc/self/environ` — exactly the exposure #8674 exists to close.

This is #8674's acceptance criterion 5, first half.

## Scope

- Give the Claude container a per-launch placeholder for its credential variable and point
  `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the host-side proxy, reusing the existing
  `egress_proxy::{Placeholder, Registry, Record, server}` types rather than a second
  implementation.
- Decide where the listener is owned: `spawn-claude.sh` is a shell adapter with no place to
  host a Rust listener, so the likely shape is a `loom-daemon` subcommand the adapter shells
  out to (the repo's language policy already says new executable logic is a daemon
  subcommand, not new shell).
- Answer #8674's own open question against the current Claude Code release: whether an OAuth
  bearer (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) needs anything beyond `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`-style
  `Authorization: Bearer` substitution — refresh behaviour, additional headers, a
  non-`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`-honouring code path.
- Keep the switch separate and default-off, as the native path does
  (`runtimes.containment.credentialProxy` / `LOOM_NATIVE_CREDENTIAL_PROXY`), and keep the
  fail-closed rule: never silently fall back to forwarding the real credential.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With containment + credential substitution enabled, a contained Claude sweep's container
      environment holds only a per-launch placeholder; the real credential is absent from the
      container's environment, filesystem and `/proc/*/environ`.
- [ ] Claude Code reaches the provider through the proxy and completes a normal sweep.
- [ ] The placeholder is invalidated when the launch ends (same registry semantics as the
      native path).
- [ ] Uncontained Claude dispatch, and contained Claude dispatch with the flag off, are
      unchanged.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/runtime-adapters.md` §Session containers drops the "Claude's own
      container is not routed through the proxy yet" caveat the first increment added.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8674 / its implementing PR #8701: must merge first — it introduces the
      `egress_proxy::{Placeholder, Registry, Record, server}` types and the native-harness
      wiring this issue's Claude-container routing reuses rather than reimplementing.

This issue cannot proceed until #8674 (or PR #8701) merges.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` — the re-exec-into-`docker run` path (#7429/#7430) that
  currently resolves and forwards the real Claude credential; needs to substitute a per-launch
  placeholder and point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the proxy instead
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/` (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — reuse
  `Placeholder`/`Registry`/`Record`/`server` rather than a second implementation
- `loom-daemon/src/main.rs` (or wherever daemon subcommands are registered) — likely home for
  the new subcommand `spawn-claude.sh` shells out to, per this repo's language policy
- `defaults/docs/runtime-adapters.md` §Session containers — drop the "Claude's own container is
  not routed through the proxy yet" caveat once this lands (per AC5)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a placeholder-substitution test confirming the contained Claude launch's
      environment holds only the placeholder, never the real credential (mirroring whatever
      test #8674/PR #8701 adds for the native-harness path)
- [ ] Manual verification: with containment + credential substitution enabled, grep a running
      contained Claude sweep's `env` / `/proc/*/environ` and confirm the real credential is
      absent
- [ ] Manual verification: a contained Claude sweep completes a normal task end-to-end through
      the proxy
- [ ] Edge cases: uncontained Claude dispatch, and contained Claude dispatch with the flag off,
      are unchanged (AC4); placeholder invalidation at launch end (AC3) verified via the same
      registry semantics as the native path

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

- Parent: #8674 · Epic: #6896
- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/` (mechanism, already shipped)
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-claude.sh` (the path that still forwards a real credential)

issues.title: auto_update fetch delegates release-fetch to the 'freshest repo-local build', which a test fixture's fake loom-daemon in target/release poisoned — host could not roll for hours and the log hid the reason
issues.body:
## Summary

`loom-daemon-update.sh --fetch` delegates the download to `loom-daemon release-fetch`, and `resolve_self_daemon_bin` prefers the **freshest repo-local build** (`loom-daemon/target/release/loom-daemon`) over the installed machine-level binary. On loom-worker-1 that path held a **472-byte bash fake** written by the updater's own test fixtures (`.loom/scripts/tests/lib/daemon-update-fixtures.sh` / `test-loom-daemon-update.sh` — the `fake loom-daemon: unsupported subcommand` stub, `--version` → `loom-daemon 0.15.0 (commit 90e514e, built 2026-07-26)`), left there by a test run at 2026-09-22 13:45Z.

Result: every `auto_update` fetch on the host failed for hours (attempts 1–5, exponential backoff to 960 s) and the host could not roll 0.19.269 → 0.19.297. The daemon log keeps only the **last** line of the updater's output, which was the innocuous `loom_locate_daemon_bin: resolved /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/loom-daemon via $PATH (mtime …)` — the real failure (`fake loom-daemon: unsupported subcommand: release-fetch --repo-root … --tag v0.19.297`) only appeared when the script was run by hand:

```
Fetching loom-daemon release artifact v0.19.297 (target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) from rjwalters/loom...
fake loom-daemon: unsupported subcommand: release-fetch --repo-root /home/ubuntu/GitHub/loom --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --repo rjwalters/loom --tag v0.19.297
```

Moving the fake aside (`mv …/target/release/loom-daemon …/loom-daemon.fake-fixture-20260923`) and re-running `--fetch` installed 0.19.297 immediately (checksum verified, systemd drain-restart onto pid 822600).

## Three defects

1. **Test fixtures write into the real `target/release` path.** Whatever suite ran at 13:45Z (a sweep's `cargo test` / `.loom/scripts/tests` run on the primary checkout) left its fake at the canonical build-output path instead of a temp dir. `test-loom-daemon-update-fetch.sh` even warns about this class ("A failure below may be a STALE-BINARY artifact rather than a regression (#8176)") but only on the way in, not on the way out.
2. **`resolve_self_daemon_bin` trusts the repo-local file without a sanity probe.** A one-line `"$rf_bin" release-fetch --help` (or `--version` matching `^loom-daemon [0-9]`) before delegating would have fallen through to `~/.local/bin/loom-daemon`, which on this host *did* implement `release-fetch`. The machine-level install is what `auto_update` is updating; it is the natural default, and the repo-local build should be the override (`LOOM_DAEMON_SELF_BIN`), not the other way round.
3. **`auto_update` logs only the final line of the fetch script's output.** The diagnostic line was two lines up. Log the last N lines (or everything on stderr) on failure, or at least the first line matching `^(fake|error|FATAL|err:)`.

## Also seen on the same host, same hour

The previous daemon there (0.19.248, started 09-21 18:21Z) resolved `gh release view` from its cwd (`~/GitHub/anvil`) and polled anvil's `v0.11.0` for 30 h — evidence recorded on #8707. Newer builds name the repo explicitly, so that half is presumably already fixed; this issue is about the fixture and the resolver.

## Repro

```
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho "fake loom-daemon: unsupported subcommand: $*" >&2; exit 1\n' > loom-daemon/target/release/loom-daemon
chmod +x loom-daemon/target/release/loom-daemon
.loom/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh --fetch    # fails; ~/.local/bin/loom-daemon release-fetch works
```

issues.title: observability: hard_exclusion loom.dispatch.disposition spans never name which hard-exclusion label applied
issues.body:
## Problem

A `hard_exclusion` `loom.dispatch.disposition` span (#9222) never says *which* hard-exclusion rule applied. On SigNoz, every `hard_exclusion` row is indistinguishable from every other, so "show me everything rejected by the `external` label" requires leaving traces and re-reading the forge.

The losing information is visible in the seam:

- The work finder records the rule: `work_finder.rs` (~line 1912) does `skip(Qd::HardExclusion, Some(rule.to_string()), None)` where `rule` is `hard_exclusion::declining_label(&item.labels)` — e.g. `"external"` — and `ReadyQueueRow::detail` carries it.
- The exporter drops it: `allowed_park_label` (loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs ~line 264) validates `detail` against the closed `PARK_LABELS ∪ SKIP_LABELS` vocabulary only, and its own doc comment concedes the outcome: hard-exclusion labels "are not in that vocabulary today, so this is expected to be absent for that disposition in practice."

So the row has the answer; the span never gets it. Same shape as the `workspace_halted` halt-cause gap (#9222 explicitly scoped `detail` extraction down to park labels + open-PR numbers), just a different disposition.

## Proposed change

Make the hard-exclusion label exportable as a structured token, never free-form:

- Either extend the closed-vocabulary check in `allowed_park_label` to include `hard_exclusion::HARD_EXCLUSION_LABELS` (then `loom.queue.park_label` covers both dispositions), or parse the rule explicitly for `QueueDisposition::HardExclusion` and emit a dedicated attribute (e.g. `loom.queue.exclusion_label`) — implementer's choice, mirroring how `open_pr_number` is extracted by disposition.
- Keep allowlist-by-disposition semantics: a repo-configured skip label that is not in the vocabulary must still never reach the wire.
- Update the `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` §`loom.dispatch.disposition` attribute table (the `loom.queue.park_label` row, or the new attribute) and the `allowed_park_label` doc comment, which currently documents the absence as expected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: a `hard_exclusion` row with `detail = Some("external")` exports the label attribute with that exact token.
2. Unit test: a detail value outside `PARK_LABELS ∪ SKIP_LABELS ∪ HARD_EXCLUSION_LABELS` is still never exported (forward compatibility if repo-configured skip labels appear on other dispositions).
3. `cargo test -p loom-daemon disposition` green, clippy clean; telemetry-schema.md updated.

Refs: #9222 #9227 #7528

issues.title: feat(telemetry): emit repo lockout duration and frozen backlog weight on work_finder skip spans
issues.body:
### Problem Statement
In repositories with high backlog density (e.g. `klayout-tools` with 51 ready issues waiting, `gf180-parasynth` with 20 ready issues), an open PR waiting on merge/hold locks the entire repository under the `pr-open-skip` safety rule.

Currently, dispatch telemetry does not record how long a repository has been locked or the aggregate backlog weight (count of ready issues / sum of story points) frozen behind that lock.

### Proposed Solution
Enrich `loom.dispatch.disposition` and work finder skip spans with repository lockout metrics:
1. `lockout.duration_seconds`: Elapsed time since the active PR in this repo was opened or entered a hold.
2. `lockout.frozen_candidates_count`: Number of ready issues in this repo blocked from dispatch by `pr-open-skip`.
3. `lockout.frozen_points_sum`: Total story points (`points:N`) of all frozen candidate issues in this repo.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `loom.dispatch.disposition` spans record `lockout.duration_seconds`, `lockout.frozen_candidates_count`, and `lockout.frozen_points_sum` on every row whose disposition is the one actually causing the repo-wide freeze (see "Which disposition is 'the lock'?" below — resolve this before writing code, it changes which rows carry the attributes).
- [ ] The three attributes are populated only on rows for the *locked* repo, never as global/cross-repo aggregates, and never on a row whose own disposition is not the locking one (a `deferred_capacity` row in a *different*, unlocked repo must not carry them).
- [ ] `lockout.duration_seconds` is omitted (not zero) when its source timestamp cannot be established — see the duration-source options below; never emit a value the code cannot actually attest to.
- [ ] `lockout.frozen_points_sum` sums only issues that actually carry exactly one `points:*` label (`story_points::resolve_story_points`); an issue with zero or multiple `points:*` labels is excluded from the sum, not treated as `0`.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md`'s `loom.dispatch.disposition` attribute table (§"`loom.dispatch.disposition` (Issue #9222)") gains rows for the three new attributes, following the existing table's style.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: a repo with N frozen candidates summing to the correct points total; an issue with no/multiple points labels excluded from the sum; the attributes absent on rows outside the locked repo.
- [ ] Operators can query SigNoz to rank which repository lockouts are causing the highest backlog starvation (e.g. `klayout-tools` freezing 51 ready issues, per the filing's own observation, unverified count as of filing).

### Context
Discovered during autonomous queue forensics by @turian and @2ambot.

## Curator notes (2026-09-30, against `origin/main` @ `d6dd1941b`)

### Which disposition is "the lock"? (embedded design decision — resolve first)

The problem statement's own framing ("an open PR ... locks the **entire
repository**") does not match how the `pr-open-skip` guard is coded today.
Traced by hand, `d6dd1941b`:

- `OpenPrDispatchError` (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs:131`) is
  raised **per issue**: it fires only when *that specific issue* already has
  its own open linked PR (`OpenPrDispatchError.issue` / `.pr`). It does not
  block any *other* ready issue in the same repo from dispatching.
- `QueueDisposition::OpenPr` (`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs`, doc
  comment: `"Blocked: open linked PR"`) is the per-issue projection of that
  same guard onto the ready-queue row — one issue, one PR, no repo-wide
  effect.
- The mechanism that actually **does** freeze an entire repo's backlog behind
  one in-flight PR is `QueueDisposition::DeferredRepoCap`
  (`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs:45`, `"its own repo already held
  maxConcurrentPerRepo of the shared concurrency budget's slots"`) — when a
  repo's `autonomous.workFinder.maxConcurrentPerRepo` is `1` (a plausible
  config for `klayout-tools`/`gf180-parasynth`, not verified against those
  repos' actual `.loom/config.json` from here), one open PR/in-flight sweep
  consumes the repo's only slot and every *other* ready issue in that repo
  defers under `DeferredRepoCap`, not `OpenPr`.

So "51 ready issues waiting" behind one open PR is very likely a
`DeferredRepoCap` phenomenon, and the per-issue `OpenPr`/`pr-open-skip` guard
is a red herring for the "frozen backlog" half of this feature (it still
matters for `lockout.duration_seconds`, since the *locking* row itself is
plausibly the one `OpenPr` row in that repo). **The Builder must confirm
which disposition(s) are actually producing the observed backlog in the
repos that motivated this issue** (or treat both `OpenPr` and
`DeferredRepoCap` rows in a repo as contributing to "frozen", whichever the
design settles on) before wiring the aggregate counters — this is the
"embedded decision" the points estimate below assumes gets made during this
issue, not before it.

### No PR-open/hold-entry timestamp exists today

Grepped `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs` and
`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/guards.rs`: `OpenPrDispatchError` carries
only `{ issue: u32, pr: u32 }` — no timestamp. `ReadyQueueRow`
(`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs:216`) carries the *issue's* own
`created_at`, never the PR's. The closest existing signal is
`OpenPrMemoEntry.verified_at` (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/guards.rs:78`,
the 15-minute verified-open-PR memo, #6788) — but that is *when the daemon
last verified* the PR was open, refreshed periodically, not when the PR was
actually opened or the hold began. Options for `lockout.duration_seconds`,
in increasing cost/accuracy:
1. Approximate from `OpenPrMemoEntry.verified_at`'s *first* observation for
   the current PR number (cheap, in-memory, resets on daemon restart — same
   caveat every in-memory tracker in this package already carries).
2. Read the PR's actual `createdAt` from the forge on the same listing pass
   that already resolves `repo_ref`/`QueueRepoRef` (an extra field on an
   existing call, if the listing already fetches PR metadata — not verified
   from here whether it does).
3. A dedicated forge read per locked repo — likely too expensive at the
   `queue_snapshot`/`disposition` sampling cadence (documented as "never
   blocks the tick loop, never a fresh forge probe" for its siblings); avoid
   unless 1 and 2 are ruled out.

### Story points are not currently threaded through the ready-queue pipeline

`WorkItem` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs`, the fetched-candidate struct)
carries `labels: Vec<String>`, so `story_points::resolve_story_points(issue,
labels)` (`loom-daemon/src/story_points.rs:133`) is callable at classification
time — but `ReadyQueueRow` (`loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs:216`) only
carries a single `tier: Option<String>` label projection, not points and not
the full label set. Populating `lockout.frozen_points_sum` requires either:
- adding a `story_points: Option<u32>` field to `ReadyQueueRow`, populated in
  `work_finder.rs` from `item.labels` via `story_points::resolve_story_points`
  (mirrors how `tier` is already projected), or
- computing the repo-level aggregate directly inside the tick (where full
  labels are still in scope) and carrying only the aggregate forward on
  `WorkFinderTickSummary`, rather than per-row.

Either is a legitimate design choice; the second avoids widening
`ReadyQueueRow`'s wire contract for a value only used in aggregate, but the
first is more consistent with how every other per-row attribute in this
telemetry package is built (`build_rows` in
`loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs:292` already reduces a
`ReadyQueueRow` to a `DispositionRow`, so a points field could flow the same
path).

### Where the aggregate counts get computed

`DispositionRow`/`build_rows` (`loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs:104-318`)
already iterate `summary.queue` once per repo-resolved row; a repo-level
`(frozen_candidates_count, frozen_points_sum)` fold keyed by `slug` (grouping
whichever disposition(s) the design above settles on) is the natural place to
compute both counts, attaching them to every row emitted for that `slug` in
the same `record()` pass (`disposition.rs:457`) — not just the locking row,
since the point is "how much backlog is frozen behind *this* lock", visible
on every frozen row's own span too, per the AC above (values scoped to that
repo only).

## Affected Files
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition.rs` — `DispositionRow`,
  `Emission`, `build_rows`, `build_span`: add the three lockout fields and
  their span attributes.
- `loom-daemon/src/types/ready_queue.rs` — likely a new `story_points` (or
  similar) field on `ReadyQueueRow`, if the per-row-points design is chosen.
- `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` — project `story_points::resolve_story_points`
  onto the ready-queue row at classification time, mirroring the existing
  `tier` projection, if the per-row-points design is chosen.
- `loom-daemon/src/types/work_finder_tick.rs` — only if the aggregate-on-summary
  design (points threaded via `WorkFinderTickSummary` instead of per-row) is
  chosen instead.
- `loom-daemon/src/story_points.rs` — reused as-is (`resolve_story_points`);
  no change expected, cited here for the Builder's reference.
- `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` — `loom.dispatch.disposition` attribute
  table (search `#### \`loom.dispatch.disposition\` (Issue #9222)`).
- New/existing test modules: `loom-daemon/src/observability/ops/disposition_tests.rs`
  (already `#[path]`-included by `disposition.rs`) is the natural home for the
  new unit tests in the Acceptance Criteria above.

## Test Plan
1. `cargo test -p loom-daemon disposition` (or the crate's equivalent scoped
   test invocation) covering the new unit tests named in Acceptance Criteria.
2. A `build_rows`/`build_span` test asserting the three lockout attributes
   are present on a synthetic locked-repo row and absent on an unrelated
   repo's row in the same sample.
3. A `story_points` integration check: an issue with `points:5` contributes
   `5` to the sum; an issue with no `points:*` label or two stacked
   `points:*` labels contributes `0` (excluded, not defaulted).
4. Manual/SigNoz spot-check (documented in the PR, not required to pass CI):
   confirm the new attributes appear on a live `loom.dispatch.disposition`
   span for a repo currently holding an open PR, once deployed.

issues.title: feat: ETA as a Loom primitive — versioned start/finish/land estimates, logged to SigNoz and scored against outcomes
issues.body:
## Problem

Operators want to know, for any active issue, **when it will start, when the running sweep will finish, and when it will land** (PR merged / issue closed as completed). They also want to know how often those guesses are wrong, so the guess can be improved over time.

Today a downstream dashboard would have to guess from outside, re-deriving order, capacity and phase durations that only Loom actually knows. Operator decision: **ETAs are a Loom primitive.** Loom computes them, versions the heuristic, and logs every estimate and its outcome to SigNoz. Dashboards only display them.

This builds on #9288 (`dispatch_plan()`), since an honest start/land ETA needs the real order, capacity and sharding.

## Ask

**1. A versioned ETA primitive in loom-daemon**
- `estimate(issue) -> { kind, p25, p50, p75, parts[], inputs, heuristic }` for `kind ∈ {start, finish, land}`.
- Inputs:
  - the dispatch plan (rank, `max_concurrent`, sharding, repo caps);
  - Loom's phase-duration history, including human stages such as awaiting curation or approval;
  - the historical changes-requested rate, which drives how likely a Doctor pass is.
- Returns **no estimate** when there isn't an honest one (blocked, held, no baseline). Never a made-up number.

**2. Versioning**
- A heuristic registry with ids like `land-v1`.
- A shipped heuristic is immutable. Any change gets a new id.
- **Shadow mode:**
  - every registered heuristic is computed and logged;
  - one is marked `current`;
  - switching is a config change, made once the SigNoz accuracy data favours the new one.

**3. Telemetry: log every estimate, then score it, in Loom**
- `eta.estimate`: per active issue × kind × heuristic, on each work-finder tick or at a fixed cadence.
- `eta.outcome`: when the outcome happens (sweep start, sweep end, merge/close). Fields:
  - `error = actual − p50`;
  - `covered` (actual within [p25, p75]);
  - `horizon`, `heuristic`, `kind`, `repo`, `stage_at_estimate`, `samples`.
- Both go out through the daemon's existing OTLP exporter to SigNoz, so no new write path is needed. They are also sent through the same ingest path as `queue.snapshot`, so dashboards can show the *current* estimate without recomputing it.

**4. CLI**
- `loom eta <repo>#<n>` and `loom eta --repo <slug>`: the "landing next" list, soonest first.

**5. Docs**
- The model, the versioning rules, and how to add v2 and compare it in shadow mode using SigNoz accuracy queries: median absolute error, p25–p75 coverage and bias, per heuristic, kind, repo and horizon.

## Downstream

2AMLogic/loom-ui will render these verbatim:
- a "Landing next" table sorted by land p50;
- "starts in" / "lands in" ranges;
- an accuracy panel with live SigNoz queries over `eta.outcome`.

It will retire its interim dashboard-side estimates once this ships.

Related: #9288 (dispatch plan), #9238 (ranking inputs), #8525 (phase tracing), #9037 (per-issue story trace).

issues.title: [#9244 A] daemon core: loom:operator-priority ordering, starred listing, overflow slot, red-main-fix lane, telemetry
issues.body:
Parent: #9244 (split approved by the operator into three PRs: A, B, C). This is **A: daemon core (Rust)**.

## Goal

Make the work finder treat `loom:operator-priority` ("starred") as the top dispatch key, fleet-wide, with an overflow slot, a red-main-fix lane, and the telemetry loom-ui needs. `loom:urgent` stops affecting order.

## Scope

### 1. Label
- Add `loom:operator-priority` to **both** `.github/labels.yml` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` (they're byte-identical today, 280 lines each). Put it next to the `loom:operator*` block (~line 161-236). Description must be at most 100 chars and include an `Applied by:` owner, e.g. `"Operator wants this landed ASAP, ahead of all other work. Applied by: humans (directly or via loom-ui star)."`. Colour `CA8A04` (matches loom-ui's copy).
- Add a YAML comment saying it is **not** `loom:operator` (the hold) and is **not a hold**: nothing may prefix-match `loom:operator` / `loom:operator-` as a hold.
- **Prefix-match audit (loom-ui asked for this):** `loom-daemon/src/pr_latency/mod.rs:117` (`hold_labels`) uses `l.starts_with("loom:operator-")`, so a starred PR would list `loom:operator-priority` as a hold label. Exclude it and add a test. No other daemon `starts_with("loom:operator` was found on `origin/main`. Re-run the grep before merging.

### 2. Ordering keys (`WorkItem` / `PriorityCandidate` / `candidate_cmp`)
- `WorkItem` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs`, `is_urgent` at :461) gains `is_operator_priority()` and a way to carry `operator_priority_at: Option<String>`. It also gains `is_main_red_fix()`, which is true when `body` contains `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` (same style as the complexity and recheck-interval markers).
- `PriorityCandidate` (:593) gains `operator_priority: bool`, `operator_priority_at: Option<String>` and `main_red_fix: bool`. The last one is already resolved against the repo's red state, so `candidate_cmp` stays pure.
- `candidate_cmp` (:624) becomes:
  1. starred first
  2. (starred only) `operator_priority_at` ascending, with a missing value falling back to `created_at` (use the `cmp_created_at` Some<None semantics, :637)
  3. `main_red_fix` first (set only while that repo's main is verified red)
  4. `workspace_priority` ascending
  5. `created_at` oldest first
  6. `number` ascending
- **Remove `urgent` from the order.** Keep parsing it harmlessly: `URGENT_LABEL` / `is_urgent()` may stay, an item carrying `loom:urgent` is never an error, and the wire `urgent` fields stay (see 7). Removing the Rust constant and wire field completely is a follow-up after one release.
- `ready_queue::key_of` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/ready_queue.rs:44-53`) builds the key. Populate the new fields there, so the view and dispatch can't drift.
- Update the sort comment at `work_finder.rs:1966` and the `candidate_cmp` rustdoc.

### 3. Starred-at source
- Primary source: the `labeled` event for `loom:operator-priority` in the issue's timeline (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/timeline` or `/events`). Fetch it **only for starred candidates** and cache it per (repo, issue). Invalidate the cache when the label is removed. A tick must not make one call per candidate per tick. `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/outcome_journal/label_timeline.rs` already reads label timelines and may be reusable.
- Fallback: `createdAt`.
- (C will add the loom-ui intent `requested_at` via a comment marker as a higher-precedence source. Leave a seam for it; don't implement it here.)

### 4. Second listing: starred issues outside `loom:issue`
- `GhWorkSource::list_ready_issues` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/forge.rs:82`) currently makes one `forge_listing::list_issues_cached(.., "loom:issue", "open")` call (`forge_listing.rs:82`). Add a second ETag-cached call with `label = "loom:operator-priority"`, drop PR rows, and **dedupe by issue number** against the `loom:issue` rows. A starred `loom:issue` appears in both.
- A starred issue whose workflow label is `loom:triage` or `loom:curated`, or that has **no workflow label at all** (#9244 liveness item 6, the loom-ui#281 shape), becomes a candidate. Dispatching it is already supported: `preflip_labels::classify_observed_labels` (`sweep_registry/preflip_labels.rs:108`) returns `NotYetApproved` for a non-`loom:issue` snapshot, and the child sweep runs the full lifecycle from Curator.
- A starred item carrying anything in `SKIP_LABELS` (`work_finder/labels.rs:69`: `loom:building`, `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator`) **or `loom:operator-decision`** must never be dispatched. **Note:** `loom:operator-decision` is *not* in `SKIP_LABELS` today; it's covered only because it always accompanies `loom:operator-only`. For starred candidates, check it explicitly (or add it to the skip set) and add a test.
- Keep the listing failure isolation (`report.listing_failed`) and the rate-limit breaker path. If the second listing fails, the `loom:issue` rows must still be used.

### 5. Overflow slot (one over-limit sweep per host, starred only)
- Multi-workspace path: `tick_multi_with_repo_cap` (`work_finder.rs:1639`), pass 2 at :1983-2033 (global cap check :1998, per-repo cap `cap.defer` :2014). Single-workspace path: `tick_with_saturation_brake` (:1109), cap check at :1339. **Both are live in production** (called at :2591 and :3203).
- A starred candidate refused **only** by the global `max_concurrent` cap and/or the per-repo cap (`maxConcurrentPerRepo`, `work_finder/repo_cap.rs`) may be admitted as the overflow sweep, provided that:
  - no live sweep on this host is already marked `overflow` (a new `WorkDispatcher` query, backed by the registry), and
  - `occupancy <= max_concurrent`. `resolve_dynamic_max_concurrent` can lower the cap below occupancy mid-flight; a host already over its limit for that reason must not add another sweep. This is how "at most one over-limit sweep" is enforced in practice.
- These gates still apply, unchanged: the saturation brake (checked first, :1987 / :1334), the host-class gate (`work_finder/host_class.rs`), token-pool preflight / exhaustion (`work_finder/pool_preflight.rs`), park and skip labels, quarantine, backoff, peer claim and the per-tick ramp cap (#4234). The ramp cap isn't a queue limit, so the overflow sweep doesn't bypass it; see the note in #9244.
- Normal (unstarred) work never uses the overflow slot. Red-main fixes don't get it either.
- Record `overflow: true` on the sweep record (`SweepInfo`, `loom-daemon/src/types.rs:904`, serde-default `false`). Thread it through dispatch: today `WorkDispatcher::dispatch(issue, complexity)` is at `work_finder.rs:910` and `forge.rs:376`. Surface it in `list_sweeps` / `get_sweep_status` (MCP) and `loom-daemon status`. Add a `TickReport` counter or `QueueDisposition` so the ready queue shows "dispatched (overflow)".

### 6. Red-main fixes and the main-health halt
- The key-3 boost applies only when the owning repo's main-health state is **verified red**: `WorkspaceHealthStates::is_halted(root)` (`main_health_gate.rs:698`). **Don't** use the `halted[]` slice for this. `dispatch_held_per_root` (:1442) also sets it while a gate run is in flight (`suppress_dispatch_during_gate`), which isn't a red main.
- With the gate disabled for a repo, fall back to the latest default-branch CI conclusion: one cached forge read per repo per tick, only when that repo has at least one marker-bearing candidate.
- Halt admits only fixes. Single-workspace: `if halted { … return }` at :1128. Multi: the per-repo `halted` branch at :1807 records every item as `WorkspaceHalted` and `continue`s. Change both so a halted repo still admits its `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` candidates, and **only** those. That includes starred issues without the marker: they keep `WorkspaceHalted`. `report.halted` semantics stay unchanged. If the gate is in flight (not verified red), admit nothing, as today.
- A marker on a green repo gets no boost.

### 7. Telemetry and CLI
- `queue.snapshot` rows: `QueueSnapshotRow` (`loom-daemon/src/telemetry/queue_snapshot.rs:55`) gains `operator_priority: bool` (serde default false) and `operator_priority_at: Option<String>` (skip if none). `urgent` (:65) is **kept and emitted always-false** for one release. Populate them in `build_record` (`observability/queue_snapshot.rs:97`, row push at :115-128) from `TickQueueRow` (`types/ready_queue.rs:~214`), which gains the same fields.
- `host.health.managed_repos[]`: `ManagedRepoEntry` (`telemetry/mod.rs:1236`) gains `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] priority: Option<u32>` from `Workspace.priority`. Construct it in `collect_managed_repos_with` (`observability/collector.rs:1060`, push at :1092). This folds in loom-ui#153.
- `ready-queue` CLI: `cli/ready_queue_cmd.rs`. Update the ordering string at :100 and the help/header text at :125. The row flags at :155 gain `starred` (and `red-main-fix`), and the `urgent` flag goes. `main.rs:196` doc comment. `dashboard.html:367` flag. `types/ready_queue.rs:7` module doc.
- In-repo Phase-2 dashboard: `dashboard/web/src/views/workQueue.ts:137` (urgent badge becomes a starred badge) and `dashboard/web/src/workQueue.ts:144` (ordering comment).

### 8. Tests and docs
- New unit tests: starred in a priority-100 repo beats unstarred in a priority-0 repo; two starred issues order by starred-at, not age; missing starred-at falls back to `createdAt`; existing ordering is unchanged when nothing is starred; `loom:urgent` no longer changes order; a starred `loom:triage` / `loom:curated` / unlabeled issue is dispatched; a starred issue carrying `loom:blocked` / `loom:operator-only` / `loom:operator-decision` / `loom:operator` is not; overflow admits exactly one starred sweep over both caps, refuses a second, refuses unstarred work, and still yields to the saturation brake, host-class and pool gates; a marker on a green repo gets no boost; a halted repo admits its fix and nothing else; a starred issue in a halted repo waits; with the gate disabled, CI status is the fallback; wire-shape snapshot tests (`observability/queue_snapshot_tests.rs`, `telemetry/tests.rs`, `observability/collector/tests.rs`) are updated.
- Incidental `loom:urgent` fixtures in Rust tests (`host_affinity.rs:274`, `merge_pr/labels/tests.rs:14,43`, `observability/queue_blocked_tests.rs:37`, `work_finder/tests.rs`, `work_finder/ready_queue_tests.rs`) switch to a neutral label where the test doesn't care about urgency.
- Docs: `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (ordering at :1928, plus overflow and red-main-fix lane), `defaults/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (:1117, row table :1149, :1169; add `operator_priority`, `operator_priority_at`, `managed_repos[].priority`; mark `urgent` always-false/deprecated). Keep `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh` green.

## File-size ratchet (read before coding)

`scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` freezes `loom-daemon/src/work_finder.rs` (1580 code lines), `work_finder/tests.rs` (3455), `main.rs` (1228) and `safehouse.rs`. They may not grow. Put new logic in **new sibling modules**, e.g. `work_finder/operator_priority.rs` (key, starred-at cache, overflow decision) and `work_finder/main_red_fix.rs`, leaving only small call sites in `work_finder.rs`, and put new tests in new sibling test files. Check `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh` locally (no cargo needed). **Never run cargo on the Mac** (use the remote build box).

## Out of scope
- **B (roles and `loom:urgent` retirement):** every role prompt, `defaults/` prompt/doc mirrors, Guide's top-3 duty, `urgent-flip-guard.sh`, marking `loom:urgent` retired in `labels.yml`, and `.loom/docs/label-state-machine.md` / CLAUDE.md. A adds the new label; B edits the `loom:urgent` entry.
- **C (liveness contract and loom-ui intents):** landing state, `needs-operator` escalation, watchdog, blocker inheritance, `/ingest` ack `operator_priority_intents`, intent-comment starred-at source, replay check.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `loom:operator-priority` is in both `labels.yml` files (description ≤100 chars, `Applied by:` owner). `pr_latency::hold_labels` doesn't report it.
- [ ] `candidate_cmp` implements keys 1-6 above. `urgent` isn't a key. All ordering tests listed in §8 pass.
- [ ] The second ETag-cached listing makes starred `loom:triage` / `loom:curated` / unlabeled issues candidates, deduped against `loom:issue` rows. Skip/park/`loom:operator-decision` are never dispatched. Tested.
- [ ] Starred-at comes from the cached `labeled` timeline event (starred candidates only), falling back to `createdAt`. Tested with a fake source.
- [ ] Overflow: at most one over-limit sweep per host, starred only, in both tick paths. Safety gates are still honoured. `overflow: true` is visible in `list_sweeps` / `get_sweep_status` / `loom-daemon status`. Tested.
- [ ] Red-main fix: key 3 applies only on verified red (not gate-in-flight). A halted repo admits only marker issues in both tick paths. Gate-disabled falls back to CI. Tested.
- [ ] `queue.snapshot` rows carry `operator_priority` / `operator_priority_at`. `urgent` is always false. `managed_repos[].priority` ships. Wire-shape tests are updated.
- [ ] `loom-daemon ready-queue` ordering string, help text, `main.rs:196`, `dashboard.html` and `dashboard/web` reflect the new keys.
- [ ] `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` and `telemetry-schema.md` are updated. `check-file-size-budget.sh` and `check-docs-defaults-parity.sh` pass.

issues.title: drain: an operator drain that times out must stay paused, not silently resume dispatch
issues.body:
## Problem

When a drain times out without `--force-after-timeout`, the daemon **resumes dispatch** and stays up. The log line reads: `drain timed out with N sweep(s) still in flight — refused restart (no --force-after-timeout); dispatch resumed, daemon stays up`.

That is the right default for an auto-update roll, where resuming work beats sitting idle. It is the wrong outcome when an operator is draining the fleet to **stop** it. On 2026-09-30 the operator paused a whole fleet to clear a PR backlog. On one launchd host and one systemd worker the drain timed out, dispatch silently resumed, and both hosts went back to re-dispatching issues and starting new sweeps. Nobody noticed until a peer check found a live daemon on a host that was believed stopped.

## Proposal

Make the post-timeout behaviour depend on why the drain was started, and make it visible:

- **Operator-initiated drain** (`restart --drain --then-exit`, `fleet drain`, any drain whose intent is "stop"): on timeout, stay **paused**. Keep dispatch off and keep in-flight work running. Emit a loud `daemon.drain.timeout` event and a status field, and wait for an explicit `--force` or `--abort-drain`. Never resume dispatch without being asked.
- **Auto-update roll drain:** keep today's behaviour, but label it clearly in status and the log as "roll deferred; dispatch resumed".
- In both cases, `loom-daemon status` should show whether dispatch is paused, and why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A timed-out operator drain leaves dispatch paused, and status and the event bus say so.
- [ ] Dispatch resumes only through an explicit operator action (`--abort-drain` / `restart --abort-drain`) or a completed drain.
- [ ] Auto-update roll drains keep their current resume-on-timeout behaviour, now clearly labelled.
- [ ] Tests cover both paths.

## Curator: technical detail and acceptance criteria (2026-09-30)

Scope folds in the watchdog-resurrection failure from the comment below and the escalation no-op seen in the same fleet stop (2AMLogic/2am#1687).

### Code map (current `main`)
- `loom-daemon/src/ipc.rs`: `DrainState::begin` pins `force_after_timeout` on the already-draining path unless `roll_pending` (#6007). A second `restart --drain --force-after-timeout` against a first-attempt drain is therefore a silent no-op ("existing deadline is unchanged").
- `run_drain_supervisor`, `DrainTick::TimedOutRefuse`: a **then-exit** drain calls `resolve_timeout`, which clears the pause flag ("dispatch resumed"). A **relaunch** drain retains a pending roll, but `refuse_roll_deadline` abandons it and resumes dispatch once `drain_pending_budget` is spent. Both paths apply the same way to an operator `restart --drain` and to the auto-update roll (`auto_update/drain_trigger.rs`), because the drain has no record of who started it.
- `autonomy-desired` marker: only `loom-daemon-stop.sh` removes it. A then-exit drain leaves it in place, so the watchdog (`watchdog/mod.rs::tick` -> `marker_present` -> outage/recovery) revives the daemon. Startup healing (`autonomy_marker::heal_on_startup`) would also re-create an absent marker on any supervised relaunch.
- `ipc.rs`, `fleet/drain.rs`, `daemon_service.rs`, `main.rs` and `types.rs` are frozen by the file-size ratchet. New logic goes in sibling modules.

### Acceptance criteria
1. **The drain records its origin.** `handle_drain_request` takes an origin: `Operator` for every IPC `DrainAndRestartDaemon` (CLI `restart --drain`, `loom-daemon-update.sh --drain`, `fleet drain`), and `AutoUpdate` for `auto_update/drain_trigger.rs`. An operator request against an in-progress auto-update drain promotes it one-way to `Operator`. The reverse never happens.
2. **An operator drain that times out stays paused.** If an `Operator` drain passes its deadline without force, whether it is then-exit or relaunch:
   - dispatch stays paused and the drain stays active;
   - the deadline is cleared and a `timed_out` state is recorded;
   - the note and a `daemon.drain.timeout` event (`paused: true`) list the stragglers by sweep id and issue;
   - the supervisor keeps polling, so the terminal action (stay down, or relaunch) still fires when in-flight reaches 0.

   Dispatch never resumes on its own. Only `--abort-drain` or a completed drain ends the pause.
3. **The auto-update roll keeps its current timeout behaviour, on purpose.** It keeps the #6007 pending-roll re-arm and budget, then abandons the roll and resumes dispatch. A version roll must not starve a host of work forever. The abandon note and the log line say "roll deferred/abandoned; dispatch resumed (auto-update roll)" so the reader can tell it apart from an operator drain.
4. **A later request escalates an in-progress drain.** It no longer no-ops:
   - `--force-after-timeout` escalates any active drain, not only a pending roll. If the drain is already timed out or pending, the deadline moves to now. Otherwise it becomes `min(existing, now + requested timeout)`, so it can move earlier but never later.
   - `--then-exit` keeps its #4521 one-way escalation, including on a timed-out paused drain.
   - The ack says ESCALATED.
5. **A durable operator-stop record.** When a then-exit drain is accepted or escalated, `<marker>.stopped` is written (with `stopped_at`, `reason`, `pid`) and the `autonomy-desired` marker is moved aside into it. The following honour it:
   - the watchdog tick: `.stopped` present -> report OK "operator stop recorded", no recovery, exit 0, even if a stale `autonomy-desired` also exists;
   - startup healing: no re-heal while `.stopped` is present;
   - daemon startup: a supervised relaunch such as launchd `RunAtLoad` or `kickstart` comes up with dispatch **held**, a note says why, and `--abort-drain` releases it.
6. **Clearing the stop record.** `restart --abort-drain` removes `.stopped` and restores the moved-aside `autonomy-desired`. An explicit start (`loom-daemon-start.sh` / `loom-daemon daemon-start`) clears `.stopped` before it launches.
7. **Status.** `loom-daemon status` (human and `--json` `drain` object) shows whether dispatch is paused and why: `origin`, `timed_out`. `fleet drain` maps a remote `timed_out: true` payload to its documented exit-2 "timed out" contract instead of waiting out its own deadline.
8. **Tests.** Unit tests cover:
   - an operator timeout holding (then-exit and relaunch);
   - an auto-update timeout keeping pending, then abandoning;
   - force escalation of a first-attempt drain and of a timed-out drain;
   - origin promotion;
   - stop-marker write, restore and clear;
   - watchdog tick exit 0 without recovery while `.stopped` is present (exercised in the watchdog shell suite under Native Port Suites);
   - heal skip;
   - `fleet drain` classifying `timed_out`.

issues.title: quarantine: escalate relapsed quarantines — probation + doubling TTL (rebuild of #8440, scope-limited)
issues.body:
Rebuild of the fix from PR #8440, which was closed (operator decision 2026-09-30) because its branch carried ~700 lines of out-of-scope quarantine-refactor code (turian's contamination hold). **Rebuild ONLY the two changes below, from current `main`**: no refactor of the quarantine module beyond what they need.

## Problem (vibesql#6639)

The insta-crash quarantine (#3939) flapped forever on a persistent breakage: **3 crashes → 1h TTL → release with a fresh 3-strike runway → 3 more crashes → repeat**. Observed 8+ cycles across vibesql #6170/#6172/#6174, each cycle costing three wasted `--claim-owned` dispatches. (The original trigger — cargo hangs on a wedged external volume — is long since recovered; this PR fixes the structural loop that let it cycle.)

## Fix — two changes, both scoped to the relapse path

**1. Probation.** A quarantine's *generation marker* survives its TTL release; only a healthy outcome (checkpoint/clean exit) or an operator `quarantine clear` removes it. While the marker exists, the **first** further insta-crash re-quarantines immediately (effective threshold 1). A relapse after a release is presumptive evidence the breakage persisted through the pause — the old behavior made it cost three more dispatches per cycle.

**2. Escalation.** Generation N serves `ttl × 2^(N−1)`, capped at the new `ttlMaxSecs` (default 24h, clamped up to `ttl`). The flap decays to at-most-daily retries instead of cycling every hour forever.

Transient breakages keep the exact old behavior: quarantine → TTL → one healthy run → ladder fully reset. Generation state is in-memory like the quarantine itself — a daemon restart resets the ladder (documented in code).

## Surfaces

- `loom-daemon quarantine list`: entries carry `generation`; `ttl_remaining_secs` reports against the **escalated** TTL
- The quarantine forge comment explains the escalation on generation ≥ 2 (the comment trail is what #6639's observers actually read)
- Config table row added to `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (`env > config > default`, per the module's convention)

## Tests (all green)

New: relapse-requarantines-on-first-crash (drives the real death-classification path, not just the tally API) · escalation math incl. cap and misconfigured-ceiling clamp · `quarantine_entries` escalated-TTL surface · healthy-outcome reset · operator-clear reset.

Modules: **sweep_registry 613/613** · health 213/213 · ipc 122/122 · reaper 76/76 · quarantine 52/52 · work_finder::tests 220/220. (The known environmental `registry_refresh` hot-apply failure is unchanged and pre-existing on base.)

Fixes vibesql#6639 (cross-repo — close the vibesql issue manually after this merges and deploys).

## Scope guard (from the operator decision)

- The diff must be limited to the relapse path: the generation marker/probation, TTL escalation with `ttlMaxSecs`, the `quarantine list` surface fields, the forge-comment wording, and the config doc row. Any unrelated restructuring of the quarantine or sweep-registry code is out of scope. Judge should check the diff size against this list.
- Cross-repo: after merge and deploy, close vibesql#6639 manually.
