issues.title: ci-telemetry captain gate: the poller silently stops on any host with no fleet.captain, and a handoff leaves a stale arm (#9002 blocking findings, merged unaddressed)
issues.body:
## Problem

PR #9002 (for #8901) merged at 2026-09-26T04:18Z with two blocking findings from an independent Judge review still unaddressed: https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/pull/9002#issuecomment-5843121796. A `loom:operator` hold was added at 04:22Z, but the PR had already merged, so the hold had no effect.

### 1. The CI-telemetry poller silently stops on any host with no `fleet.captain` (blocking)

The captain gate (`fleet_captain::arm_singleton_job("ci-telemetry-poll", …)`) refuses on **any** host that has no `fleet.captain` declared, single-host setups included. The PR's migration note says only multi-host fleets are affected, which is wrong. No committed config declares a captain, and the Rollout section of `ci-observability.md` ("pick one fleet host") never mentions one. So following the documented rollout, or upgrading an existing opted-in host, captures zero CI data.

The refusal is visible in only one place, a per-tick WARN in the daemon log:
- `ci-telemetry status` reads `stale` / `never-polled` and gives no reason.
- Nothing appears in `host.health` / `loom-daemon health`.
- The dashboard "no captain reporting" flag only fires once *some* host has a captain.
- SigNoz simply stops receiving CI runs, jobs and logs.

Meanwhile duplicate polling, the thing the gate prevents, is harmless apart from API budget, because records are deduplicated.

### 2. A captain handoff leaves a false "armed on a non-captain host" alarm for up to 6h

When the command-path arm is refused, its saved shell-arm record is never cleared. After `fleet.captain` moves from host A to host B, A keeps reporting the job as armed until the 6h expiry, and the dashboard flag fires the whole time. #8901 warned about exactly this. The in-daemon path already clears within one tick.

## Fix

- [ ] Record the refusal so `ci-telemetry status` shows it as its own state (e.g. `refused: no fleet.captain declared`), and surface it in `host.health` / `loom-daemon health`. **Or** let `ci-telemetry-poll` run when no captain is declared, documented as an explicit exception.
- [ ] Correct the migration note, the module doc, and the `ci-observability.md` Rollout steps so they say a captain is required (or describe the exception).
- [ ] Clear the saved arm record when the arm is refused, with a regression test for the handoff case.
- [ ] Non-blocking: take a lock around the saved arm-record file update (concurrent arms on one host can lose an entry until the next tick).

## Current exposure

Low today. On the operator Mac `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled=false`, so nothing is lost yet. This must land before any host enables the daemon CI poller, or CI data will silently fail to reach SigNoz.

Related: #8901, #9002, #8848, harness-ops #193 (the separate CI poller).

hardcoded two-path gh-config guard with a single declared credential-bearing
class (`loom-daemon/src/init/post_init.rs` `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS`, parity-
checked against both shell copies by `loom-daemon/src/init/credential_class_tests.rs`).

That PR's "Suspected scope (unverified)" section named several other

benefiting from the same class-level guard, but explicitly deferred rather
than assumed safe or unsafe:

- `scripts/install-loom.sh:653` (and a similar block around :788, :1422) —
  `git add -A` when creating the initial commit for a brand-new install.
- `scripts/uninstall-loom.sh:1985` — `git add -A` in a worktree built for
  the uninstall-removal PR.
- `install.sh:1360` — same "initial commit" pattern as install-loom.sh.
- `docs/guides/ci-cd-setup.md:112` and `:326` — workflow template snippets
  that run `git add .loom CLAUDE.md .claude .gitignore`.

## What this issue is for

Audit each site above, individually, against the same question #7818/#8005
answered for `land-resync-commit.sh`: can this specific `git add` run in a
repo state where a credential-bearing path (`.loom/tokens/`,
`.loom/accounts.env`, `.loom/api-keys/`, `.loom/claude-config/`,
`.loom/gh-config/`, `.loom/gh-config-by-owner/`) already exists on disk,
untracked, with a stale-or-missing `.gitignore`?

For each site, either:

1. Confirm it is structurally safe (e.g. "initial commit" runs before `.loom`
   is ever populated with live credentials, or the worktree the add runs in
   is provably fresh) and record why in a comment near the call site, or
2. Apply the same class-level exclusion — reuse `loom-daemon
   is-credential-path` / `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` (exposed via

audit finds them realistically reachable with a stale `.gitignore`.

## Out of scope

Re-litigating #8005's core design (the `CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS` const + parity
tests) — that's done. This is a per-site audit only.

Filed as a scoped follow-up per #8005's own "Suspected scope (unverified)"
section, split out to keep #8005 focused on the two call sites it was
actually filed against.

issues.title: verify-proposal-refs.sh reports BAD LINE RANGE for every .loom/docs/*.md citation (reads the symlink, not the document)
issues.body:
## What happens

`verify-proposal-refs.sh`'s line-range check reads the cited path **through git** (`git show "origin/main:$path" | wc -l`). Since #7842 every `.loom/docs/*.md` with a `defaults/docs/` counterpart is a **symlink** (tree mode `120000`), so that read returns the link-target string, `wc -l` measures the link, and every cited range under `.loom/docs/` is reported as a miss:

```
$ printf 'Cites .loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200\n' > /tmp/probe.md
$ ./.loom/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh /tmp/probe.md
verify-proposal-refs.sh: 1 miss(es) in /tmp/probe.md
  - BAD LINE RANGE: `.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200` — origin/main:.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md has only 0 lines
exit=1
```

The real document has 3031 lines. Because the script **blocks filing** (`hermit.md` / `architect.md`: "Any miss blocks filing"), this pushes proposers away from citing the installed doc paths, or into "fixing" a citation that was correct.

This is the same root cause as #8593 (Champion's premise-false gate reading `.loom/docs/*.md` symlinks through git and closing sound proposals on a check that cannot match). #8593 fixed the Champion side — the prompt rules, `champion-premise-false-evidence.md`'s `resolve_main_path()` recipe, and fixture coverage — and deliberately left this half out: see below.

## Why it was not fixed in #8593's PR

A working shell fix was prototyped in PR #8655 and dropped. It adds ~40 **code** lines to `defaults/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh`, which is category `contract` in `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`, and `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` refuses any growth of the portable pool **with no `Shell-Budget-Growth:` override** (`check_against_rev`: "Portable growth is NOT overridable, deliberately"). Per `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` the correct home for new logic behind a `contract` name is `loom-daemon`.

## Suggested shape

1. A `loom-daemon` verb that resolves a path against a rev — follow a `120000` tree entry to its real blob path (bounded hops; target is relative to the **link's own directory**; normalization must be **lexical**, since the path lives in a commit, not the working tree) and optionally report the resolved blob's line count.
2. `verify-proposal-refs.sh` calls it in the line-range branch, reports the **resolved** path in any `BAD LINE RANGE` message, and reports a dangling link as *unreadable* (e.g. `BROKEN SYMLINK`) rather than "has only 0 lines" — an unreadable file is an inconclusive check, not a disproof (the same distinction #8593 established for Champion).
3. Champion's `resolve_main_path()` snippet (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-premise-false-evidence.md`) can then point at the same verb instead of shipping a shell recipe in a prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A body citing an in-range line span under `.loom/docs/` exits 0 (no miss).
- [ ] A genuinely out-of-range span under `.loom/docs/` still misses, and the message names the **resolved** path and the real line count.
- [ ] A dangling symlink is reported as unreadable, not as a 0-line file.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-verify-proposal-refs.sh` gains a symlink fixture covering all three (a draft of these fixtures exists in PR #8655's history).
- [ ] `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` stays at +0 portable growth.

issues.title: observability: capture all GitHub Actions runs/jobs of the 2amlogic org as OTLP telemetry via a loom-daemon ci-telemetry poller (SigNoz build/CI visibility, phase 1 of 3)
issues.body:
## What

Capture **every GitHub Actions run and job** of the `2amlogic` org as first-class OTLP telemetry from a new `loom-daemon ci-telemetry` poller. This is the foundation for standing build/CI observability in SigNoz: durations, outcomes, and per-run structure become queryable so we can retro on build/CI time regressions (motivation: build and CI times are currently felt but invisible — regressions only surface as "everything is slower").

Part of the SigNoz observability track (epic #8522): the transport (daemon OTLP exporter → neutral gateway → SigNoz) already exists; this issue adds the **CI source** that currently does not exist at all. Follow-on phases: full job-log capture with collector-side redaction (filed next), and SigNoz retro surfaces (filed next) — cross-linked at filing.

## Design (grounded in existing modules)

**New Rust module** `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` + CLI subcommand `ci-telemetry` (per the shell-language policy: new executable logic is a daemon subcommand, not a `.sh`).

### CLI
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --once` — one poll cycle across the configured org; non-zero exit with a named reason on failure (a poll that cannot run must not look like a poll that passed — ci-principles rule 6)
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry status` — ledger size, per-repo watermarks, last successful poll, records emitted/exported
- Daemon-integrated periodic poller when `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled=true` (default **false**, FLAGS-OFF; `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_*` env overrides, env > config > default via `config_resolver.rs`)

### Config block (`.loom/config.json` → `autonomous.ciTelemetry`)
| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` |
| `org` | `2amlogic` |
| `intervalSecs` | 120 |
| `excludedRepos` | `[]` |
| `logCaptureEnabled` | `false` (phase 2 flips it; must be a config gate, see scope) |

### Polling + dedup ("never do the same job twice")
- Discover repos via `GET /orgs/{org}/repos` (paginated, ETag/304-cached — the `forge_cached_list.rs` mechanism, never raw re-listing)
- Per repo: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs` with a `created_after` watermark from the ledger; for each unseen run → `GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs`
- **Durable ledger** at `.loom/state/ci-telemetry/seen.jsonl`: append-only `(repo, run_id, job_id)` entries + per-repo watermark (latest observed `run.created_at`), fsynced before a record is emitted. A job is emitted **exactly once** regardless of restarts, re-polls, or re-runs. A crash between write and emit must never double-emit: the ledger write is the commit.
- Multi-host posture: polling may run on more than one fleet host, but records carry **stable identities** (`run_id`/`job_id` as the dedup key in attributes + local ledger) so a recipient can dedup; document the single-poller-as-normal-case assumption, per-repo lease coordination is explicitly out of scope unless fleet primitives make it trivial (one mechanism per behaviour — do not invent a second coordination layer)
- Rate limits: honour the existing rate-limit breaker; budget = repos × 2 request families per interval; a 403/secondary-limit backs off the whole org, not per-repo hammering

### Emission (through the existing `observability` OTLP exporter — no new transport)
- Record kinds: `ci.run` (repo, workflow, ref, head_sha, event, status, conclusion, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at) and `ci.job` (+ job name, runner label, attempts, timed_out) — mapped in `observability/otlp/mapping.rs` alongside the existing lifecycle kinds
- Metrics: `loom.ci.run.duration_ms` and `loom.ci.job.duration_ms` histograms; labels **only** `repo`, `workflow`, `job`, `runner`, `conclusion` (low-cardinality allowlist rule; never sha/ref/issue-number in metric labels)
- Traces: one trace per run, one span per job (parent/child like the sweep traces in `telemetry/trace/`), so Trace Explorer shows the CI waterfall
- **Local journal** `.loom/logs/ci-telemetry.jsonl` is written regardless of whether any exporter is configured (the `sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl` pattern) — the poller is useful offline

### Gateway allowlist
Extend `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` `keep_keys` with exactly the `loom.ci.*` attributes this phase emits; the fan-out contract test (`collector_fanout`) must assert each one. Nothing else admitted.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` documents the subcommand; building without the `otlp` feature still compiles (OTLP-gated paths behind the existing feature, like `exporter.rs`)
2. With a recorded-fixture GitHub API (wiremock-style or recorded responses, committed under the test dir — no live-network tests in CI), `--once` over a synthetic org with 2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs emits 2 `ci.run` + 3×4 `ci.job` records to the local journal with correct durations
3. **Idempotency (the money AC)**: a second `--once` over the same fixture emits **zero** records; killing the process mid-cycle and re-running emits each job exactly once total (ledger is the commit)
4. Unit tests cover: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op on repo discovery, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line is detected and repaired, not double-counted)
5. `status` distinguishes: never-polled / last-ok + age / failing + last error — silence never reads as healthy (house discipline)
6. `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` created (phase-1 section: config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) with `.loom/docs/` parity copy (Docs/Defaults Parity Check must pass); `observability.md` map-of-docs table gains the row
7. Emitted metric label set and attribute allowlist match the collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte (contract test)

## Explicit non-goals (this issue)

- **No job log download** — that is the follow-on phase; `logCaptureEnabled` exists as a gate that this phase must refuse to honour (config-gated off, named stub, no dead code that pretends to work)
- No re-hosting of GitHub's log UI, no per-step spans (job granularity is the unit)
- No per-repo lease/coordination protocol
- No changes to `sweep.*`/`tokens.*` record kinds

## Cross-links

- Epic: #8522 (SigNoz/ClickStack trial)
- Pipeline/transport docs: `.loom/docs/observability.md`, `.loom/docs/otlp-transport.md`
- Dedup/journal precedent: `.loom/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (local journal), #8669 (allowlist discipline)
- Policy home (follow-on issue): `ci-observability.md`

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` (new module) - poller, dedup ledger, CLI subcommand
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs` - add `ci.run`/`ci.job` record mapping
- `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` - extend `keep_keys` with the new `loom.ci.*` attributes
- `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` - add the phase-1 section (config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) to the existing policy doc
- `defaults/docs/observability.md` - add the map-of-docs row
- `.loom/config.json` schema - new `autonomous.ciTelemetry` block

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: fixture-based `--once` run (2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs) asserts correct `ci.run`/`ci.job` record counts and durations
- [ ] Idempotency test: second `--once` over the same fixture emits zero records; kill-mid-cycle + re-run emits each job exactly once
- [ ] Unit tests: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line)
- [ ] Contract test: emitted metric label/attribute set matches collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte
- [ ] Manual verification: `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` / `status` output reviewed for the never-polled / last-ok+age / failing+last-error states

issues.title: observability: standing policy — all 2amlogic build/CI logs and runs are captured in SigNoz (ci-observability policy doc + wiring; phase 4 of 4)
issues.body:
## What

Codify the **standing policy**: *all build and CI activity of the captured org is captured in SigNoz — runs, jobs, durations, outcomes, and full job logs — and stays captured as new repos/workflows appear.* Operator decision, stated outright: "It should be a standing policy that we capture all logs and CI there."

This issue is docs + config plumbing only (no new executable logic beyond a config default and the parity/budget constraints CI already enforces), and it can land independently of #8824/#8825/#8826 — it names what they build.

## Design

### `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` (canonical home, mirrored to `.loom/docs/`)
Sections:
1. **The policy** (one paragraph, non-negotiable wording): every `2amlogic` repo's GitHub Actions runs, jobs, durations, outcomes, and completed-job logs are captured in SigNoz via the ci-telemetry poller; org-scoped capture means new repos are in scope on day one (auto-discovery, no per-repo enrollment step); duration/outcome metrics are **never** excludable, log capture may be excluded per-repo only with a stated reason recorded in the config entry itself
2. **The pipeline, in one picture** (poller → OTLP exporter → neutral gateway redaction → SigNoz; diagram style matching `observability.md`) with map-plus-links to every detail doc (`telemetry-schema.md`, `otlp-transport.md`, collector README, signoz README) — a map, not a duplicate, per the operating-summary discipline
3. **Phases** (1: runs/jobs/metrics — #8824; 2: logs + collector redaction — #8825; 3: retro surfaces + retention — #8826) with status, each linking its issue
4. **Capture scope & exclusions**: the `excludedRepos`/`logCapture` config surface and the rule that an exclusion is a config entry *with a reason field*, reviewed like any other config change; no silent excludes, no undocumented ones
5. **Retention**: metrics ≥30d, logs/traces 7d, and why (trends outlive raw data) — owned by #8826, referenced here as policy
6. **Redaction policy**: the collector is the redaction boundary (operator decision), the scrub-class table (from #8825's design), and what this store is and is not (trusted private operational store, not the public dashboard projection — same framing as the collector README)

- Config surface: after #8824 lands, `autonomous.ciTelemetry.org` defaults to `2amlogic` (the captured org) — this issue documents that default; if #8824 landed with a different default, reconcile in this PR, not by silent drift

## Acceptance criteria

1. `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` exists, mirrors to `.loom/docs/`, passes the parity check, TOC check, and dangling-link check; every doc it links to exists
2. CLAUDE.md pointer present, budget check green (CI proves it — the check is a required status check, so the PR can't merge red)
3. `ci-principles.md` and `observability.md` cross-links present in both locations they ship
4. The policy wording in §1 names the org, the signal set (runs/jobs/durations/outcomes/logs), the never-excludable metrics, and the reasoned-exclusion rule — the four things a new operator must be able to read in one paragraph
5. No executable-logic changes beyond a config default value (if #8824 is already merged) — if it hasn't, this PR is pure docs and says so in the PR description

## Explicit non-goals

- No alerting, no new queries (that's #8826)
- No changes to the redaction implementation (#8825) or the poller (#8824)
- No fleet-wide enablement action in this PR (rollout is a per-host config operation documented in the doc; the operator/role-runner performs it when #8824/#8825 are merged and the trial is confirmed receiving)

issues.title: feat: one dispatch_plan() that owns the order Loom will work in, published fleet-wide (so dashboards never re-derive candidate_cmp)
issues.body:
## Problem

Each daemon's work-finder tick ranks its own ready issues with `candidate_cmp` and publishes `rank` in `queue.snapshot` (`loom-daemon/src/work_finder/ready_queue.rs`). That rank is real, but it has three gaps:

- **Per host only.** No fleet-wide order exists across hosts that manage overlapping repos.
- **Ready issues only.** Issues that are curated or still in triage have no rank.
- **Reflects only the last tick.** Sharding (`dispatcher-repo-sharding.md`), repo caps (`repo_cap.rs`) and capacity are applied to dispatch, but the snapshot doesn't say what the next ticks will take.

Dashboards that want to show "what will Loom work on next, in order" currently re-implement `candidate_cmp` in their own code, and that copy drifts silently whenever Loom's rules change. The ordering should live in exactly one place: Loom.

## Ask

1. **`dispatch_plan()`** (name up to Loom): the ordered list of issues Loom will dispatch. It uses the *same code* as the real dispatcher (`candidate_cmp` + sharding + repo caps + capacity), not a copy. Each row has:
   - `position`, `repo`, `issue`;
   - `state` (running / next / queued / blocked);
   - the expected host/workspace, when known;
   - a `reason` naming the keys that placed it (priority, urgent, age, cap, shard).
2. **Fleet scope.** A merged order across hosts. It can come from a coordinator, or from a documented, deterministic merge rule that Loom ships as a library function, so consumers don't invent one.
3. **Publish it** on each tick, either as a fleet position on `queue.snapshot` or as a new `dispatch.plan` record kind, so dashboards display it as-is.
4. **CLI.** `loom queue` (or similar) prints the same plan.
5. **Optional.** Define an order for pre-ready tiers (curated, triage) if Loom has one. Otherwise, state explicitly that they're unordered.

The shape is additive and optional. The downstream dashboard (2AMLogic/loom-ui) will render `position` verbatim and fall back to the per-host `rank` until this lands.

Related: #9238 (per-candidate ranking inputs in telemetry), #9244 (`loom:operator-priority`), #9017.

issues.body:
Parent: #9244 (split approved by the operator into three PRs: A, B, C). This is **B: roles and `loom:urgent` retirement (prompts, docs, shell; no Rust)**.

## Goal

Every stage treats a starred (`loom:operator-priority`) issue or PR as "act now", and `loom:urgent` is retired from every prompt, doc and script so exactly one "land this ASAP" signal remains.

## Scope

### 1. Role rules for starred work (from #9244 "Semantics" and "Liveness contract" items 5 and 6, prompt side)
The canonical role files are `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/*.md`. `defaults/roles/*.md` are **symlinks** to them.
- **Curator** (`curator.md`): at the start of every pass, query starred issues first (`gh issue list --label loom:operator-priority --state open`). Curate them immediately. After curating a starred issue, promote it straight to `loom:issue`, skipping Champion's promotion evaluation (the star is the Tier-3 approval). A starred issue with **no workflow label** is treated as `loom:triage` and curated at once. Red-main-fix issues (`<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` in the body) come next, but get no promotion bypass.
- **Champion** (`champion.md`, `champion-pr-merge.md`, `champion-issue-promo.md`, `champion-common.md`): drain starred `loom:pr` PRs before the oldest-first pass (`champion.md:293` and `:295` say "oldest first"). A `mergeable` starred PR is merged on the next pass. A merge failure on a starred PR is retried at most once, then escalated. A starred PR on a merge-risk or critical-file hold (#9016) goes to the **top** of the pinned hold digest (#6877; digest logic in `champion-common.md` / `champion-held-pr-staleness.md`). Remove `loom:urgent` from issue promotion.
- **Judge** (`judge.md`) and **Doctor** (`doctor.md`): drain starred PRs before the normal oldest-first pass. Judge's bar is unchanged.
- **Builder** (`builder.md`, `builder-pr.md`): if the issue carries `loom:operator-priority`, add the same label to the PR it opens. Remove `loom:urgent` from Builder's priority order.
- **Doctor red-main filing**: when Doctor files an issue for a pre-existing failure it confirmed on `origin/main`, put `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` in the body instead of applying `loom:urgent`. Doctor's other `loom:urgent` uses ("feedback too complex" follow-ups) become plain `loom:triage`.
- **Guards unchanged, and say so in the prompts:** `loom:blocked`, `loom:operator-only`, `loom:operator-decision`, merge-risk and critical-file holds, the host-class gate and Judge's bar all still apply to starred work. The label is human-only: no role ever applies or removes it (Builder copying it onto its own PR is the one exception).
- Cover both the role-runner and the cron paths (`.github/workflows/loom-*.yml` prompts, if they restate queue order), and the interval prompts in `defaults/roles/{curator,champion,judge,doctor,builder}.json`.

### 2. Retire `loom:urgent` from `defaults/` and repo docs
`git grep -l "loom:urgent" origin/main -- defaults` lists 38 files. All of them are in scope:
- Commands: `architect.md`, `architect-patterns.md`, `architect-reference.md`, `builder.md`, `champion-issue-promo.md`, `curator.md`, `doctor.md`, `guide.md`, `help.md`, `hermit-patterns.md`, `imagine.md`, `loom.md` (all under `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/`).
- Mirrors: `defaults/.claude/agents/loom-{architect,doctor,guide}.md` and `defaults/.agents/skills/loom-{architect,builder,curator,doctor,guide,hermit-patterns,loom}/SKILL.md`. SKILL.md files are **generated**: regenerate them with `defaults/scripts/generate-agent-skills.sh` (it execs `loom-daemon generate-agent-skills`; use an installed binary and don't run cargo on the Mac). Don't hand-edit them.
- `defaults/.loom/CLAUDE.md`, then regenerate `defaults/.loom/AGENTS.md` via `defaults/scripts/generate-agents-md.sh` (`scripts/check-agents-md-sync.sh`). `defaults/.claude/README.md`.
- Role JSON: `defaults/roles/{architect,builder,doctor,guide}.json`.
- **Guide**: remove the whole top-3 duty, from the "Maximum Urgent: 3 Issues" section through "When to Apply loom:urgent". `guide.json`'s `description` ("…by managing loom:urgent labels") and `defaultIntervalPrompt` ("…update loom:urgent labels…top 3 priorities") get rewritten around Guide's remaining duties. Guide's WORK_PLAN generator emits a `section "Urgent" "Issues flagged as highest priority (\`loom:urgent\`)."` (`guide.md:~2480`). Replace it with an "Operator priority" section that **reads** `loom:operator-priority` (Guide never applies it), and regenerate `WORK_PLAN.md`'s section accordingly.
- Tests under `defaults/scripts/tests/`: `test-guide-urgency-rank.sh` (tests the retired duty; delete it or rewrite it for the read-only section), `test-guide-operator-only-exclude.sh`, `test-guide-work-plan-debounce.sh`, `test-merge-pr-verdict-label-guard.sh` (update the fixtures).
- Docs: `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md:4891` and `:10085` are incident history (reword or keep as history). The ordering text at `:1928` and `telemetry-schema.md` belong to **A**, so don't edit them here.
- Repo-level: `README.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `docs/agents.md`, `docs/workflows.md`, `docs/design/issue-332-label-state-machine.md`, `docs/philosophy/agent-archetypes.md`, `WORK_PLAN.md`. Leave `CHANGELOG.md` and `WORK_LOG.md` alone (they're history).
- Document the new label in `defaults/docs/label-state-machine.md` (installed as `.loom/docs/label-state-machine.md`) and the repo `CLAUDE.md` label state-machine line (keep `scripts/check-claude-md-budget.sh` green).

### 3. Delete `urgent-flip-guard.sh`
- Delete `defaults/scripts/urgent-flip-guard.sh` and `defaults/scripts/tests/test-urgent-flip-guard.sh`.
- Remove their `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt` entries (:459 and :487), the `defaults/scripts/tests/ci-wired.txt:203` line and the `scripts/pipefail-early-exit-baseline.txt:104` line.
- **Add both paths (and `test-guide-urgency-rank.sh`, if deleted) to `defaults/.loom-retired.list`**, or `scripts/check-retired-list-drift.sh` fails and installed repos keep orphaned copies (#8675).
- Fix the dangling comment references in `defaults/scripts/check-evaluating-staleness.sh:146` and `defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-fence.sh:277`.

### 4. Label
- Change `loom:urgent` in **both** `.github/labels.yml:147` and `defaults/.github/labels.yml` to `description: "Retired (#9244): use loom:operator-priority"`. Don't delete it yet: `sync-labels.sh` doesn't delete fleet labels, and the open issues still carry it. The operator migrates those issues by hand.

## Constraints
- **Role-prompt size ratchet:** `scripts/role-prompt-budget.txt` freezes whole-prompt budgets (builder 31065, champion 14381, curator 47166, doctor 33789, judge 56195, guide 50832 tokens), enforced by `scripts/check-role-prompt-budget.sh`. Guide's deleted top-3 duty frees room. Each other role's net change must stay within budget, so pay for the new rules by trimming `loom:urgent` text or moving detail to a sibling doc. See `.loom/docs/file-size-policy.md`.
- **Authoring discipline** (`.loom/docs/role-prompt-authoring.md`): pressure-test the Champion rule against a starred PR with a merge-risk hold (it must stay held, go to the top of the digest, and not be merged), and audit for conflicts with the existing oldest-first and hold rules.
- Parity checks: `scripts/check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `scripts/check-hooks-defaults-parity.sh`, `check-agents-md-sync.sh`, `check-retired-list-drift.sh`, the shell allowlist and budget checks. Resync installed copies with `./.loom/scripts/resync-installed.sh`.
- **No Rust.** Don't touch daemon-side urgent parsing (`loom-daemon/src/**`, `URGENT_LABEL`, the `urgent` wire field). A handles all of it, and `dashboard/web/`.

## Out of scope
- **A (daemon core):** the label *definition* for `loom:operator-priority`, `candidate_cmp`, the listings, overflow, red-main halt admission, telemetry, the ready-queue CLI, `daemon-reference.md` ordering text and `telemetry-schema.md`.
- **C (liveness contract and loom-ui intents):** daemon-side landing state, escalation, watchdog, blocker inheritance and intent application.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The Curator, Champion, Judge, Doctor and Builder prompts (plus their `.json` interval prompts) carry the starred-first rules above. Builder copies the label to its PR. Doctor uses the `<!-- loom:main-red-fix -->` marker.
- [ ] The pressure-test of a starred PR under a merge-risk hold is recorded in the PR description.
- [ ] `git grep -n "loom:urgent" -- ':!loom-daemon' ':!dashboard/web' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!WORK_LOG.md'` finds only the retired `labels.yml` entries (and incident history, if kept verbatim). The daemon-side leftovers belong to A and its follow-up.
- [ ] Guide's prompt and `guide.json` no longer manage priority labels. WORK_PLAN's section reads `loom:operator-priority`.
- [ ] `urgent-flip-guard.sh` and its test are deleted. Allowlist, ci-wired, pipefail baseline and `.loom-retired.list` are updated.
- [ ] `loom:urgent` is marked retired in both `labels.yml` files. `label-state-machine.md` and `CLAUDE.md` mention `loom:operator-priority` (and that it isn't a hold).
- [ ] `check-role-prompt-budget.sh`, `check-claude-md-budget.sh`, `check-docs-defaults-parity.sh`, `check-agents-md-sync.sh`, `check-retired-list-drift.sh` and the shell allowlist check all pass. Installed copies are resynced.
